title: Williamsburg Bar Crawl: 5 Weekday Happy Hour Stops
h1: Williamsburg bar crawl: from Bedford Avenue to Grand Street
description: A Williamsburg bar crawl with five weekday happy hours in walking order, from Hole In The Wall on Bedford Avenue to Crystal Lake on Grand Street.
answer: For a Williamsburg bar crawl, go Monday through Friday and walk east: Hole In The Wall and Layla on Bedford Avenue, Meraki Greek Bistro on Grand Street, Northern Bell on Metropolitan Avenue, then Crystal Lake Brooklyn on Grand Street. All five weekday happy hours overlap in the late afternoon, and the route starts near the Bedford Avenue L stop and ends near Graham Avenue on the same line.
intro:
Williamsburg spreads out more than the East Village, so a crawl here needs a plan. This one starts on Bedford Avenue, where the bars sit close together, then heads east toward Metropolitan Avenue and Grand Street. Five stops, about 1.8 kilometers in straight lines, and only one leg that takes longer than five minutes.

All five happy hours run Monday through Friday, and they are on together in the late afternoon. The first three end at the same time and the last two run an hour longer, which is why the route moves west to east: you hit the early closers first and finish where the deals last. Along the way you get a cocktail and food stop, an oyster bar, a Greek bistro, a bar with a real happy hour menu and a cheap beer finish.

The cards below carry live prices and today's hours. The table under this intro shows more happy hours within a short walk of the first stop, useful if one bar is packed and you need a swap.

picks.why: Start at Hole In The Wall, a restaurant at 292 Bedford Avenue, six minutes from the Bedford Avenue L stop. Its weekday window opens earliest of the five. The list is the broadest on the route: espresso martini, a Bee's Knees with gin, Aperol, wine, drafts, bites, wings and three kinds of fries. Eat something here, since this is the longest food list you will see all night.

About three minutes south on Bedford Avenue, Layla at number 352 is a bar with European food and the oyster stop of the crawl. Its weekday happy hour covers oysters, draft beer, aperitivi beers and Contessa Boatyard gin. The window opens an hour after Hole In The Wall's and ends at the same time, so arrive close to the start. Layla lists a Resy link, and Marcy Avenue on the J, M and Z is seven minutes away.

Meraki Greek Bistro Brooklyn, at 252 Grand Street, is about four minutes northeast of Layla. Its happy hour runs on weekdays and ends with the first two stops, so keep this one to a single round. The listing tags it for outdoor seating and a food deal but does not itemize the happy hour, so ask what it covers when you sit down. Reservations go through SevenRooms.

The longest leg, about eleven minutes east, brings you to Northern Bell at 612 Metropolitan Avenue. Its weekday happy hour runs into the early evening and is one of the fullest on the route: a discount on draft and on everything, set-price well drinks and glasses of wine, a happy hour food menu and smoked wings. Lorimer Street on the G and L is two minutes away, and Resy takes bookings.

Finish about four minutes away at Crystal Lake Brooklyn, 647 Grand Street, a bar tagged for cheap beer. The weekday happy hour covers drafts, well drinks and select wines by the glass, from late afternoon into early evening. It ends at the same time as Northern Bell's, so leave room for one last round here. Graham Avenue on the L is five minutes away for the ride home.

sections.body:
Go Monday through Friday. None of these five runs a happy hour on Saturday or Sunday, and all five are on at once in the late afternoon. That overlap is what makes the route work.

Start at Hole In The Wall in the first hour of its window, which opens an hour before Layla's. Move to Layla as its deal begins, then on to Meraki. Those first three end at the same moment, so the front half of the crawl is the part to keep moving: one round, about half an hour, per stop. Once you reach Northern Bell the pressure eases a little, since Northern Bell and Crystal Lake Brooklyn both run an hour past the first three. Check the cards on the day, because bars change hours.

For a weekend crawl in the same neighborhood, this route will not work. OTB runs its happy hour on Saturday and Sunday only, with oysters, margaritas, Aperol, house wine and a plain hot dog on the list, and our weekend page lists the rest.

Leg one, Hole In The Wall to Layla: about 270 meters, three minutes, south on Bedford Avenue. Leg two, Layla to Meraki Greek Bistro: about 340 meters, four minutes, northeast to Grand Street. Leg three, Meraki to Northern Bell: about 880 meters, eleven minutes, east to Metropolitan Avenue. This is the one real walk of the night, and a good moment to drink some water. Leg four, Northern Bell to Crystal Lake Brooklyn: about 330 meters, four minutes, southeast to Grand Street.

The total is roughly 1,820 meters and 23 minutes of walking. Those are straight lines between the doors, so the actual walk on the street grid runs a little longer. If your group is slow, trim the stay at Meraki rather than skipping the eleven-minute leg; Northern Bell and Crystal Lake Brooklyn are where the later deals are.

The L to Bedford Avenue is the simplest way in. Hole In The Wall and Meraki are both six minutes from that station. From the East Village, the same L line stops at 1st Avenue, three minutes from Westville East on our East Village bar crawl. If you come in on the J, M or Z, get off at Marcy Avenue, seven minutes from Layla, and walk up Bedford Avenue to Hole In The Wall to begin.

The route ends on the L too. Crystal Lake Brooklyn is five minutes from Graham Avenue, and Northern Bell is two minutes from Lorimer Street, where the G also stops. Bedford Avenue, Lorimer Street and Graham Avenue are consecutive L stops, so you finish only two stops from where you began.

sections.h: Small things that make the crawl better
sections.body:
Eat early and again later. Hole In The Wall has wings, bites and fries, and Layla has oysters, both in the first hour. Northern Bell's happy hour food and smoked wings carry you through the second half.

Three stops list booking links: Layla and Northern Bell on Resy, and Meraki on SevenRooms. Hole In The Wall and Crystal Lake Brooklyn have none listed, so they are walk-in. A group of two to four will move through all five far more easily than a big party.

faq.a: Any weekday. All five stops run a happy hour Monday through Friday, and they overlap in the late afternoon. None of them has a weekend happy hour, so for Saturday or Sunday look at OTB and the weekend list instead.
faq.q: What day should I do a Williamsburg bar crawl?

faq.a: About 1,820 meters in straight lines between the five stops, or roughly 23 minutes of walking. The leg from Meraki to Northern Bell is the longest at about eleven minutes; the others are three or four.
faq.q: How long is the walk?

faq.a: Hole In The Wall has wings, bites and fries on its happy hour, Layla has oysters, and Northern Bell has a happy hour food menu and smoked wings. Crystal Lake Brooklyn lists drinks only.
faq.q: Where can I eat on this crawl?

faq.a: Start from Bedford Avenue on the L, or Marcy Avenue on the J, M and Z. Finish at Graham Avenue on the L, five minutes from Crystal Lake Brooklyn, or Lorimer Street on the G and L, two minutes from Northern Bell.
faq.q: Which subway stops do I need?

faq.a: No, but they are possible at three stops. Layla and Northern Bell take bookings through Resy, and Meraki through SevenRooms. Hole In The Wall and Crystal Lake Brooklyn have no booking link listed.
faq.q: Do I need reservations?

table_title: More happy hours within a short walk
method: Stops, deals, days, addresses, booking links and subway walking times come from each bar's own website as recorded in our database, with happy hours last checked on September 2, 2026. Walking times are straight-line distances between each bar's map coordinates at about 80 meters a minute, so real walks run slightly longer. The order of L stations comes from the MTA's L line map.

title: West Village Bar Crawl: 5 Happy Hours, Tuesday to Friday
h1: A West Village bar crawl built on overlapping happy hours
description: A five-stop West Village bar crawl that chains happy hours Tuesday to Friday, from Hudson Street to Christopher Street, with walk times and subway tips.
answer: For a west village bar crawl that stays on happy hour the whole way, go on a Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday and walk five stops: Cafe Luna on Hudson Street, The Mary Lane on Bank Street, Hudson Hound, Left Bank on Perry Street and Rockbar on Christopher Street. No leg is longer than about five minutes on foot, and the happy hour windows hand off from one bar to the next in that order.
intro:
Most bar crawls fall apart at the third stop, when the deals end and the prices jump. This one is built the other way around. We started from the happy hour schedules each bar publishes, kept only the stops whose windows land on the same days, and then put them in an order where the earliest window comes first and the latest comes last.

The result is a short loop through the blocks around Hudson Street, Bank Street, Perry Street and Christopher Street. Five bars, under a kilometer of walking in total, and a mix that goes from beer, wine and cocktails at a Hudson Street cafe to a spritz on a patio, a bucket of beer, a dinner-style food deal and a two-for-one to finish.

The live prices sit on each pick card below, with each bar's current hours. Use this guide for the order, the days and the walking, and check the cards on the day you go.

picks.why: Start at Cafe Luna, an all-day cafe and bar at 628 Hudson Street. Its happy hour is listed every day of the week, and its window opens and closes earliest of the five, so this is your afternoon stop. The deal is simple: beer, wine and cocktails at happy hour prices. On several days the cafe closes when happy hour ends, so do not plan to linger. The 8th Avenue station on the A, C, E and L is four minutes away.

Walk about three minutes south to The Mary Lane on Bank Street, an American bar with a seasonal patio. Happy hour runs Tuesday through Friday at the bar and on the patio, from late afternoon into early evening. Expect a Cappelletti spritz, tequila and ginger beer drinks, and glasses of French and Portuguese wine. Make this your cocktail stop, and grab a patio seat if the weather allows.

Hudson Hound, at 575 Hudson Street, is about a minute from The Mary Lane, and its Tuesday to Friday window runs at the same time. Treat it as the beer stop: all draught beer is on the happy hour menu, along with buckets of Estrella Galicia, Bud Light or Coney Island Merman IPA, plus spritzes, margaritas, sangria, wine by the glass or bottle and discounted bar food.

Two minutes south on Perry Street, Left Bank turns the crawl into dinner. Its weekday happy hour starts later than the first three stops, in the early evening, and the menu pairs food with drinks: any two apps, a burger with a draught beer, or pasta with a glass of wine. It also runs a weekend window, one of two stops on this route that do, along with Cafe Luna.

Finish about five minutes west at Rockbar, 185 Christopher Street. Its weekday happy hour shares Left Bank's early evening timing and is a two-for-one on beer, well and call liquor, the simplest deal of the night. The bar sits toward the western end of Christopher Street, a seven-minute walk from the Christopher Street-Stonewall station on the 1 train.

sections.body:
Tuesday through Friday is the only stretch of the week when all five happy hours run. On Mondays, The Mary Lane and Hudson Hound have no happy hour, which breaks the middle of the route. On Saturdays and Sundays only Cafe Luna and Left Bank keep a window, so the crawl does not work on a weekend.

The order follows the clock. Cafe Luna has the earliest window of the five and it closes first, so begin there in the afternoon. The Mary Lane and Hudson Hound share a late afternoon window, which is why they sit side by side in the middle. Left Bank and Rockbar start last and run into the early evening, so they close out the night. If you arrive late, skip Cafe Luna and start at The Mary Lane. If you only have an hour, do the middle three.

Plan on one round per stop and roughly half an hour at each. The Mary Lane's deal is at the bar and patio only, so head for the bar rather than waiting for a table. The exact start and end times for each window are on the pick cards above, and they are the thing to check before you set out.

Stop one to stop two is about 210 meters south from Cafe Luna to The Mary Lane on Bank Street, or roughly three minutes. From there Hudson Hound is about 60 meters away on Hudson Street, a one-minute walk. Left Bank on Perry Street is about 130 meters further, close to two minutes. The last leg is the longest, about 360 meters to Rockbar on Christopher Street, around five minutes.

Add it up and the whole crawl is about 760 meters of walking, or about 10 minutes of total time on your feet. Our distances are measured point to point between each bar's coordinates at about 80 meters a minute, so allow an extra minute here and there for corners and crossings.

The mix is deliberate. You get beer, wine and cocktails at Cafe Luna, a spritz and wine on The Mary Lane's patio, draught beer and buckets at Hudson Hound, a food and drink pairing at Left Bank, and a two-for-one at Rockbar. If you want to eat properly, Left Bank is the stop to do it.

Start from the 8th Avenue station, which serves the A, C, E and L trains and which our listing puts four minutes from Cafe Luna.

The route ends near the 1 train. Christopher Street-Stonewall is about five minutes from Hudson Hound and Left Bank and about seven minutes from Rockbar, so you can head home from there without doubling back.

For fares, tap the same contactless card or phone at the turnstile for every ride. The MTA caps weekly subway and local bus fares when you use one card or device, and the seven-day window starts with your first tap.

sections.h: If your day does not fit
sections.body:
On a Monday or a weekend, build a shorter version from bars with daily windows. Cafe Luna, the first stop, lists its happy hour every day. Jack & Charlie's No. 118 on Greenwich Avenue runs happy hour every day at the bar and on the patio, with oysters and a sunset menu. Osteria Nonnino on Hudson Street also runs daily, at the bar and in the outdoor area, with wine by the glass or carafe, beer, cocktails and Italian bites such as arancini and meatballs. Left Bank covers the weekend with its own Saturday and Sunday window.

For more options on the day, the table below lists every happy hour within a short walk of the first stop, closest first.

faq.a: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday. Those are the only days when all five stops on this route run happy hour. Monday drops The Mary Lane and Hudson Hound, and on weekends only Cafe Luna and Left Bank have a window.
faq.q: Which day should I do a West Village bar crawl?

faq.a: The walking adds up to about 10 minutes over roughly 760 meters. With one round and about half an hour at each of the five bars, plan on roughly three hours, starting in the afternoon and finishing in the early evening.
faq.q: How long does the crawl take?

faq.a: Not as written. On Saturday and Sunday, combine the weekend windows at Cafe Luna and Left Bank with Jack & Charlie's No. 118 and Osteria Nonnino, which both list happy hour every day.
faq.q: Can I do this crawl on a weekend?

faq.a: No. The Mary Lane's deal is at the bar and patio, so walk in and take a bar seat. Left Bank has a booking link on its card if you want a table afterward.
faq.q: Do I need reservations?

faq.a: Begin at the 8th Avenue station (A, C, E, L), four minutes from Cafe Luna. Finish at Christopher Street-Stonewall on the 1, about seven minutes from Rockbar.
faq.q: Which subway stations are closest to the start and end?

faq.a: Yes, in small numbers. Hudson Hound sells beer by the bucket at happy hour, Left Bank's food pairings work for sharing, and Rockbar's two-for-one suits rounds. Bar-only deals get tight with more than four or five people.
faq.q: Is this crawl good for a group?

table_title: More happy hours within a short walk
method: We picked the stops from our database of New York happy hours, which records each bar's schedule and offers from the bar's own website. The five bars on this route were last checked on September 2, 2026. Walking times are straight-line distances between bar coordinates at about 80 meters per minute, so real walks can run slightly longer. Subway lines and station walks come from each bar's listing, and fare capping details come from the MTA.

title: Halloween Weekend NYC 2026: Parties Night by Night
h1: Halloween weekend NYC 2026: the night-by-night party plan
description: Halloween weekend NYC 2026, night by night: the parties we list from Thursday to Sunday, Village Parade basics and happy hour bars for pre-drinks.
answer: Halloween falls on a Saturday in 2026, so the parties run four nights, from Thursday, October 29 to Sunday, November 1. A smart Halloween weekend NYC plan saves its energy for Saturday: the Village Halloween Parade steps off on Sixth Avenue at 7 p.m., then House of Yes, Elsewhere, SILO Brooklyn and the Lower East Side hotel parties run toward sunrise. For pre-drinks, Dive Bar BK in Bushwick, Ten Bells on the Lower East Side and Kingston Hall in the East Village all run Saturday happy hours a few minutes from the parties.
intro: We list 124 published parties across Halloween weekend 2026, and 106 of them are Halloween themed. This guide sorts them by night and neighborhood, with a link to each party page for tickets, age rules and the latest status. The full live list is on our Halloween party page and in the table at the bottom of this post. The shape of the weekend is simple. Thursday is a warm-up for the clubs. Friday is the first full night, with hotel rooftops in Manhattan and big rooms in Brooklyn. Saturday is Halloween itself: daytime rooftops, evening boat cruises, the parade on Sixth Avenue, then the longest night of the year on the city's dance floors. Sunday is for day parties and one last dance. Bushwick is the center of gravity, with House of Yes, Elsewhere, SILO Brooklyn, The Sultan Room, Sea Wolf and The Chocolate Factory a short walk from each other. The Lower East Side and East Village form the Manhattan cluster, and Williamsburg splits between the Wythe Avenue waterfront and the Bushwick Avenue side. Our pre-drink picks sit in each of those areas, plus one in the West Village for parade night.

picks.why: A sports-minded dive on Troutman Street, one minute from the Jefferson Street L stop. Its happy hour runs Monday through Saturday, so it covers both Friday and Saturday pre-drinks. The bar does not list specific deal items online, so ask what is included. Location is the selling point: Sea Wolf Bushwick is next door, House of Yes about a minute away and Elsewhere roughly four minutes on foot.

A bar on Bushwick Avenue, one minute from the Montrose Avenue L stop, with a happy hour every day of the week. The deal is long on drinks: drafts, well drinks, house cocktails, several margaritas and a negroni. Sleepwalk, home of the BLOODLUST Halloween dance party on Saturday, is right next door, and The Meadows and Signal are roughly six and eight minutes away on foot.

A pub on Kent Avenue by the Williamsburg waterfront, about seven minutes from Bedford Avenue on the L. Happy hour is weekdays only, so this is your Friday pick, with the house pilsner and a beer or seltzer with a shot on the deal list. Arlo Williamsburg, Desert 5 Spot and Superior Ingredients are each one to two minutes away, and the Westlight roof at The William Vale about three.

A wine and oyster bar on Broome Street, two minutes from Delancey Street (F, J, M, Z). Happy hour runs every day from opening, weekends included, with discounted oysters and carafes of wine, a lighter way to start a long night. VIRGO and Hotel Chantelle, both hosting Halloween parties on Friday and Saturday, are about a minute away, and Pianos is roughly five minutes on foot.

A Second Avenue bar four minutes from Astor Place on the 6, with one of the few 2-for-1 deals on our list: buy one beer, prosecco or well drink and get a second. It runs Monday through Saturday, plus a Sunday window. Saint, where Saint & Sinners Halloween plays on Saturday, is about a minute away, and Deluxx Fluxx, home of Gyalhattan Halloween, about four.

A New American bar and restaurant on Greenwich Avenue, two minutes from 8th Avenue (A, C, E, L). Happy hour runs daily, Saturday included, with oysters and a short happy hour menu, served at the bar and on the patio only. It is our parade-night pick: Sixth Avenue at 14th Street, near the north end of the route, is about six minutes on foot, and Le Petit Village about four.

sections.body: Eleven parties on our list start on Thursday, and seven of them carry the Halloween theme. Bushwick takes most of the night. Gaydar Halloween opens the House of Yes run, Slizzween is at The Chocolate Factory and Downstairs: Nightbreed is an 80s night at Purgatory. DYKE-o-Ween fills The Sultan Room, and Freaq: A BQ Hour Halloween Party is at C'mon Everybody in Bed-Stuy. For house and techno, Midnight Stereo Presents: Halloween runs at Signal. In Manhattan, Dead Disco takes over the roof at the PUBLIC Hotel. One warning: Out & Abt: Halloween Edition at Elsewhere is listed as sold out, so skip it unless you already hold a ticket.

sections.h: Friday, October 30: the first big night
sections.body: Friday has 45 parties on our list, 37 of them Halloween themed. If you like daylight, 1 Hotel Rooftop Halloween in Brooklyn Heights and the Rivo Day & Night takeover at Superior Ingredients in Williamsburg both start in the afternoon. After dark, Bushwick stacks up: Zombie Prom at House of Yes, SILOWEEN: Asylum at SILO Brooklyn, Gorgeous Gorgeous Halloween at The Sultan Room and WITCHSLAP, a skate, drag wrestling and dance night at Xanadu. For bigger rooms, The Heist takes over an old savings bank at One Hanson Place in Fort Greene, The Vampire Ball: Mischief Night is at Industry City in Sunset Park, and Halloween Weekender: Apollonia at Signal runs across the weekend. Circoloco's Friday night at Brooklyn Storehouse is listed as sold out. Manhattan's Friday is a hotel and rooftop night. DO NOT DISTURB at Hotel Chantelle and KELLAND: Halloween at Virgo are a couple of minutes apart on the Lower East Side. Mercer Halloween is on the Crown rooftop at Hotel 50 Bowery, Nevermore Goth Rave is at DROM in the East Village, and Halloween at Chambers Courthouse is a party inside the Surrogate's Court building at 31 Chambers Street. For something dressier, The Black Crystal Masquerade at the Baccarat Hotel runs Friday and Saturday.

Saturday is the peak, with 62 parties on our list and 57 of them Halloween themed. The day starts on the roofs: 1 Hotel Rooftop Halloween and Saints & Sinners on the Roof at Superior Ingredients both begin in the afternoon, and the ParaPara Halloween Party at Seventh Heaven in Bushwick wraps up by early evening. Five boat parties leave in the evening, including Horror on the Hudson and the Halloween Dance Cruise on the Liberty Belle from Pier 36. They are back before midnight, early enough to go dancing after. Late night in Brooklyn: House of Hallucinations at House of Yes, Elsewhere Halloween, SILOWEEN: Asylum II, Purple Disco Machine at Pacha New York and Bakermat at The Chocolate Factory are all in Bushwick. Williamsburg has Moon Boots and BYNX on the Westlight roof, Vampires and Vixens at Superior Ingredients and BLOODLUST at Sleepwalk. The Vampire Ball: All Hallows Eve returns to Industry City, and in Queens, ReSolute's Why So Serious!? at H0l0 in Ridgewood is listed to run into Monday morning. In Manhattan, the parade crowd spills into the Village and Chelsea: Moulin Rouge Halloween at Le Petit Village, Halloween at The Standard Biergarten, Blood Moon Ascent at Rory's Rooftop and Haunted Hotel at the Alameda Hotel. Downtown east, try Halloween at Pianos with its costume contest, MASHBIT at Virgo, Gyalhattan Halloween for dancehall and hip-hop at Deluxx Fluxx, or Daft Disko at DROM. Two Saturday headliners are listed as sold out: Audien at The Gallery at Dream Downtown and Horse Meat Disco at Knockdown Center.

sections.h: The Village Halloween Parade: date, route and how to march
sections.body:
The 53rd Village Halloween Parade is on Saturday, October 31, 2026, at 7 p.m. According to the parade's official site, it starts at Canal Street and Sixth Avenue and goes north up Sixth Avenue to 15th Street. This year's theme is Body & Soul.

To march, you need a costume: the organizers say only people in costume are welcome to march in the parade. The lineup area is at Canal Street and Sixth Avenue, from 6:30 to 9 p.m. You can only enter it from the east and south, by Sullivan, East Broome and Canal Streets, and if you come from the west, enter only from Canal Street. The official site also sells VIP tickets and places in a Special Theme Section that let you skip the line.

The organizers recommend the subway, since parking is always hard and the parade makes it worse. If you are watching rather than marching, plan the night on foot: a pre-drink in the West Village at Jack & Charlie's No. 118, the parade on Sixth Avenue, then one of the Village parties above.

sections.h: Sunday, November 1, and how to pace the weekend
sections.body: Sunday has six parties on our list, five of them Halloween themed, and most start in daylight. Circoloco's Sunday session at Brooklyn Storehouse starts at midday, Day of the Dead at 1 Hotel begins in the afternoon in Brooklyn Heights, and Halloween Weekend Sunday Funday at Bar 13 near Union Square plays 80s, disco and funk. Night owls have Jungle Galactica at Somewhere Nowhere and a late lineup at SILO Brooklyn. Four nights is a lot, so pick two big ones and keep the others light. Daylight saving time ends early Sunday, November 1, when clocks fall back an hour, so Saturday night gets an extra hour. Every party on this list is 21 and up, and Common Ground's two Halloween nights are 23 and up. Check each party page before you go for ticket status: several are already listed as sold out, and more will follow.

faq.a: Halloween falls on Saturday, October 31, 2026. The parties on our list run from Thursday, October 29 to Sunday, November 1, and Saturday is the busiest night with 62 listings.
faq.q: When is Halloween weekend in NYC in 2026?

faq.a: Saturday, October 31, 2026, at 7 p.m. It starts at Canal Street and Sixth Avenue and runs north up Sixth Avenue to 15th Street, per the official parade site.
faq.q: When and where is the Village Halloween Parade in 2026?

faq.a: Yes, if you wear a costume. Only people in costume may march. Join the lineup at Canal Street and Sixth Avenue between 6:30 and 9 p.m., entering from Sullivan, East Broome or Canal Street.
faq.q: Can I march in the Village Halloween Parade?

faq.a: Yes. Out & Abt at Elsewhere, Circoloco's Friday night, Audien at The Gallery at Dream Downtown and Horse Meat Disco at Knockdown Center are already listed as sold out. Buy early and check each party page for the latest status.
faq.q: Do Halloween parties in NYC sell out?

faq.a: Dive Bar BK, Post No Bills, Ten Bells, Kingston Hall and Jack & Charlie's No. 118 all run Saturday happy hours near party venues. Kent Ale House by the Williamsburg waterfront is a Friday option, since its happy hour is weekdays only.
faq.q: Where can I get cheap drinks before a Halloween party?

table_title: Every Halloween party we list
method: We pulled every published party on our list with a night date from October 29 to November 1, 2026: 124 parties at 74 venues, last checked October 13, 2026. Party details come from the ticket listings linked on each party page. Bar picks come from each bar's own website, with happy hours checked September 2, 2026; we kept bars with a Friday or Saturday window and measured walking distance to the party venues. Parade facts come from the Village Halloween Parade's official site and the daylight saving date from NIST, both checked October 15, 2026.

title: Early Happy Hours NYC: Where Drinks Start by 3pm
h1: Early happy hours NYC: bars that pour from midday to mid-afternoon
description: Early happy hours NYC guide: 8 bars in four boroughs whose weekday deals start by 3pm, for remote workers, visitors and shift workers.
answer: About a third of the bars on our list, 243 of 742, start a weekday happy hour by 3pm, and 63 of them get going by noon. Our early happy hours NYC picks: The Stag's Head in Midtown starts in the late morning, Half Moon in the Financial District and District Local in Chelsea start at midday, Gordo's Cantina in Bushwick and Spanglish NYC in Astoria do the same on the other side of the river, and Kingsbridge Social Club covers the Bronx.
intro:
Most New York happy hours open as the office empties. This guide is about the other third: 243 of the 742 bars on our list start a weekday happy hour by 3pm, and 63 of them begin by noon. Mid-afternoon is the most common early start by far, so a late-morning or midday window is the real find.

An early window changes what happy hour is for. It can be a long lunch with a beer, an afternoon laptop session that ends with a drink, or a post-shift round for people whose working day ends when everyone else's is half done. Our eight picks cover Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx, and the live table at the bottom of the page lists every bar with an early weekday start.

Read the day pattern on each card before you go. Most early windows run Monday to Friday, a few skip Monday or Friday, and a handful, like Therapy Wine Bar's, run every day of the week.

picks.why: A bar at East 51st Street and Second Avenue, three minutes from Lexington Avenue/53rd Street (E, F, 6). Its weekday happy hour starts in the late morning, one of the earliest on our list, and covers a house lager, a New England IPA, cider, canned lager and well drinks. Happy hour bites start later in the day. Good for a long Midtown lunch or an early exit from the office.

A Financial District bar on Trinity Place, one minute from Rector Street on the R and W. The weekday window opens at midday and runs into the evening, with a house margarita, an espresso martini, a whiskey gold rush, draft beers, house wine and a soft baked pretzel. Downtown visitors can slot it between afternoon sights, and office workers can stretch a late lunch.

A Chelsea bar on Seventh Avenue, two minutes from the 14th Street station (1, 2, 3, F, L, M). Happy hour starts at midday on weekdays and covers a cucumber vodka cocktail, a spicy margarita, house wine and prosecco, well drinks, drafts and an IPA. With six lines at the corner, it is an easy meeting point for friends coming from different directions.

A Bushwick cantina on St Nicholas Avenue, two minutes from DeKalb Avenue on the L. The weekday deal starts at midday and keeps it simple: lime margaritas, micheladas and a beer-and-shot combo. It suits remote workers and freelancers in the neighborhood who want a change of scene before the evening crowd, and the L runs straight to 14th Street in Manhattan.

A wine bar on Malcolm X Boulevard in Bed-Stuy, about seven minutes from Utica Avenue (A, C). Unusually, its happy hour runs every day from midday, weekends included, with house cocktails, sangria, a wine of the day and a few bites like hummus and mozzarella sticks. The bar notes the deal is for drinking in, not takeout. Shift workers with a weekday off get the same deal as everyone else.

A Mexican restaurant and bar on Ditmars Boulevard, five minutes from the Astoria/Ditmars Boulevard station on the N and W. Happy hour starts at midday on weekdays with frozen and hibiscus margaritas, red and white sangria, house wine and beer. Astoria has more early happy hours than any other neighborhood outside Manhattan on our list, and this is one of four there that start by noon.

A bar on Roosevelt Avenue, two minutes from 103rd Street/Corona Plaza on the 7. The weekday window opens in the early afternoon and closes before the evening rush, with house margaritas, domestic beers, house wine and snacks like nachos, queso fundido and elotes discounted, plus shots and tacos at a set price. It is a short window, so it fits best straight after a morning shift.

A restaurant on Kingsbridge Avenue in the Bronx, one minute from 238th Street on the 1. Its weekday happy hour starts mid-afternoon, right at the cutoff for this list, with a discount on draft beer, wine and sangria plus small plates like meatballs, Calabrian honey wings and pizza fritte. It is our Bronx pick, and an easy stop for anyone riding the 1 up from Manhattan.

sections.h: Who an early happy hour is for
sections.body: Remote workers get the most out of it. A window that opens at midday, like those at Half Moon, District Local and Gordo's Cantina, means you can close the laptop whenever the work is done instead of racing an early-evening cutoff. Be a good guest: order as you would at night, and leave the big tables to groups once the room fills. Visitors between sights can use an early start as a rest stop. Half Moon is a minute from Rector Street in the Financial District, and The Stag's Head is a few minutes from Lexington Avenue/53rd Street in Midtown. If your afternoon ends at a Broadway show, our pre-theater guide covers Times Square, which ties the Financial District for the most early happy hours on our list. Shift workers, from nurses and doormen to bartenders and line cooks, often finish when the rest of the city is still at work. An early window turns a post-shift drink into a deal. Therapy Wine Bar is the rare pick that runs every day, which helps if your days off fall midweek or your shifts cover the weekend.

sections.h: How to plan an early happy hour
sections.body: Start with the day pattern, not the clock. Early windows skew to weekdays, and several on our list skip Monday or run only part of the week, so check the card for the day you want. Our happy hour now page shows what is running at the moment you open it. Read the fine print on food. Some bars start the drinks deal before the food deal: The Stag's Head lists its happy hour bites later in the day than its beer and well drinks. Others limit the deal to drinking in, as Therapy Wine Bar does. If eating matters, look for the food tag on the card. Use the subway to chain stops. The L links Gordo's Cantina at DeKalb Avenue with District Local at 14th Street, and the 1 runs from 14th Street up to Kingsbridge Social Club at 238th Street. Several of these places also take reservations through their booking link, which is worth using for a group on a Friday.

sections.h: Best areas for an early start
sections.body: Manhattan holds 171 of the 243 early happy hours on our list. Times Square and the Financial District lead with 14 each, followed by Midtown with 13, the Upper West Side and Murray Hill with 12 each, and Tribeca and the Upper East Side with 11. For a start before noon, Midtown and Murray Hill have the most, five each, which makes the East Side office belt the strongest bet for a lunchtime round. Outside Manhattan, Astoria leads with 10 early happy hours, four of them starting by noon, followed by Jackson Heights and Park Slope with eight each. Brooklyn has 33 early spots in total, Queens 30 and the Bronx three. Staten Island is small but early: six of its eight listings start by mid-afternoon on weekdays, and The Rock House runs from midday every day. If you are choosing a neighborhood rather than a bar, open the neighborhood pages for the Financial District, Midtown or Astoria and compare the start times on the cards.

faq.a: For this guide, a weekday happy hour window that starts by 3pm. On our list that is 243 of 742 bars, about a third. Late-night windows that start after midnight are not included.
faq.q: What counts as an early happy hour?

faq.a: Yes, 63 bars on our list start a weekday window by noon. The Stag's Head in Midtown starts in the late morning, and Half Moon, District Local, Gordo's Cantina, Therapy Wine Bar and Spanglish NYC start at midday.
faq.q: Are there happy hours in NYC that start at noon or earlier?

faq.a: Mostly not. Early windows are a weekday habit. Among our picks, only Therapy Wine Bar in Bed-Stuy runs its happy hour every day, weekends included.
faq.q: Do early happy hours run on weekends?

faq.a: Times Square and the Financial District, with 14 each, then Midtown with 13. Outside Manhattan, Astoria leads with 10.
faq.q: Which neighborhoods have the most early happy hours?

faq.a: Yes. Kingsbridge Social Club is a minute from 238th Street on the 1. On Staten Island, six of the eight places on our list start by mid-afternoon on weekdays, and The Rock House runs from midday every day.
faq.q: Is there an early happy hour in the Bronx or on Staten Island?

table_title: Every weekday happy hour that starts by 3pm
method: We filtered the 742 bars on our list to those with a weekday happy hour window starting by 3pm, which gave 243 bars; late-night windows that start after midnight were left out. Hours and deals come from each bar's own website, checked September 2, 2026. We chose picks with a detailed published deal list and spread them across four boroughs and eight neighborhoods.

title: Best Neighborhoods for Nightlife in NYC, Ranked by Data
h1: The best neighborhoods for nightlife in NYC, ranked by happy hours and parties
keyword: best neighborhoods for nightlife in nyc
description: The best neighborhoods for nightlife in NYC, ranked by happy hours and upcoming parties, with the trains to take and a bar to start each night.
answer: Going by our own data, the best neighborhoods for nightlife in NYC are Bushwick, Williamsburg, Chelsea, the East Village, Midtown, the Lower East Side and Greenwich Village, ranked by how many happy hours and upcoming parties each one has. Bushwick has the most parties, Midtown has the most happy hours, and Williamsburg sits near the top of both lists. For an easy night, start at a happy hour like Post No Bills in Williamsburg or Ten Bells on the Lower East Side, then walk to a party a block or two away.
intro:
Some New York neighborhoods make a night out easy: plenty of happy hours to start, plenty of parties to finish, and a subway line that gets you home. To find them, we ranked every neighborhood on YaY NYC by two things we track ourselves: how many bars there have a current happy hour, and how many upcoming parties are on our calendar there, matched by the party's listed neighborhood or its venue's.

The seven below came out on top. Some win on one list, like Bushwick on parties and Midtown on happy hours, and some are strong on both, like Williamsburg and the East Village. We left out areas with long happy hour lists but almost no parties; they get a mention in the last section. The numbers move as bars change their deals and new parties go on sale, so each neighborhood page and both maps show live counts.

Each section covers the kinds of places you will find, the days with the most deals, the trains to take and where the parties happen. The picks are one or two bars per neighborhood that make a good first stop.

picks.why: A bar on Wilson Avenue, six minutes on foot from the Morgan Avenue L stop. The happy hour runs every day of the week and covers margaritas, including a spicy cucumber version, plus house wine, red sangria, tequila and tacos. That makes it an easy first stop before a Bushwick party: Seventh Heaven Bar & Karaoke is about five minutes away, and House of Yes and The Sultan Room are under ten.

A bar on Bushwick Avenue, a one-minute walk from the Montrose Avenue L stop, with a happy hour that runs every day. The deal is wide: drafts, beer, well drinks, house cocktails, a Negroni and several margaritas, from grapefruit to elderflower. It sits right next door to Sleepwalk, one of the busiest party venues on our Williamsburg calendar, so you can start here and walk straight in.

OTB on Broadway, six minutes from the Marcy Avenue stop on the J, M and Z, runs its happy hour on Saturday and Sunday only, which is rare in a neighborhood where most deals are weekday-only. It covers margaritas, Aperol, house wine, a budget beer, a plain hot dog and oysters by the dozen. It takes reservations, and the Jolene Sound Room and LilliStar at Moxy Williamsburg are about two minutes away.

A Mexican taqueria and bar on Eighth Avenue, three minutes from the 23rd Street stop on the C and E. The happy hour runs Sunday through Thursday, so it covers the weekend night most Chelsea deals skip. Expect margaritas (classic, frozen, watermelon and Blue Hawaiian), a passionfruit martini, a lemon drop, small bites and tacos. It takes reservations, and the party venue loulou is about a minute away on the same avenue.

A bar on Avenue A with a happy hour every day of the week, including Saturday, a day fewer East Village bars cover than Sunday. The deal is simple and drinks-only: draft beer, house wine and well drinks. The 1st Avenue L stop is seven minutes away. DROM, one of the neighborhood's party venues, is about a minute and a half away on Avenue A, so this works as a warm-up before a night there.

A bar at East 51st Street and Second Avenue, three minutes from the Lexington Avenue–53rd Street stop on the 6, E and F. The happy hour is a weekday, all-day deal covering lagers, cider, a New England IPA, well drinks and happy hour bites, so it suits a late lunch that turns into after-work drinks. It takes reservations, which helps when you are bringing a group on a Friday.

A bar on Broome Street, two minutes from the Delancey Street stop on the F, J, M and Z. The happy hour runs every day and covers oysters and carafes of wine, so it fits a Sunday as well as a weeknight. VIRGO and Hotel Chantelle, two Lower East Side party venues, are each about a minute away, which makes this a natural first stop on a Friday or Saturday. It takes reservations.

A restaurant on Carmine Street, two minutes from the Houston Street stop on the 1. The happy hour runs every day and covers house wine, rosé, a Tommy's margarita, a Venetian spritz and bar bites, which makes it one of the easier weekend options in the Village. It takes reservations. Houston Hall, which hosts parties on our calendar, is about two minutes away on West Houston Street.

sections.body: Bushwick ranks first because of parties. It has the most upcoming parties on our calendar by a wide margin, and they fill big rooms on and around Wyckoff, Scott and Johnson Avenues: SILO Brooklyn, House of Yes and its Onyx Room, Elsewhere, 99 Scott, The Chocolate Factory and Sea Wolf Bushwick. House, techno and disco lead most lineups, Sea Wolf leans Latin and reggaeton, and The Sultan Room on Starr Street adds afrobeats, amapiano and dancehall. Friday and Saturday carry most nights, though SILO books plenty of midweek dates too. The happy hour list is shorter than in the other top neighborhoods and almost all bars, with a pub, a dive bar and a rooftop in the mix. Wine, cocktails and food deals come up most, with cheap beer at a few places and oysters at one. Deals run evenly from Monday to Friday, and about half also run on Saturday or Sunday, the biggest weekend share of any neighborhood in this guide. Getting there: the L does most of the work, with stops at Morgan Avenue, Jefferson Street, DeKalb Avenue and Myrtle–Wyckoff Avenues. The M covers Central Avenue and meets the L at Myrtle–Wyckoff. Every deal is on the Bushwick happy hours page.

Williamsburg is the one neighborhood near the top of both rankings: it has the second-longest happy hour list on the site and one of the three busiest party calendars. About three in five places are bars, the rest mostly restaurants plus a few pubs, and wine, cocktails and food deals turn up equally often. Oysters appear on several menus. Deals peak Tuesday through Thursday, thin out a little on Monday and Friday, and only about a quarter run on the weekend, so a Saturday plan here takes more picking. The parties stretch from the waterfront to the Bushwick border. Sleepwalk on Bushwick Avenue books a long run of Wednesday nights with disco, funk and house. Superior Ingredients on Wythe Avenue covers house, techno and disco, mostly on Saturdays. The Meadows and The Brooklyn Monarch on Meadow Street mix techno, drum and bass, Latin and pop, and Westlight Rooftop at The William Vale hosts house nights up top. Getting there: Bedford Avenue on the L is the stop for the most bars, followed by Marcy Avenue on the J, M and Z. Lorimer Street, Graham Avenue and Montrose Avenue on the L cover the east side, and the G stops at Metropolitan Avenue and Broadway. The full list is on Williamsburg happy hours.

Chelsea ranks third almost entirely on parties: no Manhattan neighborhood has more upcoming parties on our calendar. Two rooms do most of the work. Somewhere Nowhere NYC on West 25th Street runs Latin and drum and bass nights from Friday through Sunday, and Marquee New York on Tenth Avenue books mostly Fridays and Saturdays. PHD Lounge on West 16th Street adds house and EDM, with The Gallery at Dream Downtown at the same address, loulou sits on Eighth Avenue, and to the north Marquee Skydeck at Edge Hudson Yards hosts parties of its own. The happy hours lean toward bars, with some restaurants and a few pubs. Cocktails come up most, then food deals such as tacos, olives and small bites, and several places run their deal all day. Deals hold steady from Tuesday to Friday, dip on Monday, and about a third continue on the weekend. Getting there: the A, C, E and L stop at 14th Street and 8th Avenue for the south end. The C and E also stop at 23rd Street, the 1 stops at 23rd and 28th Streets, and the 7 reaches the far west side at 34th Street–Hudson Yards. The full list is on Chelsea happy hours.

The East Village has the third-longest happy hour list on the site and a solid party calendar, which makes it the most balanced choice in Manhattan. About seven in ten places on our list are bars rather than restaurants. Wine and cocktails lead, food deals are less common, and the weekend is stronger than in Williamsburg or Midtown, especially Sunday, which more places here cover than Saturday. Weekday deals peak on Tuesday and stay steady through Friday. For parties, Deluxx Fluxx on East 11th Street is the busiest room, with hip-hop, R&B, dancehall and Latin nights on Fridays and Saturdays. DROM on Avenue A books house, disco, drum and bass and pop, while Saint Restaurant Bar & Speakeasy on Second Avenue and Blind Barber New York on East 10th Street add the odd party night. Getting there: 1st Avenue on the L serves the biggest share of bars here, followed by the 6 at Astor Place and the F at 2nd Avenue. The L also stops at 3rd Avenue for the Second Avenue strip. The full list is on East Village happy hours.

Midtown has more happy hours on our site than any other neighborhood, and the list is built around office life. Bars and restaurants are close to even, with a few pubs. Cocktails and wine are on most menus, food deals on about a third, oysters on several, and a good number run all day. Monday through Thursday is the peak, Friday is a little lighter, and about a third keep a deal on the weekend. Parties are fewer, but there is a steady base. Nebula on West 41st Street books Tuesday, Friday and Saturday nights, Daintree Rooftop on West 38th Street hosts house nights, and Margaritaville Times Square adds the occasional party. Getting there: our Midtown runs from the blocks around 28th Street up into the 50s, so choose a stop by area. The 6 serves the most bars, at 28th Street and 51st Street. The E and F stop at Lexington Avenue–53rd Street and 5th Avenue–53rd Street, the 7, B, D, F and M at 42nd Street–Bryant Park and 5th Avenue, and the 4, 5, 6, 7 and S at Grand Central. The full list is on Midtown happy hours.

sections.h: 6. Lower East Side: parties on a tight grid
sections.body: The Lower East Side ranks sixth, with a mid-sized happy hour list and a party calendar about as busy as the East Village next door. Bars and restaurants are close to even, with a couple of pubs. Cocktails come first, food deals are common, and a weekend deal is easier to find here than in Midtown or Chelsea. Tuesday to Thursday is the peak, and Monday is noticeably thinner than elsewhere, so plan around it. For parties, The Delancey on Delancey Street is the busiest room, with Latin and reggaeton on Fridays and Saturdays. VIRGO on Grand Street books house, Hotel Chantelle on Ludlow Street adds house and EDM, and Pianos: The Mezzanine, The Skinny Bar and 122 Orchard St fill in around Orchard and Ludlow. Liberty Belle, Pier 36 NYC on South Street runs Saturday parties. Getting there: the F stops at Delancey Street, 2nd Avenue and East Broadway, and Essex Street adds the J, M and Z. The J and Z also stop at Bowery for the western blocks. The full list is on Lower East Side happy hours.

Greenwich Village has one of the five longest happy hour lists on the site but few parties, which puts it seventh. Bars make up a little over half, restaurants about a third, plus a few pubs, spread along Hudson Street, Carmine Street and the blocks off West 4th Street. Wine leads, then cocktails and food deals, with oysters at a few addresses. Thursday is the strongest day, and weekend deals are common: about two in five places keep one. For parties, Houston Hall on West Houston Street and Le Petit Village on Seventh Avenue South host occasional nights, and the White Horse Tavern on Hudson Street books the odd party too. Getting there: the 1 covers the most bars, at Houston Street and Christopher Street–Stonewall. West 4th Street–Washington Square brings in the A, B, C, D, E, F and M. The full list is on Greenwich Village happy hours.

sections.h: How to choose: after work, a big night out or a weekend day
sections.body: After work, go where the weekday list is longest. Midtown has the most happy hours and many that run all day, which suits an early start near the office, and Williamsburg and the East Village have the next-longest lists. Three areas missed this ranking only because they have almost no parties: Hell's Kitchen and the Upper West Side both have long happy hour lists, and Astoria has a deep one along the N and W. For a big night out, start with a happy hour and walk to a party in the same neighborhood. Bushwick and Williamsburg share the L, so you can move from one to the other without changing trains, and the L also stops in the East Village and Chelsea on the Manhattan side. The East Village and the Lower East Side share the F at 2nd Avenue. Friday and Saturday carry most of the parties everywhere in this guide, so check the party map for what is on tonight. For a weekend day, pick places that keep the deal going on Saturday and Sunday. Bushwick has the biggest weekend share of the top neighborhoods, the East Village is stronger on Sunday than Saturday, and the Lower East Side and Greenwich Village both have plenty of weekend deals. In Williamsburg, look for weekend-only spots like OTB. The weekend happy hours page lists them all.

faq.a: It depends on the night you want. On our data, Bushwick has the most upcoming parties by a wide margin, Midtown has the most happy hours, and Williamsburg sits near the top of both, which makes it the safest all-round pick. In Manhattan, the East Village is the most balanced choice.
faq.q: What is the best neighborhood in NYC for nightlife?

faq.a: Brooklyn wins on parties: Bushwick has the busiest party calendar on our site and Williamsburg is close behind. Manhattan wins on choice: five of the seven neighborhoods in this guide are there, and Midtown, the East Village and Greenwich Village all have long happy hour lists. Many people do both, with a happy hour in Manhattan and then the L to Brooklyn.
faq.q: Is Brooklyn or Manhattan better for a night out?

faq.a: Friday and Saturday, by far, across every neighborhood in this guide. A few venues book midweek: Sleepwalk in Williamsburg hosts many Wednesday nights, Nebula in Midtown has Tuesdays, SILO Brooklyn runs parties from Tuesday to Thursday, and Somewhere Nowhere NYC in Chelsea keeps going on Sunday. The party map shows what is on tonight.
faq.q: Which nights are busiest for parties in NYC?

faq.a: Tuesday through Thursday. In most of the neighborhoods here those three days carry the most deals, Monday and Friday are a little lighter, and the weekend has the fewest. Midtown stays steady from Monday to Thursday. For weekends, Bushwick, the Lower East Side, Greenwich Village and the East Village have the biggest share of Saturday and Sunday deals.
faq.q: Which days have the most happy hours?

faq.a: Yes, and it is the easiest way to plan a night. Post No Bills is next door to Sleepwalk in Williamsburg, Ten Bells on Broome Street is about a minute from VIRGO and Hotel Chantelle, Niagara on Avenue A is a short walk from DROM, and El Coco on Eighth Avenue is a minute from loulou.
faq.q: Can I walk from a happy hour to a party in the same neighborhood?

faq.a: We added up two counts for each neighborhood: bars with a current happy hour on our site and upcoming parties on our calendar, matched by the party's neighborhood or its venue's. We skipped bars whose latest check found the deal had changed or could only partly confirm it, and left out areas with almost no parties. The counts move all the time, so the neighborhood pages and maps show live numbers.
faq.q: How did you rank these neighborhoods?

method: We ranked neighborhoods on October 16, 2026 by adding two counts from our own database: bars with a listed happy hour in each neighborhood, using each bar's neighborhood as corrected that day and leaving out bars whose latest recheck marked the deal as changed or partial, and upcoming parties on our calendar, matched by the party's listed neighborhood or its venue's. Neighborhoods with almost no upcoming parties were left out of the ranking. Kinds of places, busiest days and subway lines are summarized from the same bar rows. Happy hour details, days, booking links and subway walking times come from each bar's own website; the eight picks were last checked on October 15, 2026. Party listings come from the DICE ticket pages linked on each party page.

title: Things to Do in NYC at Night: Happy Hour to Last Call
h1: Things to do in NYC at night, one stage at a time
keyword: things to do in nyc at night
description: Things to do in NYC at night, in stages: happy hour, a rooftop, a dinner deal, a club night, a late bite and a few free sights, across the boroughs.
answer: The easiest way to plan things to do in NYC at night is in stages. Start with a rooftop round at Glass Ceiling Rooftop in Koreatown or Castell Rooftop Lounge near Times Square, eat off a happy hour menu at Papacito's in Greenpoint or Burgerology in Astoria, then pick a club night from our parties list. Finish at Soho Diner on Friday or Saturday, or at Meller's on the Upper East Side early in the week.
intro:
New York does not really have one night out. It has several, stacked on top of each other. The bars that discount drinks right after work are rarely the places that are busy after midnight, and the rooms where DJs play often do not get going until most happy hours have ended. If you plan the night as a series of stages, each with its own spot, you spend less and wait in fewer lines.

This guide walks through those stages in order: an early happy hour, a rooftop or a view, a dinner built from a happy hour menu, live music or a club night, a late deal, and a few free things that work after dark. Each stage links to a live page on yaynyc.com, so you can check what is running tonight instead of trusting a list that was right last month.

The picks below come from our bar data and spread across Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx. Every card shows the current hours and prices. Use the guide to choose the order, and the cards to check the clock.

picks.why: A rooftop on Broadway in Koreatown that runs its happy hour Tuesday through Saturday, which is unusual for a roof. The deal covers classic cocktails such as margaritas, old fashioneds and seasonal spritzes, plus martinis, flatbreads and a Caesar. The first window is short and early, so come straight from work, and a second one runs late at night. The 28th Street R and W station is a minute away.

A rooftop lounge inside the AC Hotel Times Square on West 40th Street, with Spanish tapas, small plates and flatbreads on the menu. The happy hour runs Monday to Friday and covers cocktails, wine and beer. It sits steps from Broadway, so it works as the first stop before a show. The 42nd Street-Port Authority station, served by a dozen lines, is three minutes away on foot.

A taco and margarita bar on Manhattan Avenue in Greenpoint with a happy hour every day of the week. The deal covers house and frozen margaritas, with the frozen ones two for one, plus pints, a tequila shot with a Tecate, tacos and nachos with or without meat. The bar also runs a third happy hour in the last hour of every night. Greenpoint Avenue on the G is three minutes away.

A burger bar on Ditmars Boulevard, three minutes from the last stop of the N and W in Astoria. The weekday happy hour is served at the bar only and covers wine, select drafts, well cocktails and a slider menu: the house sliders, short rib, buffalo chicken and a turkey burger. Two orders of sliders make a cheap dinner before a night out in Astoria or the ride back into Manhattan.

A tapas restaurant on Riverdale Avenue in the Bronx, about seven minutes on foot from 238th Street on the 1 train. The happy hour covers sangria, margaritas, house wines and every beer, Monday to Thursday, with an earlier window on Friday. Add a few plates from the regular menu and it becomes dinner. It is the northern end of this guide and a good start for anyone who lives uptown.

A diner on West Broadway in SoHo whose happy hour exists only in the small hours of Friday and Saturday nights. The deal is all food: hot wings, crispy cheese curds, smoky black-eyed pea hummus with flatbread, zucchini chips and a smash burger. It is a good landing spot after a club night or a late show downtown, and Canal Street on the A, C and E is a minute away.

A sports bar on Second Avenue on the Upper East Side whose happy hour starts late at night and runs into the early morning, Sunday through Thursday. The deal covers wine, frozen drinks, mixed drinks, margaritas in a long list of flavors and Aperol, plus canned beers, hard teas and seltzers. The 86th Street Q station is two minutes away, which keeps the ride home simple.

sections.h: Early evening: happy hour and a view
sections.body: Start the night when the deals start. Most happy hours on our list run on weekdays in the late afternoon and early evening, and many end before a typical dinner reservation. Open happy hours running now to see what is live at this minute, or the happy hour map to find the closest deal to wherever you are standing. If you want a view with the first drink, go up early. Rooftop deals are a short list, and nearly all of them run on weekdays and close early in the evening. Glass Ceiling Rooftop is the exception that adds Saturday and a late-night window, and Castell covers the weekdays near Times Square. The rooftop happy hours page has the rest. Open-air seating depends on the weather, so check before you head up on a cold or wet night.

sections.h: Dinner from a happy hour menu
sections.body: A happy hour with food can stand in for dinner if you order with a plan. Papacito's in Greenpoint has tacos and nachos on its list every day, Burgerology in Astoria discounts a whole slider menu on weekdays, and Tin Marin in Riverdale is a tapas restaurant with sangria on its happy hour. The happy hour food deals page lists every bar that includes food, and our cheap happy hour food guide goes deeper. Two habits help. Food deals are often served at the bar only, so sit there. And order food early in the window, because kitchens tend to get slower as the after-work crowd arrives.

Club nights in New York start late and lean toward Friday and Saturday. On our NYC parties list, Bushwick has the most nights, followed by Williamsburg, with Ridgewood in Queens and Chelsea, Flatiron and the Lower East Side in Manhattan close behind. Most of them are 21 and over, so bring ID. Browse by sound with house, techno, Latin, disco or jazz, or use the party map. A few nights coming up stand out. The Ritual with Anané and Louie Vega is a Sunday house session at H0L0 in Ridgewood on October 18. Soul In The Horn with Natasha Diggs brings house, soul, disco, funk and hip hop to Bushwick on Friday, October 23. Regal86, 1OO1O, Shekdash and 1morning mix Latin club rhythms with techno and breaks at 314 Scholes Street in Williamsburg on Friday, November 13. Techno Thursday: Melodic2Hard takes over SILO's main room in Bushwick on November 19, free with an RSVP. And Time Warp NYC runs two nights at the Brooklyn Navy Yard on November 20 and 21, with Sven Väth, DVS1 and VTSS on the bill. For the costume weekend, see Halloween parties.

The second round of deals comes after dark. A late night happy hour usually starts after the dinner rush, and most of them run early in the week rather than on Friday and Saturday. Meller's on the Upper East Side fits a Sunday to Thursday night, while Soho Diner saves its food deal for the weekend. Papacito's in Greenpoint adds a deal in the last hour of every night. Our reverse happy hour guide covers the format in more detail. Getting home is part of the plan. The subway runs 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, but not every line runs at all times, and late-night routes change, per the MTA. Check the MTA trip planner or app before you order the last round, and pick a final stop on a line that runs all night.

sections.h: Free things to do at night
sections.body: Some of the city's big views cost nothing. The Staten Island Ferry is free and runs 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, between Whitehall Terminal in Lower Manhattan and St. George on Staten Island, according to NYC DOT. The crossing takes about 25 minutes each way, with views of the Statue of Liberty, Ellis Island and the Lower Manhattan skyline. Boats run less often late at night, so check the schedule on the ferry's site. For a drink before boarding, see happy hours near South Ferry. Walking the Brooklyn Bridge is free too. NYC DOT runs the promenade, which has its own path for pedestrians beside a protected bike lane, and weekend crowds can be heavy, so a weeknight walk is calmer. Two park options work in the evening: the High Line is free and open until the evening, with earlier closing in winter, per its official site, and Central Park is open daily until 1 a.m., per the Central Park Conservancy. Pair a High Line walk with happy hours near the High Line.

faq.a: Ride the Staten Island Ferry, which is free and runs around the clock between Lower Manhattan and St. George, according to NYC DOT. Walk the Brooklyn Bridge promenade, stroll the High Line before it closes in the evening, or walk in Central Park, which is open until 1 a.m. per the Central Park Conservancy.
faq.q: What are some free things to do in NYC at night?

faq.a: Yes. The MTA says the subway runs 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, but not all lines run at all times and some routes change late at night. Check the MTA app or trip planner before heading home.
faq.q: Does the NYC subway run all night?

faq.a: Late. Most club nights on our list begin well after dinner and run into the early morning, and Friday and Saturday carry most of them. A few are daytime or Sunday sessions, so check the start time on each party page.
faq.q: When do club nights in NYC start?

faq.a: Usually. Most parties on our list are 21 and over, and a small number are 18 and over. Each party page shows the age limit from the ticket listing, so check it and bring a photo ID.
faq.q: Do I need to be 21 to go to NYC parties?

faq.a: Meller's on the Upper East Side runs a deal late at night from Sunday to Thursday, Soho Diner has a food deal in the small hours of Friday and Saturday, and Papacito's in Greenpoint has a deal in the last hour of every night. The late night happy hour page lists the rest.
faq.q: Where can I get a late night happy hour in NYC?

faq.a: Yes, but the list is short and most run on weekdays only, ending early in the evening. Glass Ceiling Rooftop in Koreatown runs Tuesday through Saturday, and Castell Rooftop Lounge near Times Square runs Monday to Friday.

title: Cheap Date Night NYC: 8 Happy Hours for Two
h1: Cheap date night NYC: happy hours for two
description: Cheap date night NYC ideas built on happy hour: wine bars, cocktail bars and small plates in eight neighborhoods, plus free walks nearby.
answer: The simplest cheap date night NYC plan: book the happy hour window instead of the dinner slot. Therapy Wine Bar in Bed-Stuy and Mayfield in Crown Heights run their deals every day, Big Tiny in Carroll Gardens covers Sunday through Thursday, and Bar Baserri in Williamsburg and La Devozione in Chelsea turn small plates into dinner. Then walk it off for free in Domino Park, on the High Line or in Central Park.
intro:
A date in New York gets expensive at the same moment every night: when the happy hour ends and the regular menu comes back. Move the date earlier and the same room, the same bartender and often the same wine list cost a lot less. Many restaurants take reservations for that early slot too, so you can plan it like a proper night out instead of hoping for two stools.

This guide is built for two people who want a real evening without a big bill. The picks are wine bars, cocktail bars and restaurants with small plates, chosen from our bar data for what the deal actually covers and which days it runs. They sit in eight different neighborhoods across Manhattan, Brooklyn and Queens, so there is likely one near you or near where you are staying.

After the picks you will find how to time the date around the window, how to choose between wine, cocktails and food, and which free walks sit close to the bars. Each card below shows the live hours and prices, so check it on the day.

picks.why: A wine bar on Malcolm X Boulevard in Bed-Stuy with a window that opens at midday and runs into the early evening, every day of the week. The deal covers house cocktails, including sangria, and a red or white wine of the day, with bites such as lemon hummus, buffalo chicken rolls and mozzarella sticks. It is in-house only. Utica Avenue on the A and C is about seven minutes away.

A Basque bar on Kent Avenue in Williamsburg whose happy hour is mostly food, Tuesday to Thursday: pan con tomate, patatas bravas with miso mayo and chipotle, and marinated Spanish olives with bread. These are plates made for sharing across a small table. Domino Park is a few minutes' walk away on the waterfront for after. Bedford Avenue on the L is about nine minutes on foot.

A restaurant on Smith Street in Carroll Gardens with a happy hour Sunday through Thursday. One deal covers a glass of red, white, rosé, orange or sparkling wine or the house spritz, and the menu adds combos that pair a drink with a classic pizza, six oysters or a tartine. It is one of the few picks here that works on a Sunday. Bergen Street on the F and G is four minutes away.

A restaurant on Franklin Avenue in Crown Heights with a happy hour every day of the week, weekends included. The deal is oysters by the piece plus beer and wine specials, an easy way to start a date before dinner on Franklin. The window is short and early, and the restaurant takes reservations, so book the start of the evening. Park Place on the Franklin Avenue Shuttle is a minute away.

An Italian restaurant and cocktail bar on West 16th Street in Chelsea. The weekday happy hour is served at the cocktail bar and communal tables only, and the food list includes crispy pasta chips made from spaghetti aglio e olio, a marinated olive plate and fried mac and cheese lollipops. The High Line runs a short walk to the west. The 14th Street A, C, E and L station is five minutes away.

A bar on Sixth Avenue in the West Village whose weekday happy hour covers house cocktails and martinis, red and white wine by the glass and beer, with a short food list that includes vegetable spring rolls and steamed crystal shrimp dumplings. The window is short and ends early, so meet straight from work. Washington Square Park is a short walk away. Houston Street on the 1 is three minutes away.

An Italian and American bar on Columbus Avenue on the Upper West Side. The weekday happy hour is served at the bar only and covers a short cocktail list, including a limoncello spritz and the Taylor Who, made with vodka, house hibiscus and lemon. Central Park is a few minutes east and stays open late, so a walk after drinks is easy. The 72nd Street 1, 2 and 3 station is five minutes away.

A bar on 34th Street in Astoria with an early-week happy hour, Monday to Thursday on our listing. The deal covers select house cocktails, marked on the menu, and a beer and shot. The cocktail list runs from a dirty pickle martini to a spicy margarita, so ask which ones count before you order. It is three minutes from 30th Avenue on the N and W.

sections.h: Time the date around the happy hour window
sections.body: Most happy hours on our list run on weekdays and end early in the evening, so the date has to start early too. Meet at the start of the window, not near the end: you get the full deal, an easier table and time for a second round before prices change. If one of you works late, look for the bars whose window runs every day or on Sunday, like Therapy Wine Bar, Mayfield and Big Tiny. Book if you can. Seven of these eight picks list online reservations, and an early slot is usually the easiest one to get. Ask whether the happy hour applies at your table: Da Capo serves it at the bar only, and La Devozione limits it to the cocktail bar and communal tables. Sitting side by side at a bar is a good date seat anyway. To find a deal running at this exact moment, open happy hours now, or pick a day such as Tuesday or Sunday.

Decide what kind of date it is before you pick the bar. A wine happy hour usually means a house red and white by the glass, sometimes sparkling or rosé. Big Tiny goes further with five styles, including orange wine, and Therapy Wine Bar pours a wine of the day. A cocktail happy hour tends to cover a few named drinks rather than the whole menu, as at Da Capo, Cha Cha Tang and Sweet Afton, so read the offer list first. If you want dinner out of it, go for food. Bar Baserri's deal is almost all tapas, La Devozione has several small plates on its list, and Mayfield's oysters make a good opener. Our cheap happy hour food guide and the oyster happy hours page have more options. Sharing three or four plates between two people can stand in for dinner.

sections.h: Pair it with a free walk nearby
sections.body: A cheap date gets better with a free second act. From Bar Baserri, Domino Park is a few minutes away on the Williamsburg waterfront, and the park's own site lists it as open daily until 11 p.m. From La Devozione, the High Line is a short walk west; it is free and open into the evening, closing earlier in winter, per Friends of the High Line. See happy hours near the High Line for more stops on that stretch. From Cha Cha Tang, it is a short walk to Washington Square Park and its marble arch, designed by Stanford White and dedicated in 1895, according to NYC Parks. From Da Capo, Central Park is a few blocks away, and the Central Park Conservancy lists it as open daily until 1 a.m. For a longer free outing, the Staten Island Ferry costs nothing, runs around the clock and passes the Statue of Liberty on its roughly 25-minute crossing, according to NYC DOT.

sections.h: A few rules for a cheap date
sections.body: Check the card on the day. Happy hours change, and the live hours and prices on each pick are more current than any article. Order the deal items, not the regular list, and ask once which drinks count, since many deals name exact cocktails or a single house wine. Keep the bar tab and the dinner plan in the same neighborhood so you are not paying for a cab between them. If the first bar is full, have a backup a few blocks away. The happy hour map shows every deal near you, and neighborhood pages such as Williamsburg, West Village and Upper West Side list the alternatives close to these picks.

faq.a: Book an early table during a happy hour at a wine bar or a small-plates restaurant, then take a free walk nearby. Bar Baserri in Williamsburg pairs well with Domino Park, La Devozione in Chelsea with the High Line, and Da Capo on the Upper West Side with Central Park.
faq.q: What is a good cheap date night idea in NYC?

faq.a: Therapy Wine Bar in Bed-Stuy and Mayfield in Crown Heights run their deals every day, and Big Tiny in Carroll Gardens runs Sunday through Thursday. Check each card for the current window before you go.
faq.q: Which NYC happy hours work on a Sunday date?

faq.a: Often, yes. Seven of the eight picks here list online reservations, including Mayfield, Bar Baserri, Cha Cha Tang and Da Capo. Ask whether the deal applies at your table, since some places serve it only at the bar.
faq.q: Can you make a reservation for happy hour?

faq.a: It can be if you share. Bar Baserri's happy hour is mostly tapas, La Devozione has several small plates, Big Tiny pairs a drink with a pizza, oysters or a tartine, and Therapy Wine Bar adds bites. Order early in the window.
faq.q: Is happy hour food enough for dinner?

faq.a: Walk the High Line before it closes in the evening, stroll Central Park, which is open until 1 a.m., visit the arch in Washington Square Park or ride the free Staten Island Ferry, which runs 24 hours a day according to NYC DOT.
faq.q: What free things can we do after drinks?

faq.a: At the start of the window. Most deals on our list run on weekdays and end early in the evening, so starting early gives you the full deal, an easier table and time for a second round.
