title: Trivia Happy Hour NYC: 8 Bars to Drink Cheap, Then Play
h1: Trivia happy hour NYC: bars where the deal meets the first round
description: Trivia happy hour NYC guide: 8 bars in Manhattan, Brooklyn and Queens where the deal runs into the quiz or ends just before it, sorted by night.
answer: For a trivia happy hour NYC night, pick a bar where the deal is still on when the quiz starts, or one where it ends just before. The Rabbit Hole in Astoria keeps its weekday happy hour going into Tuesday trivia. At Josie Woods Pub on Waverly Place, Keg & Lantern in Greenpoint, Phoenix Bar in the East Village and Faces & Names near Times Square, the deal ends at or before the first question, so come early.
intro:
Trivia night and happy hour are a natural pair. Both live on weeknights, and both reward the people who show up early. The catch is timing: most quizzes start in the evening, right around when most deals end. So the real question is whether the happy hour is still on when the first round begins, or ends close enough that you can get a round in before the cutoff.

We matched the 259 trivia nights on our list against the happy hour windows of the bars we cover. 51 of those nights are at bars with a happy hour page on this site, and 50 of them line up. At three, the deal is still running when the game starts. At the other 47, it ends within two hours before the game, which means a drink at the deal, then pens out. Our eight picks cover Manhattan, Brooklyn and Queens and five different nights of the week.

Trivia listings come from the companies and directories that publish them, read on October 16, 2026. Schedules change, so confirm with the bar before you go.

picks.why: A bar on Broadway in Astoria, two minutes from Steinway Street on the M and R. Tuesday trivia here is listed by NYC Trivia List, BadSlava and TriviaNearMe, which calls it free trivia, and the weekday happy hour is still running when the game starts. It covers shots, house beers and wines, house mixers, mocktails, frozen drinks and discounted apps, plus a free hot dog when you buy a beer or wine.

A pub at 11 Waverly Place, two minutes from 8th Street–NYU on the R and W. TriviaNYC runs a Wednesday game here, also listed by NYC Trivia List. Happy hour runs Monday to Friday from mid-afternoon and ends as the game begins, with draft beers, well drinks, a flavored martini, wine and buffalo wings on the list. Get there early and order before the first question.

A brewery pub on Nassau Avenue, one minute from the G at Nassau Avenue. NYC Trivia League runs weekly Tuesday trivia here, and Brooklyn Trivia Finder and TriviaNearMe list it too, the latter as free to play. The weekday happy hour covers any draft beer and ends right as the game begins. Get there early, order a round, and claim a table before the room fills with teams.

A pub on Fourth Avenue, one minute from Union Street on the R. NYC Trivia League hosts trivia here every Monday. The weekday happy hour wraps up shortly before the game, with money off the house cocktail menu and the non-alcoholic cocktails, plus a smaller discount on every tap, bottle and can. Come straight from work, order before the cutoff, then settle in for the questions.

A bar on Broadway at 38th Street, three minutes from Steinway Street on the M and R and a minute's walk from The Rabbit Hole. NYC Trivia League runs a weekly Monday game. The weekday happy hour ends about an hour before it, with signature cocktails like a smoked old fashioned and a spicy ginger margarita, select apps and jumbo wings. The bar's page also mentions a late happy hour every night, and it takes reservations through Resy.

A pub at 1644 Third Avenue, four minutes from 96th Street on the Q. NYC Trivia League runs weekly Wednesday trivia here, also listed by NYC Trivia List and BadSlava. The weekday happy hour includes food deals and ends about half an hour before the first round, so it suits a team that wants to eat first. It is our Upper East Side pick.

A bar on East 13th Street, a minute from 1st Avenue on the L. NYC Trivia League runs a weekly Thursday game here, also listed by NYC Trivia List. Happy hour runs every day from mid-afternoon and ends about an hour before trivia, with Bud and Bud Light, well drinks and red or white wine. Come early for the deal and stay for the questions.

A bar on West 54th Street, one minute from 7th Avenue on the B, D and E. NYC Trivia League runs a weekly Sunday game here, one of only 13 Sunday trivia nights on our list. Happy hour runs every day and ends as the game begins, with bottled domestic beers, red or white house wine, well drinks, a daily drink special and beer buckets. A good way to close out a weekend in Midtown.

sections.h: How to plan a trivia night around happy hour
sections.body: Start with the night, then pick the bar. Our trivia listings are sorted by day, and each day page shows the game's start time from the company that lists it. Then check the happy hour window on the bar's card for that same day. If the deal is still on at game time, as at The Rabbit Hole and Houston Hall, you can arrive whenever you like. If it ends before, plan to get there while it is still running. The early arrival does double duty. Trivia rooms fill up with regular teams, and the table you claim during happy hour is the one you will play at. Order your first round and any food before the cutoff, then switch to regular prices once the game starts. Our happy hour now page shows which deals are running at the moment you open it. Watch the cadence. Most picks here are weekly, per NYC Trivia League, but some games on our list run every other week or once a month. The trivia pages say which is which.

sections.h: Which nights have the most trivia
sections.body: Tuesday is the big night. Of the 259 trivia nights on our list, 91 fall on a Tuesday, 71 on a Wednesday, 42 on a Monday and 36 on a Thursday. The weekend is thin: 13 on Sunday, five on Friday and a single Saturday game. If you want the most choice, Tuesday trivia and Wednesday trivia are where to look, while Monday and Thursday still give you plenty. By borough, Manhattan has 121 trivia nights on our list, Brooklyn 102 and Queens 33, with two in the Bronx and one on Staten Island. NYC Trivia League runs 145 of the 259, which is why its name comes up so often in our picks. Browse by borough on the Manhattan, Brooklyn and Queens pages.

NYC Trivia League says its games cost nothing to play and that six players is the sweet spot for a team. If you have more than six, it suggests splitting into two teams and playing against each other. A night has six rounds of eight to ten questions, and most nights include a music round and a picture round. The house rules are short: no phones, do not shout out answers, and the host has the final say. League teams can play at more than one of its bars in a week, and the highest weekly score counts toward the season standings.

Other hosts set their own rules, so ask before the first round. A few habits help anywhere: bring people who know different things, agree on one writer for the answer sheet, and tip well, since your team holds a table all night.

If trivia is not your thing, or your friends would rather sing along than argue over capitals, try music bingo. There are 25 music bingo nights on our list, all run by NYC Trivia League, with Wednesday the busiest night at eight. The same timing trick applies: catch the happy hour, then play. Several bars on our list host both, on different nights. See the full schedule on our music bingo page, and for pool, darts, shuffleboard and arcade games, our guide to bars with games.

faq.a: Tuesday, by a wide margin. On our list, 91 of the 259 trivia nights are on Tuesday, followed by Wednesday with 71, Monday with 42 and Thursday with 36.
faq.q: What night has the most bar trivia in NYC?

faq.a: Rarely. Of the 50 trivia nights on our list that line up with a happy hour, only three have the deal still running when the game starts, all on Tuesday: The Rabbit Hole, Houston Hall and The Factory 380. At the rest, the happy hour ends before the game, so arrive early.
faq.q: Do happy hours last through trivia?

faq.a: At NYC Trivia League games, yes: the company says it costs nothing to play and its league is free to join. Other hosts set their own terms, so check the listing or ask at the bar.
faq.q: Is bar trivia free to play in NYC?

faq.a: NYC Trivia League calls six players the sweet spot and suggests splitting larger groups into two teams. Other hosts may have different limits, so ask the host before the first round.
faq.q: How many people can be on a trivia team?

faq.a: Not at NYC Trivia League games. Its rules ban phones and apps for looking up answers, and teams caught cheating are disqualified.
faq.q: Can I use my phone during bar trivia?

faq.a: Yes, though fewer games. There are 13 Sunday trivia nights on our list, including NYC Trivia League's weekly game at Faces & Names near Times Square. Sunday trivia has its own page on the site.
faq.q: Is there trivia on Sundays in NYC?

method: We took the 259 trivia nights in our listings, read on October 16, 2026 from NYC Trivia League, NYC Trivia List, BadSlava, TriviaNearMe, Brooklyn Trivia Finder and TriviaNYC, and matched every night held at a bar on our list against that bar's happy hour windows for the same day. A night counts when the window covers the game's start or ends within two hours before it; windows without a published start or end were left out. Happy hour hours and deals come from each bar's own website, checked between September 2 and October 16, 2026. Game rules come from NYC Trivia League's how-it-works page. We chose picks across three boroughs and five nights.

title: Happy Hours Near NYU: 7 Bars Close to Washington Square
h1: Happy hours near NYU, from the closest bar outward
description: Happy hours near NYU, sorted by the walk from Washington Square Park: pubs with cheap beer, cocktail bars and bar food deals, all within about ten minutes.
answer: The closest happy hours near NYU are Amity Hall on West 3rd Street and White Oak Tavern and Josie Woods Pub on Waverly Place, each two to four minutes from the middle of Washington Square Park. For beer go to The Red Lion or Phebes, for cocktails try White Oak Tavern, and for bar food head to Little Havana or The Spaniard.
intro:
Washington Square Park is the front yard of NYU, and plenty of after-class and after-work drinks sit within ten minutes of its center. We measured from the center of the park to every bar in our database and kept the ones within about 900 meters, then picked seven that cover the three things people around campus ask for: cheap beer, a proper cocktail, and food that counts as dinner.

The picks below run from closest to farthest, with the walk in minutes from the middle of the park. Most of these happy hours run on weekdays, which suits a class or office schedule. Prices are live on each card and in the table at the bottom, which lists every happy hour near the park, closest first.

picks.why: About two minutes from the middle of the park, Amity Hall on West 3rd Street is the closest happy hour to the square. It is a sports pub, and its weekday window starts around midday and runs into the early evening, one of the longest weekday stretches near campus. The pub posts its times but not the items, so check the card. The West 4th Street station is four minutes away.

Three minutes from the park, on Waverly Place, White Oak Tavern is a gastropub with comfort food and a short cocktail list: rose sangria, a jalapeño tequila Daisy Picante with blood orange, and a bourbon White Mule. Happy hour runs from midday into the early evening on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday, and the bar's menu says Thursday is happy hour all day. The R and W stop at 8th Street-NYU is two minutes away.

A few doors from White Oak on Waverly Place, about four minutes from the park, Josie Woods Pub runs happy hour Monday through Friday, from the afternoon into the early evening. Its happy hour menu includes buffalo wings alongside draft beer, well drinks and wine.

About four minutes south of the park on Bleecker Street, The Red Lion is a live music and sports bar. The weekday happy hour runs from late afternoon into early evening and covers Red Lion draft beer, mixed well drinks, house wine and the house Red Lion Mule or Margarita. Come at the end of the window and stay for the band. West 4th Street is five minutes away.

Five minutes west of the park on Cornelia Street, Little Havana runs a bar-only happy hour on weekdays in the late afternoon. The food is the draw: nachos with black beans, cheese sauce and pico de gallo, french fries, and a Cuban sandwich with slow-roasted pulled pork. Sit at the bar or the deal does not apply. West 4th Street is a two-minute walk.

Six minutes west of the park on West 4th Street, The Spaniard is a bar with classic American bar food. Weekdays from late afternoon into early evening, happy hour brings a discount on all drafts, the Little Spaniard smash burger with fries, a griddled hot dog called the Happy Dawg, and a weekly featured spirit pour. Christopher Street-Stonewall on the 1 is one minute away.

About eight minutes east of the park, on the Bowery, Phebes is the beer-first pick. Its weekday happy hour runs from late afternoon into the evening, one of the longer windows on this list, and covers beers, Guinness and Stella drafts, wines and select cocktails. It does not run on holidays. The Bleecker Street station on the 6, B, D, F and M is four minutes away.

sections.body:
The legal age to buy alcohol in New York is 21, and bars can be penalized for serving anyone younger, whatever the person looks like or claims. Expect to be asked for ID, even at an afternoon happy hour.

Bring a real government ID. The New York State Liquor Authority lists a valid driver's license from New York, another state or Canada, a New York non-driver ID, a U.S. military ID, or a valid passport as acceptable proof of age. A college ID is not enough on its own; the SLA says it can only back up one of those documents. New York's Mobile ID is also accepted, per a 2024 SLA advisory.

On a student budget, the long weekday windows help. Amity Hall and White Oak Tavern start around midday, so a gap between classes can line up with happy hour. For beer, The Red Lion, The Spaniard and Phebes all put draft beer on the happy hour menu. For food that works as dinner, Little Havana and The Spaniard are the two to know.

If you want a quieter drink or are meeting visiting parents, look north of the park. On West 8th Street, 8th Street Winecellar runs a daily happy hour on select glasses and bottles, plus an oyster happy hour Monday through Thursday. Its neighbor Amelie Wine Bar, a French bistro, has a daily happy hour in the late afternoon. On West 10th Street, APERITIVO by CARTA does weekday wine, spritzes, oysters, beer, cider, zero-proof drinks and plates to share, and takes table bookings for groups.

For a sit-down meal with a deal, White Oak Tavern's gastropub menu works. The Grey Dog on University Place, a few minutes northeast of the park, runs happy hour every day, with house wine, margaritas, spritzes and bar bites, which makes it an easy pick for a weekend visit.

Most of these places post a booking link on their cards. For a department gathering, book ahead and ask whether the happy hour applies at your table, since several deals near the park are bar only.

Think of the park as the center of four small clusters. Just east, on Waverly Place, White Oak Tavern and Josie Woods Pub sit a few doors apart near the 8th Street-NYU station on the R and W. North, along West 8th Street, are the wine bars, close to the West 4th Street station. South, West 3rd Street and Bleecker Street hold Amity Hall and The Red Lion, the sports and music end of the neighborhood.

West of Sixth Avenue, Cornelia Street has Little Havana and West 4th Street has The Spaniard, both near Christopher Street-Stonewall on the 1. Southeast of the park, on the Bowery, Phebes is close to the Bleecker Street station. Below Houston Street, SoHo adds Cómodo, and on Sixth Avenue the West Village adds Cha Cha Tang, both with weekday happy hours within about seven minutes of the park.

If you want a longer night, the West Village bar crawl starts about ten minutes west of the park. On weekends, when most of these windows are off, The Grey Dog and the West 8th Street wine bars still run daily.

faq.a: 21. New York law bars the sale of alcohol to anyone under 21, and the State Liquor Authority holds bars responsible even if a customer looked older or lied about their age.
faq.q: What is the drinking age in New York?

faq.a: No. The State Liquor Authority does not accept a college ID as primary proof of age. Bring a driver's license, a non-driver state ID, a U.S. military ID or a passport. A college ID can only back one of those up.
faq.q: Is an NYU ID enough to get served?

faq.a: Amity Hall on West 3rd Street, about two minutes from the middle of the park. White Oak Tavern and Josie Woods Pub on Waverly Place are next, at three to four minutes.
faq.q: What is the closest happy hour to Washington Square Park?

faq.a: Phebes on the Bowery has beers and Guinness and Stella drafts on its weekday happy hour. The Red Lion pours its house draft and The Spaniard discounts all drafts. Check the live prices on each card.
faq.q: Where can I find cheap beer near NYU?

faq.a: Yes. The Grey Dog on University Place runs every day, and 8th Street Winecellar, Amelie Wine Bar and Pepe Rosso also list daily happy hours.
faq.q: Are there happy hours near NYU on weekends?

faq.a: For a full meal, Little Havana's Cuban sandwich and nachos and The Spaniard's smash burger with fries are the most filling options on this list.
faq.q: Which happy hours near NYU are good for food?

table_title: Every happy hour near Washington Square Park
method: We measured straight-line distances from the center of Washington Square Park to every bar in our New York happy hour database and kept those within about 900 meters, converting to walking minutes at about 80 meters per minute. Schedules, items and subway details come from each bar's own website, last checked September 2 and 3, 2026. Drinking age and ID rules come from the New York State Liquor Authority.

title: East Village Bar Crawl: 5 Weekday Happy Hour Stops
h1: East Village bar crawl: five happy hours, one short walk
description: An East Village bar crawl built on weekday happy hours that overlap: five stops from Emmy Squared to Kingston Hall, each a few minutes apart on foot.
answer: For an East Village bar crawl, go on a weekday and walk five stops in this order: Emmy Squared on 1st Avenue, Ruffian and Niagara on East 7th Street, Westville East on Avenue A, and Kingston Hall on 2nd Avenue. All five run a happy hour Monday through Friday, the deals overlap in the late afternoon, and no leg is longer than about six minutes on foot.
intro:
A bar crawl works when the stops are close and the deals line up at the same time. This route does both. Five East Village bars and restaurants sit along 1st Avenue, East 7th Street, Avenue A and 2nd Avenue, and the whole walk is about a kilometer, measured door to door in straight lines.

Every stop runs its happy hour Monday through Friday, and all five are on together in the late afternoon, so any weekday works. The order follows the clock as much as the map: the deals that end first come first, and the one that runs latest closes the night. You get a food stop, a wine bar, a beer bar, a cocktail stop, and a two-for-one finish.

Each card below shows live prices and today's hours. The table under this intro lists more happy hours within a short walk of the first stop, in case you want to swap one out.

picks.why: Start at Emmy Squared, a pizza, burger and salad restaurant at 83 1st Avenue. Its weekday happy hour opens first on the route and covers house wine, well cocktails, beer and sriracha glazed chicken wings, so this is where you put some food down before the night. The F at 2nd Avenue is five minutes away, and Resy takes bookings if your group wants a table.

Ruffian, a wine-focused bar at 125 E 7th St, is about three minutes from Emmy Squared. Its weekday happy hour takes a discount off everything, with separate discounts on wine and on food. It also has one of the shortest windows of the five, so it goes second, while the deal is still on. No booking link is listed, so walk in.

Niagara, at 112 Avenue A, is the beer stop and barely a minute from Ruffian, at the Avenue A end of the block. Its happy hour starts when the doors open, seven days a week, and covers draft beer, house wine and well drinks until early evening. Order a draft, slow the pace a little, then head north up Avenue A.

About four minutes north, Westville East at 173 Avenue A is a restaurant with a weekday happy hour that covers cocktails, wine and beer. Its deal ends at the same time as Ruffian's, so do not linger at Niagara. The L at 1st Avenue is three minutes away if someone has to leave early.

Finish at Kingston Hall, 149 2nd Avenue, about six minutes west of Westville East. Its happy hour runs Monday through Saturday, with a separate Sunday window, and it stays on later than any other stop here. The deal is two-for-one on beer, prosecco and well drinks, so pair up and split rounds. Astor Place on the 6 is four minutes away for the ride home.

sections.body:
Pick a weekday. Emmy Squared, Ruffian, Niagara, Westville East and Kingston Hall all run a happy hour Monday through Friday, and all five are on at the same time in the late afternoon. That shared stretch is your crawl.

Emmy Squared's window opens an hour before Ruffian's, so time your first round there to land you at Ruffian right as its deal starts. Ruffian has one of the shortest windows, and Emmy Squared's ends at the same moment, which is why they lead the route. Westville East ends then too, so keep the Niagara round short and reach Westville East before its deal closes. After that the pressure is off: Kingston Hall keeps its deal going well into the evening. Plan on one round, roughly 40 minutes, per stop and you finish with time to spare. Check the cards on the day, because bars do change hours.

On a Saturday or Sunday, Emmy Squared, Ruffian and Westville East drop out. A shorter weekend version still works: Niagara, then Smør at 441 East 12th Street (about a minute from Westville East, with house wines and cocktails every day), then Kingston Hall, whose Sunday window starts earlier than its weekday one.

Leg one, Emmy Squared to Ruffian: about 220 meters, three minutes. Walk up 1st Avenue and turn east onto East 7th Street. Leg two, Ruffian to Niagara: about 80 meters, one minute, to the Avenue A end of the same block. Leg three, Niagara to Westville East: about 300 meters, four minutes, straight up Avenue A. Leg four, Westville East to Kingston Hall: about 460 meters, six minutes, west and a little north to 2nd Avenue.

That adds up to roughly 1,060 meters and 14 minutes of walking. These are straight-line distances, so the real walk on the street grid runs a little longer, but it stays well under the time you spend at any one bar.

Want an earlier, longer day? Hair Of The Dog at 168 Orchard Street in the Lower East Side runs a weekday happy hour on all drinks, plus a slider deal, starting early in the day. It is about a seven-minute walk south of Emmy Squared, so it slots in as a stop zero.

Coming in, the F to 2nd Avenue leaves you five minutes from Emmy Squared, the natural first stop. The L at 1st Avenue is the other good arrival point: Westville East is three minutes from it, and Ruffian and Niagara are about seven.

Going home, Kingston Hall is four minutes from Astor Place on the 6. If you are headed for the L instead, peel off after Westville East, three minutes from 1st Avenue station. The same L line also stops at Bedford Avenue in Williamsburg, where our Williamsburg bar crawl begins, if you want to compare the two neighborhoods on another night.

sections.h: Small things that make the crawl better
sections.body:
Eat in the first hour. Emmy Squared's wings and Ruffian's food discount come early, which is when you need them; the last three happy hours list drinks only.

Only Emmy Squared lists a booking link, so the other four are first come. A group of two to four moves through bars like these far more easily than a big party. Kingston Hall's two-for-one rewards pairs, so plan your last round with a friend.

faq.a: Any weekday. All five stops on this route run a happy hour Monday through Friday, and they overlap in the late afternoon. On weekends, Emmy Squared, Ruffian and Westville East have no happy hour, so use the shorter Niagara, Smør and Kingston Hall version.
faq.q: What day should I do an East Village bar crawl?

faq.a: About 1,060 meters in straight lines between the five stops, or roughly 14 minutes of walking in total. No single leg is longer than about six minutes.
faq.q: How long is the walk?

faq.a: Emmy Squared's happy hour includes sriracha glazed chicken wings, and Ruffian discounts its food. Both come early in the route. Niagara, Westville East and Kingston Hall list drinks only in their happy hours.
faq.q: Where can I eat on this crawl?

faq.a: Emmy Squared takes bookings through Resy. Ruffian, Niagara, Westville East and Kingston Hall have no booking link listed, so plan to walk in.
faq.q: Do I need reservations?

faq.a: Arrive on the F at 2nd Avenue, five minutes from Emmy Squared, or on the L at 1st Avenue. Leave from Astor Place on the 6, four minutes from Kingston Hall.
faq.q: Which subway should I take?

table_title: More happy hours within a short walk
method: Stops, deals, days, addresses, booking links and subway walking times come from each bar's own website as recorded in our database, with happy hours last checked on September 2, 2026. Walking times are straight-line distances between each bar's map coordinates at about 80 meters a minute, so real walks run slightly longer. The L line stops come from the MTA's L line map.

title: What Time Do Bars Close in NYC? 4 a.m. Last Call, Explained
h1: What Time Do Bars Close in NYC? The 4 a.m. Rule, Explained
keyword: what time do bars close in nyc
description: What time do bars close in NYC? Legally at 4 a.m. in all five boroughs. Here is how last call works, Sunday hours, ID rules and late happy hours.
answer: What time do bars close in NYC? Legally, 4 a.m., every night, in all five boroughs, and you get half an hour after that to finish your drink. Sales can start again at 8 a.m., or 10 a.m. on Sunday. Plenty of bars close earlier by choice, so for a deal after dark try Barfly in Gramercy or Meller's Sports Hub & Grill on the Upper East Side, which run happy hour late into the night early in the week.
intro:
New York bars can legally serve late, and the rule is the same in Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx and Staten Island. The State Liquor Authority lists the hours county by county, and all five New York City counties match: bars, taverns and restaurants can serve until 4 a.m. Saturday night is no exception, because the Sunday rule only changes when serving can start again in the morning.

The legal limit is a ceiling, not a promise, and your local may lock up long before it on a Tuesday. Below: what the law says, how last call works, why many places close early, what ID to carry, and where to find late happy hours. The six picks are bars on our list with a happy hour that ends late in the evening or after midnight, spread across Manhattan, Brooklyn and Queens.

picks.why: Barfly is a Gramercy sports bar on Third Avenue that saves its happy hour for the late shift. Sunday through Thursday the deal starts after dinner and runs to the legal close, with Coors and Miller High Life plus beer-and-shot combos with Jameson or Skrewball, and a spicy margarita too. It suits a weeknight game or a nightcap after work. The 6 at 23rd Street-Baruch College is a five-minute walk.

Meller's Sports Hub & Grill on Second Avenue starts its happy hour late in the evening. Sunday through Thursday it runs past midnight, covering canned beer, hard seltzer and cider, wine, frozen drinks and mixed drinks, with margaritas and Aperol spritzes on the list. The Q at 86th Street is a two-minute walk, which makes the ride home easy.

Soho Diner is the food answer to a late night out. Its happy hour runs only on Friday and Saturday, and only after midnight, with a short list of plates: hot wings, crispy cheese curds, black-eyed pea hummus with flatbread, zucchini chips and a smash burger. It sits a minute from the Canal Street A, C and E station, so you can eat and catch the train in one stop.

The Rosemont on Montrose Avenue runs happy hour every day, from late afternoon on weekdays and earlier on weekends, and it keeps going into the evening. The list covers classic cocktails such as an Old Fashioned, Negroni, Sazerac and Daiquiri, plus well drinks, draft beer and wine. The G at Broadway is a three-minute walk.

Bar LunAtico on Halsey Street in Bed-Stuy posts a happy hour menu that runs every night of the week, from early evening deep into the night. It leans on small plates such as Spanish olives, house focaccia with tapenade and gigante beans, with vegan and gluten-free options marked. Utica Avenue on the A and C is a seven-minute walk.

American Brass is a Long Island City brasserie that serves its happy hour menu at the bar every day, and Friday and Saturday run the latest, well into the evening. The menu includes starters such as sourdough focaccia with whipped ricotta and crispy calamari, and our list tags it for cocktails and wine. Vernon Boulevard-Jackson Avenue on the 7 is a five-minute walk.

sections.body:
Closing time is set by law. Last call is set by the bar. State law bars on-premises sales between 4 a.m. and 8 a.m. Monday through Saturday, and until 10 a.m. on Sunday, according to the State Liquor Authority's pages for New York, Kings, Queens, Bronx and Richmond counties. The same law adds a grace period: nobody may drink on the premises later than half an hour after the cutoff.

Last call is the warning that comes before all that. Bartenders call it ahead of their own closing time so they can clear glasses, settle tabs and get people out on time. Some bars ring a bell, some flip the lights. If you want one more round, order it when you hear the call, not after the music stops.

The 4 a.m. limit is the latest a bar may serve, not the time it has to stay open. Each bar picks its own hours inside that window, and on a weeknight in a residential block that often means closing well before the legal limit. Kitchens can stop earlier than the bar, so if food matters, ask before you settle in. The State Liquor Authority can also set tighter hours for an individual license, so two bars on the same street can keep different schedules. The practical move is simple: look at the posted hours for the night you are going, not a general rule. Hours often differ from one night of the week to the next, and our happy hour now page shows which deals are running at the moment you open it.

You must be 21 to buy or be served alcohol in New York, and bars take it seriously because the license holder is on the hook even if a guest looked older or lied. Under state law, accepted proof of age is a valid driver's license or non-driver ID issued by a government, a valid passport, or a U.S. armed forces ID. College IDs do not count as the main proof, and an expired card can be turned away.

For visitors from outside the U.S., the passport is the safe choice, because the list covers driver's licenses from U.S. states and territories and Canadian provinces but not from other countries. New York's Mobile ID is also accepted. Expect to be carded at busy spots, whatever your age.

A happy hour after dark usually means a reverse happy hour: a second, shorter window after the dinner rush. On our list, 23 bars have a window that ends late in the evening or after midnight, and none of them are in the Bronx or Staten Island yet. After-midnight deals lean toward the start of the week: Barfly and Meller's run Sunday through Thursday, while Soho Diner saves its deal for Friday and Saturday. Our late-night happy hours page keeps the full list current, and the reverse happy hour guide covers the second-window idea in more depth. If you would rather dance than sit at a bar, our NYC parties list collects club nights and events with the venue and date for each. Check each party's ticket listing for end times. The same 4 a.m. rule applies to alcohol at licensed venues, even when the music keeps going.

The subway runs 24 hours a day, every day of the year, which is a big part of why a 4 a.m. closing works here. Not every route runs overnight, though, and late-night trains come less often, so check the MTA app or station signs before you rely on a specific line. Pay your tab before last call so you are not stuck in the closing rush.

faq.a: Yes. The legal cutoff for on-premises sales is 4 a.m. every day of the week in all five boroughs. Saturday night runs to 4 a.m. Sunday morning. The Sunday rule only means sales cannot restart until 10 a.m., instead of 8 a.m. on other days.
faq.q: Do NYC bars close at 4 a.m. on weekends too?

faq.a: At 10 a.m., according to the State Liquor Authority's county pages for New York City. Monday through Saturday, on-premises sales can start at 8 a.m. Many bars open much later.
faq.q: What time can bars start serving on Sunday in New York City?

faq.a: State law says nobody may drink on a licensed premises later than half an hour after sales must stop. At a bar open to the legal limit, that means roughly half an hour after 4 a.m.
faq.q: How long do I have to finish my drink after closing?

faq.a: Yes. The State Liquor Authority lists the same on-premises hours for all five New York City counties: New York (Manhattan), Kings (Brooklyn), Queens, Bronx and Richmond (Staten Island).
faq.q: Is closing time the same in Manhattan, Brooklyn and Queens?

faq.a: Bring your passport. State law accepts a valid passport, a U.S. armed forces ID, or a valid driver's license or non-driver ID from a U.S. state or territory or a Canadian province. A driver's license from another country is not on that list.
faq.q: What ID do tourists need to get into a bar in NYC?

faq.a: On our list, Barfly in Gramercy and Meller's Sports Hub & Grill on the Upper East Side run late Sunday through Thursday, and Soho Diner runs a food happy hour after midnight on Friday and Saturday. Lovers of Today in the East Village and Blue Haven in Kips Bay also run late early in the week.
faq.q: Which NYC bars have a happy hour after midnight?

table_title: Late-night happy hours in NYC
method: Legal hours come from the New York State Liquor Authority's county pages for all five New York City counties, the half-hour drinking rule from an SLA briefing document quoting the Alcoholic Beverage Control Law, ID rules from SLA guidance, and subway hours from the MTA rider guide, all checked October 16, 2026. Bar picks come from the 718 bars on our list: we kept those with a happy hour window ending late in the evening or after midnight (23 bars) and picked six across three boroughs. Deals come from each bar's own website, checked between September 2 and October 15, 2026.

title: Village Halloween Parade 2026: Where to Drink Nearby
h1: Village Halloween Parade 2026: bars near the route, before and after
description: Village Halloween Parade 2026 on Sixth Avenue, Saturday Oct 31: start time, route, how to march, and 6 bars with Saturday happy hours near the route.
answer: The Village Halloween Parade 2026 steps off at 7 p.m. on Saturday, October 31, and heads north up Sixth Avenue to West 15th Street, according to the organizers. Before it, 8th Street Winecellar, L'accolade on Bleecker Street and Left Bank on Perry Street run Saturday happy hours a few minutes from the route. After it, Bobo on West 10th Street has the only late Saturday happy hour near Sixth Avenue on our list.
intro: Halloween lands on a Saturday this year, which means the Village Halloween Parade gets a weekend crowd on top of its usual one. The 2026 theme is Body & Soul, and the organizers name Joey Arias as Grand Marshal. It moves up Sixth Avenue through Greenwich Village from early evening until late, and the blocks on either side fill up fast. That makes the drinks plan more important than usual. Happy hours near the route mostly run in the afternoon and early evening on Saturdays, so the smart move is to drink early, eat something, and claim a spot on the avenue before the parade reaches you. We checked every bar on our list within about 700 meters of Sixth Avenue and West 8th Street: 38 have a happy hour, and 13 of those run one on Saturday. The six picks below are the ones with published deals and the clearest fit for parade day, plus one for after. If you want to keep going once the last float passes, our Halloween parties list has the club nights and costume parties across the city, and the Halloween weekend guide covers all four nights from Thursday to Sunday.

picks.why: A restaurant at 302 Bleecker Street, about four minutes west of Sixth Avenue at West 4th Street. It runs a separate Saturday happy hour in the afternoon that starts earlier than most Saturday windows nearby, with wine by the glass, cocktails, selected martinis and oysters by the dozen or half dozen until they run out. Book on Resy if you want a table before the crowds build. Christopher Street-Stonewall on the 1 is two minutes away.

Left Bank on Perry Street is the sit-down dinner stop, about eight minutes west of Sixth Avenue. Its weekend happy hour, Saturday included, runs in the late afternoon and pairs food with drinks: any two apps, a burger with a beer, or pasta with a glass of wine, plus draught beer, wine by the glass, margaritas and martinis. Eat here, then walk east to the avenue. Reservations are on Resy.

A wine bar on West 8th Street, about two minutes east of Sixth Avenue and close to the middle of the route. Happy hour runs every day, Saturday included, until the evening, with select glasses and select bottles of wine on the deal. Its oyster happy hour is Monday to Thursday only, so it will not apply on parade night. West 4th Street-Washington Square (A, B, C, D, E, F, M) is a four-minute walk.

An all-day American spot on University Place, about six minutes east of Sixth Avenue at West 11th Street. Happy hour runs every day in the late afternoon, so it works as an early stop on a Saturday. The list covers a house lager, house wine, a Tommy's margarita, a mule and a Venetian spritz, plus bar bites such as fried cheese, wings and spinach and artichoke dip. Union Square station is three minutes away.

A New American bar on Greenwich Avenue, about six minutes from Sixth Avenue at 14th Street, near the north end of the route. Happy hour runs every day from late afternoon into the early evening, at the bar and on the patio only. The sunset menu includes oysters, a Caesar salad and a popover French dip. If you plan to watch near 14th Street, this is the pick closest to that end.

A French bar and restaurant on West 10th Street, about four minutes from Sixth Avenue at West 8th Street, and the pick for after the parade. Its Friday and Saturday happy hour runs late at night in the den, with martinis: classic gin or vodka, an espresso version and a French martini. The bar also lists a daily early-evening apero in the den with oysters and wine. Christopher Street-Stonewall is one minute away.

sections.body:
Date and time: Saturday, October 31, 2026, starting at 7 p.m. The organizers' watch page says it ends around 11 p.m., so plan on about four hours of parade moving north past you. Spectrum News NY1 carries it live from 8 p.m. if you would rather watch from a bar stool.

Route: the parade runs north on Sixth Avenue to West 15th Street. The organizers describe the start two ways: their watch page says the viewing stretch runs from King Street to West 15th Street, while the march page and press page put the line-up at the south end, around Canal Street and Sixth Avenue. Either way, the part you can stand along is Sixth Avenue from about King Street up to 15th Street.

The opening act is a new puppet piece called Firehorse, and the theme, Body & Soul, is the prompt for costumes if you want to match it.

Anyone in costume can march. Only costumed people are let into the line-up, which opens at 6:30 p.m. and stays open until 9 p.m. on October 31. The organizers' press page puts it on Sixth Avenue between Spring Street and Broome Street and asks marchers to come in from the east or south. If you approach from the west, enter from Canal Street. No costume, no entry, so plan the outfit before the drinks.

To watch, stand on either side of Sixth Avenue anywhere between King Street and West 15th Street. The organizers warn that the blocks from Bleecker Street to 14th Street are the most crowded, so arrive early if you want a front spot there, or walk south of Bleecker for more room. The parade takes time to travel north, so the farther up the avenue you stand, the later it reaches you.

A simple plan: happy hour in the late afternoon, food by early evening, then on the avenue by the time the parade starts. Bars near Sixth Avenue fill up after the first floats pass, and you will lose your viewing spot if you leave it.

sections.h: Timing your drinks around the parade
sections.body: Saturday is a weaker happy hour day than a weeknight. Of the 38 bars on our list within about 700 meters of Sixth Avenue and West 8th Street, only 13 run a Saturday window, and all but one end by the early evening. That lines up well with the parade: drink before 7 p.m., then move. For the early slot, start at L'accolade on Bleecker Street, whose Saturday deal begins in the afternoon, or at The Grey Dog on University Place. Left Bank and 8th Street Winecellar keep going into the evening, and Jack & Charlie's No. 118 runs until the early evening on Greenwich Avenue, near the north end. After the parade, Bobo is the one pick with a late Saturday window, in its den, and it overlaps the parade's last hour. Everything else will be full price by then. Happy hour times on a holiday night are the bar's call, not ours. Check each pick card on the day, and see what time bars close in NYC if you plan to stay out late.

The organizers advise against driving. For marchers, they name the Spring Street station on the Eighth Avenue line as the closest stop to the line-up. For spectators, the picks above sit near West 4th Street-Washington Square (A, B, C, D, E, F, M), Christopher Street-Stonewall (1) and Union Square, according to their listings.

Expect crowds on every platform near the route after the parade ends. Walking a few blocks east or west of Sixth Avenue before you look for a train, or toward Union Square, usually beats waiting at the nearest entrance.

We could not confirm street closures, crossing points or any subway service changes for parade night from an official source, so we have left them out. Check the organizers' site and the MTA before you go. The organizers' pages also describe the start of the route slightly differently, King Street on one page and Canal Street on others, so treat the southern end as approximate. Bar happy hours come from each bar's own published schedule and may change on Halloween.

faq.a: It starts at 7 p.m. on Saturday, October 31, 2026, according to the organizers, and ends around 11 p.m. Spectrum News NY1 broadcasts it live from 8 p.m.
faq.q: What time does the Village Halloween Parade 2026 start?

faq.a: North on Sixth Avenue to West 15th Street. The organizers say you can watch from either side of the avenue between King Street and West 15th Street, and that Bleecker to 14th Street is the most crowded stretch.
faq.q: Where does the parade go?

faq.a: Yes, if you are in costume. The line-up runs from 6:30 p.m. to 9 p.m. on Sixth Avenue near Canal Street, between Spring and Broome Streets per the press page. Only people in costume are let in.
faq.q: Can I march in the Village Halloween Parade?

faq.a: On our list, 13 bars within about 700 meters of Sixth Avenue and West 8th Street run one on Saturday, including L'accolade, Left Bank, 8th Street Winecellar, The Grey Dog on University Place and Jack & Charlie's No. 118. Most end by the early evening.
faq.q: Which bars near the route have a happy hour on Saturday?

faq.a: Bobo on West 10th Street is the only bar near the route on our list with a late Saturday happy hour. It runs in the den and overlaps the last part of the parade.
faq.q: Is there a happy hour after the parade?

faq.a: Body & Soul. The organizers also name Joey Arias as the 2026 Grand Marshal and open the parade with a new puppet piece, Firehorse.
faq.q: What is the 2026 parade theme?

table_title: Happy hours within about nine minutes of Sixth Avenue and West 8th Street
method: Parade date, start time, route, line-up rules, viewing advice and broadcast details come from the organizers' site, halloween-nyc.com (home, march, watch, press and theme pages), checked October 23, 2026. Bars come from our database of New York happy hours, which records each bar's schedule and offers from its own website. We measured straight-line distance from each bar to Sixth Avenue at about 80 meters a minute and counted bars within 700 meters of Sixth Avenue and West 8th Street. The six picks were last checked between September 2 and October 23, 2026; Bobo's listing is the oldest, from September 2.

title: Hells Kitchen Bar Crawl: 5 Happy Hour Stops, 42nd to 50th
h1: Hells Kitchen bar crawl: five happy hours from 42nd Street to 50th
description: A Hells Kitchen bar crawl for Tuesday to Friday: five happy hours off Ninth Avenue, about nine minutes of walking, with pre-show and late options.
answer: For a Hells Kitchen bar crawl that stays on happy hour, go Tuesday through Friday and walk north: West Bank Cafe on West 42nd Street, The Brazen Tavern on West 44th, Lady Blue on West 46th, The Molly Pitcher Club on Ninth Avenue and Boxers HK at Ninth and 50th. The five stops add up to about 690 meters of walking, and the windows that run latest sit at the north end.
intro:
Hell's Kitchen is one of the easiest places in the city to string happy hours together. Our list has 32 bars in the neighborhood, and 29 of them run a happy hour on every day from Tuesday to Friday. The hard part is not finding a deal. It is picking five that hand off cleanly, so you are never walking into a bar just as its window closes.

This route does that. It starts on West 42nd Street at a bar with an all-day happy hour, climbs through the side streets just east of Ninth Avenue, and ends on Ninth near 50th Street at the bar whose window runs longest. Along the way you get a food stop, an oyster and cocktail stop, a short and simple drinks list, and a sports bar to finish.

The pick cards below show live prices and each bar's current hours. Use this guide for the order, the days and the walk, and check the cards on the day you go.

picks.why: Start at West Bank Cafe, 407 West 42nd Street, where the happy hour runs all day, every day, at the bar only. That makes it the flexible first stop: come early or late. The bar list covers tap beer, prosecco, merlot, pinot grigio, white wine sangria and a Peach Pony Club, and the bites run from risotto balls and deviled eggs to meatball sliders, calamari and a cheeseburger with fries. The 42nd Street-Port Authority station is four minutes away.

Two minutes north, The Brazen Tavern at 356 West 44th Street is an Irish and American pub whose weekday happy hour is all about food. The Monday to Friday menu lists housemade chicken fingers with honey mustard, classic hummus with pita and vegetables, glazed wings in five sauces, boneless wings and mango habanero cauliflower bites. Eat here so the rest of the route goes easier. The window opens in mid-afternoon and runs into the early evening.

Lady Blue, a cocktail bar at 363 West 46th Street, is about two minutes further. Its weekday happy hour pairs a dozen oysters with a bottle of bubbly, takes a little off select small plates, and sets prices on a limoncello lemon drop martini, a house margarita, a classic old fashioned, draft beer and wine. It ends at the same time as The Brazen Tavern's window, so keep the first two stops short. It also runs a second happy hour late every night.

The Molly Pitcher Club sits at 675 Ninth Avenue, about a minute from Lady Blue. Its happy hour runs Tuesday through Friday and starts later than the first three, in the early evening, which is why it comes fourth. The list is short and easy: wine, well drinks, canned beer and Harpoon American Flyer Lager. This is the stop that sets the route's days, because it has no Monday happy hour.

Finish three minutes north at Boxers HK, 742 Ninth Avenue, which calls itself Hell's Kitchen's go-to gay sports bar. Its weekday happy hour lasts the longest of the five, well into the evening, with beer, wine, well drinks and call drinks on the list. LED screens show the games and RuPaul's Drag Race, there is beer on tap and pizza, and the 50th Street station on the C and E is four minutes away.

sections.body:
Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. Those are the only days when all five stops run a happy hour. West Bank Cafe runs every day, and The Brazen Tavern, Lady Blue and Boxers HK all run Monday to Friday, but The Molly Pitcher Club starts its week on Tuesday.

On a Monday, swap The Molly Pitcher Club for VERS at 714 Ninth Avenue, which sits between it and Boxers HK and runs a happy hour every day into the early evening. Its list has a martini and a margarita at a set price, two-for-one well drinks and discounted appetizers. The route stays the same length.

On a weekend the route does not work as written, since The Brazen Tavern, Boxers HK and The Molly Pitcher Club have no Saturday or Sunday window, and Lady Blue's afternoon deal is weekdays only. For a Saturday, build it from West Bank Cafe, Friki Tiki on West 44th Street (Tuesday to Sunday, with a Zombie, a frozen paloma, a Hugo spritz, wine, beer and buckets), VERS, and then Lady Blue's late-night window.

sections.h: Before a show, and after it
sections.body: If you have theater tickets, do a short version. West Bank Cafe's bar happy hour runs all day, and The Brazen Tavern and Lady Blue run theirs from mid-afternoon into the early evening, so the first three stops fit before an evening show. Check the curtain time on your ticket and leave yourself time to walk. Our guide to pre-theater drinks near Times Square covers more bars closer to the theaters. After the show, Lady Blue is the stop to come back to. Its late-night happy hour runs every night of the week, starting late in the evening from Sunday to Thursday and an hour later on Friday and Saturday, with a Negroni, a Moscow Mule, a Manhattan and a margarita on the list. West Bank Cafe's all-day bar deal is the other option once the curtain comes down.

West Bank Cafe to The Brazen Tavern is about 165 meters, a two-minute walk north. From there Lady Blue is about 185 meters away, roughly two and a half minutes. The Molly Pitcher Club is the shortest leg, about 80 meters, or one minute. The last leg to Boxers HK is about 260 meters, a little over three minutes.

In total that is about 690 meters, or about nine minutes on your feet. We measure straight lines between each bar's coordinates at about 80 meters a minute, so add a minute here and there for avenue crossings.

Plan on one round and about half an hour at each stop. The order follows the clock: West Bank Cafe never closes its window, The Brazen Tavern and Lady Blue end together, and The Molly Pitcher Club and Boxers HK run later. If you start late, skip straight to Lady Blue. For more options nearby, the table below lists every happy hour within 500 meters of Lady Blue, closest first. There are 22 of them.

The route starts near the 42nd Street-Port Authority Bus Terminal station, which our listing puts four minutes from West Bank Cafe and which serves the 1, 2, 3, 7, A, C, E, N, Q, R, S and W lines. The Brazen Tavern is three minutes from the same station.

It ends near the 50th Street station on the C and E, four minutes from Boxers HK and five from Lady Blue and The Molly Pitcher Club. You never need to double back.

faq.a: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday. Those are the only days when all five stops on this route run happy hour. On a Monday, swap The Molly Pitcher Club for VERS on Ninth Avenue, which runs a happy hour every day.
faq.q: Which day should I do a Hell's Kitchen bar crawl?

faq.a: About three hours. The walking adds up to about 690 meters, or nine minutes, and with one round and half an hour at each of the five bars you will start in the afternoon and finish in the evening.
faq.q: How long does the crawl take?

faq.a: Yes, if you keep it to the first two or three stops. West Bank Cafe runs its bar happy hour all day, and The Brazen Tavern and Lady Blue run theirs from mid-afternoon into the early evening. Check your curtain time and leave time to walk.
faq.q: Can I do this crawl before a Broadway show?

faq.a: Yes. Lady Blue on West 46th Street runs a late-night happy hour every night, starting an hour later on Friday and Saturday, and West Bank Cafe's bar happy hour runs all day.
faq.q: Is there a happy hour after the show in Hell's Kitchen?

faq.a: No. West Bank Cafe's deal is at the bar, so walk in and take a bar seat. West Bank Cafe does list a Resy link if you want a table for dinner afterward.
faq.q: Do I need reservations?

faq.a: Start at 42nd Street-Port Authority Bus Terminal, four minutes from West Bank Cafe. Finish at 50th Street on the C and E, four minutes from Boxers HK.
faq.q: Which subway stations are closest to the start and end?

The five stops were last checked between October 16 and October 23, 2026. title: Park Slope Bar Crawl: 4 Weekday Happy Hours on Fifth Avenue
h1: Park Slope bar crawl: four happy hours on Fifth Avenue
description: A Park Slope bar crawl for Monday to Friday: four happy hours on Fifth Avenue, from pizza and cocktails to a dive bar finish near the R at Union Street.
answer: For a Park Slope bar crawl, go Monday through Friday and stay on Fifth Avenue: start at Emmy Squared Pizza, walk north to Blueprint and 200 Fifth, then finish a block back south at High Dive. All four weekday happy hours overlap in the late afternoon, the walking adds up to about 730 meters, and the R at Union Street is three to six minutes from every stop.
intro:
Park Slope is a weekday happy hour neighborhood. Of the 22 Park Slope bars and restaurants on our list, nine run a happy hour on every day from Monday to Friday, and only two run one on Saturday. So this crawl is built for a weeknight, and it keeps to one street: Fifth Avenue, between the blocks north of Union Street and the blocks south of it.

Four stops is the right size here. The bars with deals on the same days cluster tightly on Fifth, so a fifth stop would mean a long detour for little gain. The four below go from a pizza place with wings, to a cocktail bar, to a bar with draft beer and champagne on its list, to a dive bar that keeps its deal going latest.

The order has one quirk: you walk past the last stop on the way to the second. That is on purpose. The pick cards below show live prices and hours, and the sections explain the timing and the walk.

picks.why: Start at Emmy Squared Pizza, 315 Fifth Avenue, a pizza, burger and salad restaurant whose happy hour runs Monday to Friday from mid-afternoon. It opens earliest of the four and closes at the same time as Blueprint's, so come here first and eat. The list covers select beer, house wine and well cocktails, plus sriracha glazed chicken wings, boneless or bone-in, for the table. The Union Street R station is six minutes away.

Walk about six minutes north to Blueprint at 196 Fifth Avenue, the cocktail stop. Its weekday happy hour starts an hour after Emmy Squared's and is the shortest window of the four, so do not linger at the first stop. House cocktails include the Kickstarter, with Gosling's rum and espresso, the Parks and Leisure, with vodka, Aperol and grapefruit, and the Smoky Mary's, with chipotle-infused tequila. Food, wine and beer are on the happy hour menu too.

200 Fifth is a few steps south of Blueprint, close enough that you barely need a coat. Its weekday happy hour starts with Blueprint's but runs an hour longer, so this is the stop to settle into. The deal covers draft beer, bar drinks, house wine and champagne. It takes OpenTable bookings if you are bringing a group and want a table, and the R at Union Street is three minutes away.

Finish at High Dive, 243 Fifth Avenue, about three minutes back south. You passed it on the way to Blueprint; it comes last because its window runs latest of the four, into the evening. Our listing tags it as a dive bar, and the happy hour is simple: PBR and well drinks at set prices and a discount on everything else. It runs Monday to Friday, and the Union Street R is four minutes away.

sections.body:
Monday through Friday. All four stops run their happy hour on every weekday and none of them run one on Saturday or Sunday, so this is a weeknight crawl only.

From Monday to Thursday you can add a fifth stop. The Commissioner, a pub at 247 Fifth Avenue, sits right next to High Dive and runs a happy hour until the early evening, with a discount on all drafts and set prices on wine, well drinks and a beer and a shot. Its window ends early, so visit it on the walk north, between Emmy Squared and Blueprint, rather than at the end.

On a weekend, the options are thin. Only two Park Slope bars on our list run a Saturday happy hour: Bar Louise on Seventh Avenue, with an oyster happy hour that adds martinis when you order oysters, and Siren, further south on Fifth Avenue, with oysters, littleneck clams and cocktails from Friday to Sunday. On Sundays, Whisk and Whiskey on Fourth Avenue runs its happy hour all day, and 390 Social and Chela on Fifth Avenue have Sunday windows.

The order follows the clock. Emmy Squared opens its window first, in mid-afternoon, and Blueprint opens an hour later. Both end at the same time, which is why you go to Emmy Squared first and keep it to one round. Blueprint has the shortest window on the route, so arrive soon after it starts.

200 Fifth starts with Blueprint and runs an hour longer, and High Dive, which started earliest of all, runs latest. That is why High Dive closes the night even though it sits between the first and second stops. If you arrive after work and miss the first window, start at Blueprint and do the last three.

Plan on about half an hour per stop and roughly two and a half hours in total. The exact start and end times are on each pick card, and they are worth checking before you head out.

Emmy Squared Pizza to Blueprint is the long leg, about 500 meters north on Fifth Avenue, or six minutes. Blueprint to 200 Fifth is about 15 meters, a matter of seconds. The last leg, back south to High Dive, is about 215 meters, close to three minutes.

That makes about 730 meters of walking in total, roughly nine minutes on your feet. We measure straight lines between each bar's coordinates at about 80 meters per minute, so allow a little extra for crossings.

Everything sits on one avenue, so you never have to look for a side street. If you want more choices along the way, the table below lists every happy hour within 800 meters of High Dive, closest first. There are 15.

The Union Street station on the R is the anchor. Our listings put it three minutes from Blueprint and 200 Fifth, four minutes from High Dive and six minutes from Emmy Squared, so you can arrive and leave from the same station. If you start at Emmy Squared, walking south from Union Street to it and then back north along the route works fine.

The 9th Street station on the F, G and R is the other option for the southern end of Fifth Avenue, closer to 390 Social and Chela if you extend the night.

faq.a: Any weekday, Monday through Friday. All four stops run a happy hour on every weekday and none of them on weekends. Monday to Thursday you can add The Commissioner next to High Dive as a fifth stop.
faq.q: Which day should I do a Park Slope bar crawl?

faq.a: About two and a half hours. The walking adds up to about 730 meters, roughly nine minutes, and with one round and half an hour at each of the four bars you start in the afternoon and finish in the evening.
faq.q: How long does the crawl take?

faq.a: Not this one. On Saturday only Bar Louise and Siren run a happy hour among the Park Slope bars on our list. On Sunday, add Whisk and Whiskey, which runs its happy hour all day, plus 390 Social and Chela.
faq.q: Can I do a Park Slope bar crawl on a weekend?

faq.a: Union Street on the R. It is three to six minutes from every stop on the route, so you can start and finish at the same station.
faq.q: Which subway station is closest?

faq.a: Emmy Squared Pizza is the food stop, with sriracha glazed chicken wings on its happy hour list. Blueprint also has food on its happy hour menu.
faq.q: Where can I eat on the route?

faq.a: Yes. 200 Fifth takes OpenTable bookings, so reserve a table there for the middle of the night. The other stops work best for small groups that can share the bar.
faq.q: Is this crawl good for a group?

method: We built this route from our database of New York happy hours, which records each bar's days, windows and offers from the bar's own website. The four stops were last checked between October 17 and October 23, 2026. The counts (22 Park Slope bars, nine with a happy hour every weekday, two with a Saturday happy hour, and 15 within 800 meters of High Dive) come from the same database on October 23, 2026. title: Bushwick Bar Crawl: 5 Happy Hours From DeKalb to Wilson Ave
h1: Bushwick bar crawl: five happy hours, then a party
description: A Bushwick bar crawl for Tuesday to Friday: five happy hours with margaritas, a rooftop, oysters and tacos, ending a short walk from House of Yes.
answer: For a Bushwick bar crawl, go Tuesday through Friday and walk west: Gordo's Cantina on St Nicholas Avenue, Vacations Bar & Rooftop on Cypress Avenue, The Ten Bells on Irving Avenue, Mad Tropical on Troutman Street and The Little Whiskey on Wilson Avenue. It is about 1.6 kilometers of walking in total, and the last stop is about nine minutes on foot from House of Yes if you want to keep going.
intro:
Bushwick bars keep generous hours, and our list shows it: 13 of the 15 Bushwick bars we track run a happy hour on every day from Tuesday to Friday. The neighborhood is spread out, though, so a crawl here needs an order that follows the clock and the map at the same time.

This route starts near the DeKalb Avenue L stop, swings north to Cypress Avenue, then works west through the blocks around the Jefferson Street stop to Wilson Avenue, near Morgan Avenue. Five bars, five different deals: margaritas and micheladas, a rooftop with a discount on everything, oysters and tapas, tacos and cocktails, and cheap cans to finish.

Bushwick is also where many of the city's club nights happen, so the last section covers the parties on our list that fall on the same nights as the crawl. The pick cards below carry live prices and each bar's current hours.

picks.why: Start at Gordo's Cantina, 140 St Nicholas Avenue, two minutes from the DeKalb Avenue L. Its weekday happy hour opens in the middle of the day and runs into the early evening, the longest window on the route, so this is where to begin in the afternoon. The list is short: a lime margarita, a michelada, and a beer and a shot. Have one round, then walk north before the next window opens.

Vacations Bar & Rooftop, at 48 Cypress Avenue, is about six minutes away. Its happy hour runs Tuesday through Friday in a short window from late afternoon to early evening, and the deal is a flat discount on everything. That window is one reason the route skips Monday. Our listing tags it for a rooftop, so head upstairs if it is open. The Jefferson Street L stop is four minutes away.

Walk about six minutes southwest to The Ten Bells Brooklyn at 65 Irving Avenue, the oyster stop. Its happy hour runs every day until the early evening and ends at the same time as Vacations', so keep the first two stops brisk. The deal covers oysters, wine specials and Spanish tapas. Walk-ins are welcome, and it takes Resy bookings for groups. The Jefferson Street L stop is three minutes away.

Mad Tropical, at 236 Troutman Street, is four minutes west. Its happy hour runs from late afternoon into the evening, Tuesday through Sunday, and on Tuesday it lasts all night for Taco Tuesday. The deal covers cocktails at two price levels, draft beer and a pair of tacos, so this is the place to eat. The bar is closed on Mondays, the other reason this crawl starts its week on Tuesday.

Finish three minutes west at The Little Whiskey, 36 Wilson Avenue, a pub whose Tuesday to Friday happy hour runs into the evening, as late as Mad Tropical's. The list covers PBR tall boys, Miller High Life, wine and well drinks, and on Mondays the deal runs all day. La Loncheria, with margaritas, micheladas and guacamole on its daily happy hour, is right across the street, and the Morgan Avenue L is six minutes away.

sections.body:
Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. Those are the only days all five happy hours run. Gordo's Cantina and The Little Whiskey run Monday to Friday and The Ten Bells runs every day, but Vacations has no Monday happy hour and Mad Tropical is closed on Mondays.

Tuesday is the strongest night of the four, because Mad Tropical keeps its happy hour going all night for Taco Tuesday, so you can stay at the fourth stop as long as you like.

On a weekend, six of the 15 Bushwick bars on our list run a Saturday happy hour. A Saturday version that stays close to this route: La Loncheria on Wilson Avenue, which runs its happy hour every day, then Mad Tropical and The Ten Bells, then Keybar on Troutman Street, which runs a daily window into the evening.

Gordo's Cantina has the earliest and longest window, so start there in the afternoon. Vacations opens its window later and keeps it short, and The Ten Bells ends at the same time, so the second and third stops are the ones to watch: arrive at Vacations as its window opens, have one round, and move on. Mad Tropical and The Little Whiskey run the latest, which gives you a relaxed finish.

The walk is longer than a Manhattan crawl. Gordo's Cantina to Vacations is about 450 meters, six minutes. Vacations to The Ten Bells is about 515 meters, a little over six minutes. The Ten Bells to Mad Tropical is about 335 meters, four minutes, and the last leg to The Little Whiskey is about 280 meters, three to four minutes. That adds up to about 1.6 kilometers, or 20 minutes on foot. We measure straight lines between each bar's coordinates at about 80 meters per minute, so real walks run a little longer.

Plan on about three hours. The table below lists every happy hour within 800 meters of The Ten Bells, closest first, in case one stop is full. There are 13.

sections.h: Ending the night at a party
sections.body: The Little Whiskey is about nine minutes on foot from House of Yes at 2 Wyckoff Avenue, and about the same from The Sultan Room on Starr Street and Sea Wolf Bushwick on Wyckoff Avenue. Most of the parties below open their doors after the last happy hour ends, which leaves time for dinner, but DYKE-o-Ween opens earlier in the evening, so check the time on each party page. Everything below is 21 and over. On the crawl nights coming up: Club Joon Halloween and 1 Year Anniversary at House of Yes on Wednesday, October 28. On Thursday, October 29, Gaydar Halloween at House of Yes and DYKE-o-Ween at The Sultan Room. On Friday, October 30, Zombie Prom at House of Yes and the American Horror Halloween Party, a reggaeton night with a costume contest, at Sea Wolf Bushwick. On Friday, November 6, House of Yes hosts House of Grooves: Eli Escobar All Night. For other nights, our NYC parties list and the Halloween parties page are kept current, with the venue and date for each.

The route follows the L. Start at DeKalb Avenue, which our listing puts two minutes from Gordo's Cantina. The middle stops are near Jefferson Street: four minutes from Vacations and three from The Ten Bells. Mad Tropical is seven minutes from Central Avenue on the M. The Little Whiskey is six minutes from Morgan Avenue on the L, so you can ride home from there or walk on to a party.

faq.a: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday. Those are the only days all five stops run happy hour. Tuesday has an extra edge, since Mad Tropical's happy hour lasts all night for Taco Tuesday.

title: New Year's Eve in NYC 2026: How to Pick Your Party
h1: New Year's Eve in NYC 2026: a planning guide for the big night
description: Planning New Year's Eve in NYC 2026? Choose a party by type and neighborhood, check tickets and age limits, plan the ride home and a Thursday happy hour.
answer: New Year's Eve in NYC 2026 lands on a Thursday, and we list 22 published parties that night, 15 in Manhattan and 7 in Brooklyn, all 21 and up. Choose by kind first: club nights at SILO Brooklyn and Elsewhere in Bushwick or Marquee in Chelsea, rooftops such as Darling Rooftop on Central Park South and El Nico in Williamsburg, or big rooms like Capitale on the Bowery and Sony Hall. Most parties start at 9 p.m., so a Thursday happy hour nearby, such as Desmond's Tavern near the Koreatown parties or Lucky in the East Village, makes an easy first stop.
intro: New Year's Eve is the one night when every plan in the city competes for the same few hours. The trick is to decide early what kind of night you want, then pick a neighborhood where you can walk between dinner, a first drink and the party. This guide walks through those choices. For the full live list, with tickets, start times and status for each party, go to every NYE party we list. Right now our list has 22 published parties on Thursday, December 31, 2026, at 21 venues. Eighteen of them start at 9 p.m. The early outlier is the Rooftop Ball Drop View party at Margaritaville Times Square, which starts at 7 p.m. Capitale and El Nico Rooftop start at 8 p.m., and Elsewhere opens last, at 10:30 p.m. The picks below are bars whose regular happy hour runs on Thursdays, each a short walk from one of the party clusters. Holiday hours can change, so treat them as a plan to confirm, not a promise.

picks.why: A Park Avenue South tavern two minutes from the 28th Street station on the 6. Its happy hour runs Monday through Friday, so Thursday the 31st is on the schedule, from mid-afternoon into the early evening. Expect pints, an Irish or American shot-and-beer combo, margaritas, well drinks and wine. Tavern 29 is about a minute's walk away and Ainsworth roughly four minutes, which makes this the warm-up for the Koreatown cluster.

An Avenue B bar in the East Village with one of the longer weekday windows on our list, from midday into the evening, Monday through Friday. The deal covers drinks, shots, wine and White Claw, with money off drafts and a separate price on Aperol spritzes and prosecco. Blind Barber, which hosts a New Year's Eve party, is about 30 meters away. The 1st Avenue L stop is five minutes on foot.

A Hudson Street bar whose Tuesday to Friday happy hour covers Thursday the 31st in the late afternoon. Every draught beer is on the deal, along with buckets of beer, spritzes, margaritas, sangria, wine by the glass or bottle and bar food. The White Horse Tavern, one of the West Village's NYE parties, is under a minute away on foot. Christopher Street-Stonewall on the 1 is a five-minute walk.

A Rivington Street spot two minutes from Essex Street (F, J, M, Z). Its Thursday window opens in the early evening and runs later than most on this list. Beer, wine, well drinks and a margarita tower are on the deal, and the tower is built for a group. The Skinny Bar, where the Downtown Crawl registers, is about three minutes away, and VIRGO on Grand Street about five.

An 11th Avenue bar in West Chelsea with a happy hour every day of the week, Thursday included, from mid-afternoon into the early evening, built around a list of house cocktails. It is the closest pick to the West 27th Street pair of parties: Hotel Alameda is about three minutes away and Marquee about four. The 7 train at 34th Street-Hudson Yards is a six-minute walk.

A Cypress Avenue bar with a rooftop, four minutes from the Jefferson Street L stop. Happy hour runs Tuesday through Friday in the early evening, and the deal is a discount on everything rather than a short menu. Elsewhere is about a three-minute walk and SILO Brooklyn about four, so it works before either Bushwick club night. The window closes well before doors, so come early and eat nearby.

A pub on Kent Avenue near the Williamsburg waterfront, seven minutes from Bedford Avenue on the L. Its weekday window covers Thursday the 31st. The deal centers on the bar's own pilsner, plus a beer-or-seltzer-and-shot combo at the bartender's choice. Superior Ingredients, home of both the Roof and the Room parties, is about two minutes away, which makes this the natural meeting point for either ticket.

sections.h: Start with the kind of night you want
sections.body: Club nights are for people who care who is playing. In Bushwick, New Year's Eve: Gravagerz at SILO Brooklyn and Elsewhere New Year's Eve with San Pacho sit about two minutes apart. &ME New Year's Eve takes over the Duggal Greenhouse at the Brooklyn Navy Yard, and Loud Luxury headlines Marquee in Chelsea. For Latin sounds, there is a reggaeton party at The Meadows in Brooklyn and a Latin-tagged night at Hotel Alameda in Chelsea. Rooftops and views trade the dance floor for a skyline. Darling Rooftop is on Central Park South, the Rooftop Ball Drop View party is at Margaritaville Times Square, and Williamsburg has El Nico Rooftop and the Superior Ingredients Roof. Big rooms and halls suit a large group that wants one ticket and one address: Capitale on the Bowery, Sony Hall off Times Square, Houston Hall on West Houston Street and the Superior Ingredients Room. Smaller bar and lounge parties fill in the rest: Tavern 29, 5th & Mad, Ainsworth, Blind Barber, White Horse, Common Ground and VIRGO. If you cannot choose one place, the Downtown Crawl Til the Ball Drops starts at The Skinny Bar on the Lower East Side. One gap: no boat parties are on our list for December 31 yet.

sections.h: Pick a neighborhood you can walk
sections.body:
On New Year's Eve, the best plan keeps you on foot. Koreatown has the tightest Manhattan cluster: Tavern 29, Ainsworth and 5th & Mad are each about four minutes from the next. In Chelsea, Hotel Alameda and Marquee sit about a minute apart on West 27th Street. Downtown, VIRGO, The Skinny Bar and Capitale are all within about eight minutes of each other, and Blind Barber is a short trip north in the East Village.

The West Village and Meatpacking District give you White Horse and Common Ground, about six minutes apart, with Houston Hall a ten-minute walk south. In Brooklyn, SILO Brooklyn and Elsewhere form the Bushwick pair, and The Meadows is about a 14-minute walk from Elsewhere. Williamsburg's two Superior Ingredients parties share one building on Wythe Avenue, with El Nico Rooftop about 11 minutes away.

Midtown is the one area where we would plan with extra care. Margaritaville Times Square and Sony Hall are both close to the Times Square crowds, so read each party page's entry notes before you set out, and leave more time than you think you need.

sections.h: Tickets: what to check before you buy
sections.body:
Read the ticket type, not just the party name. Superior Ingredients sells the Roof and the Room as separate listings, so a ticket for one does not cover the other. Some parties bundle an open bar and a midnight toast, others sell entry only, and table packages are a different product again. The party page spells out what each listing includes.

Check the status and the lineup next. Every Dec 31 party on our list is currently marked as scheduled, but Elsewhere's lineup is still partly to be announced, and other parties have not named their DJs yet. Finally, read the refund terms on the ticket site before paying, because they differ between sellers and promoters. Current prices are on each party page.

Every one of the 22 parties on our December 31 list is listed as 21 and up, so there is no all-ages option on it. Bring a valid government photo ID, and plan for a door check even if you look older. Visitors from abroad should carry a passport. Our guide to what time bars close in NYC covers which IDs New York bars accept and why bouncers are strict about it.

Plan the ride home before you plan the outfit. The MTA says the subway runs 24 hours a day, every day of the year, but not every route runs around the clock, and late trains come less often, so check your line before the night. Choosing a party near your own subway line is the simplest fix.

Bars and clubs must stop serving alcohol at 4 a.m. in Manhattan, according to the State Liquor Authority's county hours, so that is the latest any of these nights can pour. Each party page lists its own end time. January 1, 2027 is a Friday, which gives most people a long weekend to recover. Agree on a meeting point before midnight, because phones and crowds both get unreliable right after the countdown.

faq.a: Thursday. December 31, 2026 falls on a Thursday, and New Year's Day, January 1, 2027, is a Friday. That means regular Thursday happy hour schedules apply on the eve itself, if the bar keeps its usual hours.

faq.a: We list 22 published parties on December 31, 2026, at 21 venues: 15 in Manhattan and 7 in Brooklyn. The full live list is on our every NYE party page.
faq.q: How many New Year's Eve parties are there in NYC in 2026?

faq.a: Not on our list yet. None of the 22 published December 31 parties is a boat party. We add new listings as they are announced, so check the NYE party page again closer to the date.
faq.q: Are there New Year's Eve boat parties in NYC this year?

faq.a: No. All 22 parties on our December 31 list are 21 and up, so bring a valid government photo ID.
faq.q: Can people under 21 go to these New Year's Eve parties?

faq.a: Some do on paper, because December 31, 2026 is a Thursday and many bars list a Thursday happy hour. Holiday hours often change, so call or check the bar's site that week before you count on it.
faq.q: Do NYC bars run happy hour on New Year's Eve?

faq.a: The subway runs 24 hours a day, every day, according to the MTA. Not every route runs around the clock, and trains are less frequent late at night, so check your line before you go out.
faq.q: Does the subway run all night on New Year's Eve?

method: We pulled every published party on our list with a night date of December 31, 2026: 22 parties at 21 venues, with details from the ticket listings linked on each party page, last checked October 22, 2026. Start times, age limits and neighborhoods come from those listings.
