title: Where to Watch the NYC Marathon 2026: Bars Near the Course
h1: Where to watch the NYC Marathon in 2026, with a Sunday happy hour nearby
keyword: where to watch the nyc marathon
description: Where to watch the NYC Marathon on Sunday, Nov 1, 2026: Fourth Avenue, Greenpoint and First Avenue, plus 6 bars nearby with Sunday happy hours.
answer: If you are deciding where to watch the NYC Marathon on Sunday, November 1, 2026, pick a stretch with a bar behind you: Fourth Avenue in Park Slope, Manhattan Avenue in Greenpoint, or First Avenue on the Upper East Side. Whisk & Whiskey sits on Fourth Avenue with an all-day Sunday happy hour, Papacito's and Troost are a few minutes from the Greenpoint course, and Westville, The Hunterian and The Alvin Public House run Sunday happy hours on or just off First Avenue.
intro:
The 2026 TCS New York City Marathon is on Sunday, November 1, and it marks 50 years of the five-borough course. Runners start on Staten Island, cross the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge, and pass through Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx and Manhattan before finishing in Central Park. New York Road Runners says most of the course is open to spectators from mile 3 to mile 26, which leaves a lot of curb to choose from.

This guide picks three spectator areas where the course runs past streets with bars, and checks which of those bars publish a happy hour on Sunday. That last filter matters: plenty of bars only run deals on weekdays, and a Sunday window is what turns a few hours of cheering into a cheaper afternoon. We counted every bar on our list within about a five-minute walk of each stretch and kept six with a Sunday happy hour and published offers.

One honest warning up front. Race day is one of the busiest Sundays of the year near the course, and no bar has told us its marathon-day hours. The schedules below are each bar's regular Sunday happy hour. Treat them as a plan, not a promise, and check the pick cards before you go.

picks.why: A bar on Fourth Avenue itself, at number 259 in Park Slope, so the course runs right past the door. Sunday is its strongest day: the happy hour runs all day, with draft beers, wines, well drinks, two house cocktails called the Queen Bee and the Jenny, and a Narragansett with a well shot. It also runs Wednesday to Friday. Union Street on the R is a two-minute walk.

A bar on Manhattan Avenue in Greenpoint, about four minutes on foot from where the course meets Greenpoint Avenue, in the stretch NYRR places at miles 10 to 13. Its afternoon happy hour runs every day, Sunday included, with two-for-one frozen margaritas, Tecate and Modelo cans, house margaritas, sangria by the pint, a tequila and Tecate combo, and nachos. Greenpoint Avenue on the G is three minutes away.

A cocktail and wine bar a little farther up Manhattan Avenue, at number 1011, about five minutes on foot from the course at Greenpoint Avenue. Happy hour runs daily in the late afternoon, Sunday included, with money off beer, cocktails and house wine by the glass or quartino, plus a tap Negroni. Pair it with Papacito's for a two-stop Greenpoint afternoon. Greenpoint Avenue on the G is three minutes away.

A pub on East 64th Street, a few steps from First Avenue and close to where runners come off the Queensboro Bridge at mile 16. Its happy hour runs every day in the late afternoon, Sunday included, with Trumer pilsner, Kona Big Wave, Sloop Juice Bomb, pinot grigio and pinot noir, a pineapple mule, a blackberry gimlet, a house margarita, sangria and a green tea shot.

A bar on East 70th Street, just east of First Avenue. On Sundays, as on every day from Tuesday on, happy hour runs from opening until the early evening, which suits a long watch that starts with the front of the field. The deal covers money off draft beer, plus wine by the glass and well shots and drinks at happy hour prices. The Q at 72nd Street is five minutes away.

A restaurant right on First Avenue at number 1359, inside the stretch NYRR places at miles 16 to 18. Happy hour runs every day from late afternoon into the early evening, Sunday included, with classic, spicy or smoky margaritas, sangria, signature and seasonal cocktails, all wines by the glass, all beers and mocktails. The 72nd Street Q station is three minutes away.

sections.body:
The race is on Sunday, November 1, 2026, with the official start at 8 a.m., according to NYRR. Spectators can watch along most of the course from mile 3 to mile 26. There is no viewing at the start on Staten Island or on any of the bridges, and NYRR asks spectators to stay behind the blue tape or barricades. Pedestrian crossing zones are set up in Brooklyn and Manhattan so you can get from one side of the course to the other.

NYRR recommends the subway as the way to move between spots, and its app has a spectator guide and runner tracking, which is the easiest way to know when your runner will reach you. NYRR also says the 2026 course has a new section through East Harlem and the Bronx after the Willis Avenue Bridge, so check the official map if you plan to watch up there.

Fourth Avenue is where the field comes off the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge and heads north through Brooklyn, and NYRR points spectators to the R train for it. It is long and straight, so crowds spread out more than they do in Manhattan.

On our list, 15 bars sit within about five minutes of the avenue, and 4 of them run a Sunday happy hour. Whisk & Whiskey is the one right on the course, with an all-day Sunday deal. Chela and 390 Social, both on Fifth Avenue in Park Slope, a block over, list Sunday windows in the late afternoon but do not publish their offers, so the pick cards show times only. Both take reservations on Resy, which is worth doing on a crowded Sunday.

NYRR describes Williamsburg and Greenpoint as the stretch where spectators line streets full of shops and restaurants as runners head toward the Pulaski Bridge into Queens. Manhattan Avenue, before Greenpoint Avenue, is listed among the streets closed to traffic on race day. The Pulaski Bridge itself is closed to spectators, and NYRR notes many fans cheer on the Queens side, just past the halfway mark.

We found 8 bars on our list within about five minutes of Manhattan Avenue and Greenpoint Avenue, 3 with a Sunday happy hour. Papacito's and Troost are the two with published offers, and they sit a minute apart on Manhattan Avenue, just north of Greenpoint Avenue. Walk back to the course between rounds, or settle in once your runner has passed. The G at Greenpoint Avenue serves both.

sections.h: First Avenue, Upper East Side, miles 16 to 18
sections.body:
Runners come off the Queensboro Bridge onto First Avenue at mile 16, and NYRR describes this as a stretch where spectators line the sidewalks and cheer runners on. It is the most bar-friendly part of the course on our list: 22 bars sit within about five minutes of First Avenue between the bridge and the low 90s, and 10 of them run a Sunday happy hour.

The Alvin Public House is closest to the bridge, The Hunterian runs its deal from opening, and Westville is right on the avenue. If you want to see your runner twice, NYRR lists Fifth Avenue between East 90th and East 105th Streets, at miles 23 and 24, as another viewing spot. From First Avenue at East 90th Street, that is about a 13-minute walk west across the Upper East Side, straight-line, which gives you time after a runner passes on First Avenue to catch them again near Central Park.

sections.h: Crowds, hours and what we could not confirm
sections.body: Expect the bars on these stretches to be full, especially on First Avenue. Arrive early, go in small groups, and do not count on a table with a window. We could not confirm race-day hours or whether any bar will run its usual Sunday happy hour on November 1. Bars on a big event day sometimes change menus or skip deals. The times and offers on the cards come from each bar's regular published schedule. We also have no bars on our list with a Sunday happy hour within a short walk of the East Harlem or Fifth Avenue viewing areas, so we have not recommended any there. For the rest of the day, our Sunday happy hours page lists every Sunday deal in the city.

faq.a: Sunday, November 1, 2026. NYRR lists the official start at 8 a.m., and the 2026 race marks 50 years of the five-borough course.
faq.q: When is the 2026 NYC Marathon?

faq.a: Almost anywhere from mile 3 to mile 26, except the start and the bridges. NYRR highlights Fourth Avenue in Brooklyn, Williamsburg and Greenpoint at miles 10 to 13, First Avenue at miles 16 to 18, and Fifth Avenue from East 90th to East 105th Streets at miles 23 and 24.
faq.q: Where can I watch the NYC Marathon?

faq.a: On our list: Whisk & Whiskey on Fourth Avenue in Park Slope, Papacito's and Troost on Manhattan Avenue in Greenpoint, and The Alvin Public House, The Hunterian and Westville on or just off First Avenue on the Upper East Side.
faq.q: Which bars near the marathon course have a Sunday happy hour?

faq.a: We could not confirm it. The schedules on our cards are each bar's regular Sunday happy hour, and bars along the course may change hours or menus on a busy race day. Call ahead or check the bar's site that morning.
faq.q: Will bars run happy hour on marathon day?

faq.a: No. NYRR does not allow spectators on any bridge on the course. Many fans watch the Pulaski Bridge crossing from the Queens side, just past halfway, and First Avenue picks up the field as it comes off the Queensboro Bridge.
faq.q: Can I watch from the Queensboro or Pulaski Bridge?

faq.a: Take the subway, which NYRR recommends for spectators. Use the official pedestrian crossing zones in Brooklyn and Manhattan to cross the course, and follow your runner in the NYRR app.
faq.q: How do I get between viewing spots?

table_title: Happy hours near First Avenue and East 70th Street
method: Race date, start time, course, viewing areas, bridge rules, crossing zones and the 2026 course change come from nyrr.org (the 2026 race page, the course pages, the Watch the Race guide and NYRR race-week news), checked October 23, 2026. Bars come from our database of New York happy hours, which records each bar's schedule and offers from its own website; the six picks were last checked between October 18 and October 21, 2026. We counted bars within about 400 meters of points along each stretch of the course and kept those whose happy hour includes Sunday. Walking times are straight-line distances at about 80 meters a minute.

title: Bars Near Madison Square Garden: 8 Happy Hours Close By
h1: Bars near Madison Square Garden for before and after the show
description: Bars near Madison Square Garden with weekday happy hours, all within about a 10-minute walk: walk times, deals and a late option for after the game.
answer: The closest bars near Madison Square Garden with a weekday happy hour are Tara Mor on West 30th Street, Burgerology Midtown on West 36th Street and Legasea Bar & Grill on Seventh Avenue, each about four or five minutes on foot. We count 36 happy hour bars within about a 10-minute walk of the Garden, and 22 of them keep a weekday window running into the early evening or later. For after the game, Glass Ceiling Rooftop on Broadway runs a second happy hour late in the evening, Tuesday through Saturday.
intro: A game or a concert at the Garden usually means one of two plans: a fast round on the way in, or a drink once the crowd spills out. The blocks around Penn Station have plenty of bars, but not all of them run a deal at the hours you need, and the closest ones fill first. We measured every happy hour on our list from the Garden and kept the ones within about a 10-minute walk. That gave us 36 bars. The eight picks below cover the main directions out of the arena: south toward 28th Street, north toward 36th to 40th Streets, and east into NoMad. Each card shows the live deal and hours, so check it on the day. If you are coming straight from the office, our guide to after-work drinks near Grand Central and Penn Station covers more commuter-friendly options, and the Penn Station and MSG happy hour map shows everything nearby at a glance.

picks.why: An Irish pub on West 30th Street, about four minutes on foot from the Garden and two minutes from the 28th Street station on the 1. The Monday to Friday happy hour runs from late afternoon into the early evening, so it suits a straight-from-work arrival. Aperol spritzes, a Midtown Mule, margaritas, house wine and every draft beer are on it, plus a food special where you choose any two bites or fries.

A burger bar on West 36th Street, about five minutes north of the Garden and two minutes from 34th Street-Penn Station on the A, C and E. Happy hour runs Monday through Friday, at the bar only, into the early evening. Well cocktails, wine and select drafts are on the list, along with sliders: the house Burgerology slider, short rib and buffalo chicken, plus a turkey burger. Other cocktails and beers get a smaller discount.

A bar and grill on Seventh Avenue, about five minutes away and two minutes from the 1, 2 and 3 at Penn Station. The weekday happy hour starts mid-afternoon and runs into the early evening, with oysters, fries, beer, wine and martinis. It is served at the bar only and walk-ins are welcome, so aim for stools rather than a table. A dozen oysters and a martini make a quick pre-game.

A bar on West 38th Street, about six minutes north of the Garden and three minutes from Times Square-42nd Street. Its Monday to Friday window runs from late afternoon into the early evening. The list is short and drink-focused: a cucumber gimlet, house red, white or prosecco, well drinks and a Five Boroughs session IPA on draft. It suits a group that wants one round and an easy walk south to the arena.

A cocktail bar on West 28th Street, about six minutes from the Garden and three minutes from the 28th Street R and W. Its Tuesday to Friday happy hour starts and ends later than most nearby, running from early evening into the evening, which helps on a night with a later start. The draw is mini martinis, with a flight of three for sampling, plus beer, wine and bites. Tables book through OpenTable.

A modern American bar and restaurant on West 38th Street, about seven minutes away and five minutes from 42nd Street-Port Authority. Happy hour runs every day from late afternoon into the early evening, so it also works for a weekend matinee or a Sunday game. Expect a short cocktail list with a Boulevardier and the house margarita, beer, rotating wines and prosecco, plus pizza and the Altair burger on the food side.

A rooftop bar on Broadway in NoMad, about eight minutes east of the Garden and a minute from the 28th Street R and W. It runs two windows Tuesday through Saturday: a short one in the early evening and a second late in the evening, the only weekday happy hour within a 10-minute walk that starts that late. Espresso, dirty and cosmo martinis, classic cocktails, flatbreads, a Caesar and a chip-and-charcuterie plate are on the deal.

A tavern on West 40th Street, about nine minutes from the Garden and a minute from 42nd Street-Bryant Park. Happy hour runs Tuesday through Friday and stays on into the evening, one of the latest nearby, served in The Speakeasy on the lower level. The list is long: two margaritas, an Old Fashioned, a Manhattan, sangria, a cosmo, an Aperol spritz, select wines, draft beer and well drinks. Reservations go through OpenTable.

sections.h: Before the game: matching the window to your night
sections.body:
Most happy hours near the Garden run on weekdays and wrap up in the early evening, so the pre-show round works best if you leave work a little early. Tara Mor, Burgerology, Legasea and District Tap House all run Monday through Friday, and all four are within about six minutes of the arena. If your night starts later, The Fleur Room and Croton Reservoir Tavern keep their windows going longest, but both skip Mondays.

On a Monday, stick to the Monday-to-Friday group, or Altair, which runs every day. On weekends the options thin out: Altair covers Saturday and Sunday, and The Dawson 39 on West 39th Street runs its happy hour all day on both weekend days. Juniper and Muses 35 Bar & Karaoke on West 35th Street, each about three minutes away, also list a happy hour every day, though neither posts its deal items, so ask at the bar.

A tip for the bar-only deals at Burgerology and Legasea: one person holds stools while the others arrive. They are among the closest bars to the arena, and they fill early on event nights.

Late deals are rare in this part of Midtown. Within about a 10-minute walk, Glass Ceiling Rooftop is the only bar on our list with a weekday window that starts late in the evening, Tuesday through Saturday. On Saturdays, The Dawson 39's all-day window runs past midnight, and on Sundays it goes well into the evening, with spritzes, house wine, draft beer and bar bites such as nachos, wings and pretzel bites. Maru Karaoke Lounge on West 32nd Street runs an evening happy hour Sunday through Wednesday on beer, shots, well drinks and cocktails, with a karaoke discount during the same window. It is about a nine-minute walk east of the Garden. If none of those fit, the table below lists every happy hour around Penn Station and the Garden, and our late-night happy hours page covers the rest of the city.

Pick a direction before you leave the arena, because the crowd moves with you. Heading north puts you on West 36th to West 40th Streets, where Burgerology, District Tap House, Altair and Croton Reservoir Tavern sit between about five and nine minutes away. Heading south and east takes you to Tara Mor on West 30th Street, The Fleur Room on West 28th Street and Glass Ceiling Rooftop on Broadway. Legasea is the closest on Seventh Avenue itself.

Our walking times are straight-line distances at about 80 meters a minute, measured from the Garden, so add a minute or two for crossings. Most picks are within three minutes of a subway stop, which makes it easy to head home without walking back past the arena.

Door times and bag rules are set event by event, so check your event's page on msg.com before you settle in at a bar, and leave enough time to get through the entrance. We do not list event start times here because they change from show to show. If you want a guaranteed table for a group, Tara Mor, The Fleur Room, Glass Ceiling Rooftop and Croton Reservoir Tavern all have a booking link on their cards. title: What Time Is Happy Hour in NYC? What 685 Bars Tell Us
h1: What Time Is Happy Hour in NYC? The Answer From 685 Bars
keyword: what time is happy hour in nyc
description: What time is happy hour in NYC? We checked 685 bars: the most common window is 4 to 7 p.m. on weekdays. Here are the patterns by day and borough.
answer: What time is happy hour in NYC? Across the 685 bars we track, the most common window is 4 to 7 p.m., Monday to Friday: 4 p.m. is the most common start and 7 p.m. the most common end. About three in five bars run happy hour on weekdays only. For exceptions, Cafe Luce in Midtown East starts before lunch, LOLITA near Times Square adds a late-night round every day, and 169 Bar on the Lower East Side runs its deal only on weekends.
intro:
Ask a New Yorker when happy hour is and you will hear "after work." That is right most of the time, but the exceptions are where the good afternoons and late nights are. So we counted. We took every happy hour window on our list of 685 bars across the five boroughs, 785 windows in all, and tallied when they start, when they end, which days they run and how that changes from borough to borough.

The five picks each stand for one pattern: an early window, an all-day one, a late-night one, a weekend-only one and the classic weekday slot. Their exact hours and prices sit on the cards, which update from each bar's own site, so check those on the day you go.

picks.why: Cafe Luce, a restaurant on East 53rd Street, is our example of an early window. Its happy hour runs Monday to Friday, opening in the late morning and closing in the late afternoon, before most bars on our list have even started theirs. The list is short: house red and white by the glass, prosecco, an Aperitivo Spritz, a Hugo Spritz and an Amarena Fizz. Lexington Av/53 St on the E and F is a two-minute walk.

Chateau 49 on Second Avenue shows what all-day means on our list: a window that opens around lunchtime and runs into the early evening, seven days a week, which puts it among the 191 bars with a deal every day. The menu leans on wine, from cremant rose and prosecco to sauvignon blanc, Bordeaux and pinot noir, plus espresso martinis, spritzes, margaritas and all beers. The 51st Street station is a five-minute walk.

LOLITA, a Mexican bar on West 45th Street, runs two windows every day: one in the afternoon and a second that starts late in the evening and runs into the night, making it one of 28 bars in our data with a window starting at 9 p.m. or later. The menu covers cocktails such as the Lolita Margarita and Mezcal Negroni, house wines, cervezas and discounted bites. Rockefeller Center on the B, D, F and M is three minutes away.

169 Bar on East Broadway is one of only six bars on our list whose happy hour runs on Saturday and Sunday and never on a weekday. The window covers the weekend afternoon into the early evening, with money off liquor drinks (well shots excluded) and beer, plus a well shot when you order any beer. Our listing tags it for cocktails and outdoor space. The East Broadway stop on the F is a one-minute walk.

The Penny Farthing, a pub on Third Avenue near Union Square, keeps the single most common schedule in our data: Monday to Friday, through the after-work hours. The menu covers a full round: draft beer, wines, espresso martinis, Aperol, green tea shots, well drinks and beers, plus a burger if you need dinner. The 3rd Avenue stop on the L is a one-minute walk, which makes it an easy meeting point.

sections.h: The most common happy hour times
sections.body: Start times bunch up in mid-afternoon. Of the 685 bars, 252 have a window that starts at 4 p.m., the most common start by a wide margin, followed by 3 p.m. (147 bars) and 5 p.m. (106 bars). In all, 503 bars, close to three in four, have a window starting between 3 and 5 p.m. Another 72 bars list only an end time, so they sit out the start-time counts. End times are even more uniform. 341 bars have a window ending at 7 p.m. and 194 end at 6 p.m., so 570 bars, about five in six, finish between 6 and 7 p.m. Only 58 run to 8 p.m. The most common pairing is 4 to 7 p.m. (125 bars), then 4 to 6 (93), 5 to 7 (70), 3 to 7 (64) and 3 to 6 (60). Walk into a bar at 5:30 p.m. on a weekday and a deal is likely running; at 7:15 p.m., most have just ended. Our happy hour now page shows the deals running at the moment you open it.

Happy hour in New York is mostly a weekday habit. 404 of the 685 bars, about three in five, run it on weekdays only, and 298 of those keep the straight Monday to Friday pattern. The other 281 have a window on at least one weekend day, and 191, a little over one in four, run a deal all seven days. Only six bars save their happy hour for the weekend alone. Tuesday through Thursday are the safest bets. Thursday has the most bars with a deal (672), then Wednesday (669) and Tuesday (653). Friday drops to 603, and Monday is lower at 587, since 98 bars have no Monday happy hour. Sunday (264 bars) edges out Saturday (235). Our weekend happy hours page keeps that list current.

A minority of bars break the after-work mold. 106 have a window that starts before 3 p.m., and 87 start by noon or when the doors open, often with a long lunch-to-evening window like Chateau 49's. Our guide to early happy hours covers the ones worth an afternoon off. At the other end, 28 bars have a window starting at 9 p.m. or later, three of them after midnight. These are reverse happy hours, and 20 of the 28 run them as a second round on top of an earlier window, the way LOLITA does. Late windows peak midweek: 24 bars run one on Wednesday, against 17 on Saturday. In all, 78 bars run more than one window. See late-night happy hours for the list, and our bar closing time guide for how late New York bars can legally serve.

4 p.m. is the most common start in Manhattan, Brooklyn and Queens, and 7 p.m. the most common end everywhere, but the details shift. Brooklyn starts later: 43 of its 158 bars, about one in four, have a window starting at 5 p.m., against 53 of 445 in Manhattan, about one in eight. Manhattan ends earlier: a third of its bars (152) have a window ending at 6 p.m., against fewer than one in five in Brooklyn (29).

Manhattan is also the borough for weekend deals: 201 of its 445 bars run on at least one weekend day, while in Brooklyn 108 of 158 bars are weekday only. Queens sits in between, with 27 of 68 bars offering a weekend deal. Manhattan has 20 of the 28 late-night windows, Brooklyn 6 and Queens 2. The Bronx and Staten Island have seven bars each on our list, too few to call a trend, though 3 p.m. is the most common start in both.

sections.h: The rules, and how to check before you go
sections.body:
Happy hour itself is legal in New York, but bottomless deals are not. State law bars a licensee from offering unlimited drinks over a set period of time for a fixed price, so a New York happy hour means a lower price per drink, not an open bar.

Schedules change with the seasons, the sports calendar and new management, so treat any list as a starting point. Our cards pull each bar's hours from its own site, with the date we last checked on every listing.

faq.a: Most often 4 to 7 p.m. on weekdays. In our data on 685 bars, 4 p.m. is the most common start (252 bars) and 7 p.m. the most common end (341 bars), and 503 bars have a window starting between 3 and 5 p.m.
faq.q: What time is happy hour in NYC?

faq.a: Some do, but most do not. 281 of the 685 bars on our list run happy hour on at least one weekend day and 191 run it every day, while 404 keep it to weekdays. Sunday has slightly more deals (264 bars) than Saturday (235).
faq.q: Do NYC bars have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: Thursday, with 672 bars on our list running a deal, just ahead of Wednesday (669) and Tuesday (653). Friday (603) and Monday (587) have fewer, and Saturday has the fewest of the week.
faq.q: Which day has the most happy hours in NYC?

faq.a: Yes, at 28 bars on our list, with a window starting at 9 p.m. or later. Twenty of them run it as a second round after an earlier happy hour, like LOLITA near Times Square. Twenty are in Manhattan.
faq.q: Are there late-night happy hours in NYC?

faq.a: No. New York's Alcoholic Beverage Control Law bars licensees from offering unlimited drinks over a set period for a fixed price. Happy hour discounts on each drink are allowed.
faq.q: Are bottomless drink deals legal in New York?

table_title: Happy hours that also run on weekends
method: We counted every happy hour window for the 685 bars on our list on October 23, 2026, using the schedules each bar publishes on its own site, last checked between September 2 and October 23, 2026. A bar counts once in each finding even when it has several windows. Bars that list only an end time (72) are left out of start-time counts, and late-night means a window starting at 9 p.m. or later. Shares are of bars, not of discounts. The note on unlimited-drink offers comes from New York's Alcoholic Beverage Control Law section 117-a as published by the New York State Senate.

title: Thanksgiving Eve NYC 2026: A Night-Out Plan
h1: Thanksgiving Eve NYC 2026: happy hour first, then the party, then home
description: Thanksgiving Eve NYC on Wednesday, Nov 25, 2026: bars with a Wednesday happy hour near the night's parties in Bushwick, Williamsburg and Chelsea.
answer: Thanksgiving Eve NYC 2026 is Wednesday, November 25, the night before Thanksgiving on Thursday the 26th. Our list has seven parties that night, grouped in Bushwick (Elsewhere, SILO Brooklyn, The Chocolate Factory), Williamsburg (Sleepwalk, The Meadows, Superior Ingredients) and Chelsea (Marquee). Start at a bar with a Wednesday happy hour near your party: Vacations or SURA in Bushwick, Post No Bills or Kent Ale House in Williamsburg, or Porchlight in Chelsea.
intro: The Wednesday before Thanksgiving is a night when a lot of people are back in town, off work the next day and looking for each other. Thanksgiving falls on Thursday, November 26, 2026, which puts Thanksgiving Eve on Wednesday, November 25. This guide is a plan for the whole night: where to start on a happy hour, which party to walk to, and how to get home. The parties themselves have their own page. Our Thanksgiving Eve parties list keeps the full lineup current as new nights are announced. Here we use the seven published parties on our list for November 25 to anchor the plan, then look for bars nearby with a happy hour that runs on Wednesday. We found 14 bars with a Wednesday window within about a six-minute walk of one of those venues, and picked six with published deals. The idea is simple. Pick your party first, have a cheap first round and some food a few blocks away, then walk over. The next day is a holiday for many people, so there is no need to rush the start.

picks.why: A bar with a rooftop on Cypress Avenue in Bushwick, about three minutes on foot from The Chocolate Factory and four from Elsewhere and SILO Brooklyn. Its happy hour runs Tuesday through Friday in the early evening, Wednesday included, and takes money off everything, the simplest deal on this list. Jefferson Street on the L is four minutes away, so it works as the meeting point before any of the three Bushwick parties.

A bar on Wyckoff Avenue, a minute from Jefferson Street on the L and about four minutes from Elsewhere. Its weekday happy hour, Wednesday included, runs in the early evening and leans on food combos: Korean crispy boneless chicken with disco potatoes and a Sura Spritz, vegetable kimbap with two shots of soju, or a crispy miso cod taco with a white peach highball. Eat here before a long night. Reservations are on Resy.

The bar on Bushwick Avenue that hosts Date Nite: Vinyl Happy Hour on Thanksgiving Eve, a minute from Montrose Avenue on the L. Its regular happy hour runs every day until the early evening and takes money off all drinks, so you can catch the deal and the records in one stop. Post No Bills is next door for a second round, and The Meadows is about a six-minute walk.

A bar on Bushwick Avenue next door to Sleepwalk, one minute from Montrose Avenue on the L. Its happy hour runs every day and lasts into the evening, later than most picks here, with drafts, Budweiser and Miller High Life, well drinks, house cocktails, a beer and shot, margaritas in grapefruit, cucumber jalapeno, fresh lime and elderflower versions, and a Negroni. The Meadows is about a six-minute walk.

A pub on Kent Avenue about two minutes on foot from Superior Ingredients, where Flashback with Louie Vega plays on Thanksgiving Eve. Happy hour runs Monday to Friday from late afternoon into the early evening, with the house Kent Pilsner, and the bar also lists an all-night mystery beer or seltzer with a shot, at the bartender's choice. Bedford Avenue on the L is seven minutes away.

A cocktail bar on Eleventh Avenue in West Chelsea, about four minutes on foot from Marquee New York, where Twinsick plays on Thanksgiving Eve. Happy hour runs every day from the afternoon into the early evening, Wednesday included, with a list of house cocktails: a salty dog, a daiquiri, a porn star martini, a dirty martini and a Tommy's margarita. 34th Street-Hudson Yards on the 7 is six minutes away.

sections.body: Work backward from the party. Most of the Thanksgiving Eve nights on our list open their doors between 9 and 11 p.m., and the happy hours near them end by the early evening, with Post No Bills the late exception. That leaves a gap, and it is the right gap: first round on a deal, then dinner, then the walk over. Stay in one neighborhood. The seven parties fall into three clusters, and every pick below is within a few minutes on foot of at least one venue. Crossing from Chelsea to Bushwick mid-night costs you time you will want later. All seven parties are listed as 21 and over, so bring a valid ID. Our guide to what time bars close in NYC covers which IDs New York bars accept and how late they can serve.

sections.h: Bushwick: three dance floors near Jefferson Street
sections.body: Bushwick has the deepest Thanksgiving Eve lineup on our list, with three venues within a couple of minutes of each other off the Jefferson Street L stop. DayBreak is at Elsewhere, Tony Guerra and Luquez b2b Maria Sifontes play a house night at SILO Brooklyn, and Soul In The Horn with Natasha Diggs and Friends brings disco, funk, soul, hip-hop and house to The Chocolate Factory. All three open at 10 p.m. For the pre-game, Vacations Bar & Rooftop is the closest pick to all three, and SURA on Wyckoff Avenue is the one to choose if you need to eat. Little Beaver on St Nicholas Avenue and Dive Bar BK on Troutman Street also run Wednesday happy hours nearby, but they list times without published offers.

sections.h: Williamsburg: from vinyl to reggaeton to Louie Vega
sections.body: The Williamsburg side gives you the earliest start and the widest spread of music. Date Nite: Vinyl Happy Hour at Sleepwalk on Bushwick Avenue is a funk and soul night that starts at 6 p.m., the only early-evening party on our list for November 25. Next door, Post No Bills keeps its happy hour going into the evening. Later, Reggaeton Throwbacks opens at The Meadows on Meadow Street at 11 p.m., about six minutes on foot from both bars. Near the waterfront, Flashback with Louie Vega plays disco and house at Superior Ingredients on Wythe Avenue from 9 p.m. Kent Ale House is two minutes away for a first round. The Montrose Avenue and Bedford Avenue stops are both on the L, so you can do the vinyl hour early and still ride over to Wythe Avenue for Louie Vega.

If you would rather stay in Manhattan, Twinsick at Marquee New York on Tenth Avenue is the one Thanksgiving Eve party on our list there, with doors at 11 p.m. Porchlight on Eleventh Avenue is about four minutes away and runs its happy hour every day. Bar Avant Apres Bar on West 26th Street also lists a daily happy hour nearby, without published offers.

The MTA says the subway runs 24 hours a day, every day, but not every line runs at all times, and late-night routes can change. Check the MTA app before you leave the party. The Brooklyn picks here sit on the L, according to their listings, and Porchlight is closest to the 7 at 34th Street-Hudson Yards. Thursday, November 26, is Thanksgiving Day, a federal holiday on the OPM schedule and a holiday on New York City's 2026 holiday calendar. If you want to keep going, Groundcontrol Presents: Thanksgiving with KOFLA and Cristian Arango plays Superior Ingredients on Thursday night. Happy hours on the holiday itself are a different story, so check the cards before you count on one.

faq.a: Wednesday, November 25, 2026. Thanksgiving Day falls on Thursday, November 26, according to the federal holiday schedule published by the U.S. Office of Personnel Management.
faq.q: When is Thanksgiving Eve 2026?

faq.a: Our list has seven published parties for November 25: DayBreak at Elsewhere, Tony Guerra and Luquez b2b Maria Sifontes at SILO Brooklyn, Soul In The Horn at The Chocolate Factory, Date Nite: Vinyl Happy Hour at Sleepwalk, Reggaeton Throwbacks at The Meadows, Flashback with Louie Vega at Superior Ingredients and Twinsick at Marquee New York. The Thanksgiving Eve parties page keeps the list current.
faq.q: What parties are on Thanksgiving Eve in NYC?

faq.a: Near the parties, Vacations Bar & Rooftop and SURA in Bushwick, Sleepwalk, Post No Bills and Kent Ale House in Williamsburg, and Porchlight in Chelsea all list a Wednesday happy hour. These are their regular schedules; we could not confirm holiday-eve hours.
faq.q: Which bars have a happy hour on the Wednesday before Thanksgiving?

faq.a: Yes, all seven parties on our list for November 25 are listed as 21 and over. Bring a valid government ID or passport.
faq.q: Are Thanksgiving Eve parties 21 and over?

faq.a: Yes, the MTA runs the subway 24 hours a day, but not every line runs at all times. Check the MTA app for late-night service before you head home.
faq.q: Does the subway run late on Thanksgiving Eve?

faq.a: Yes, one on our list so far: Groundcontrol Presents: Thanksgiving with KOFLA and Cristian Arango at Superior Ingredients in Williamsburg on Thursday, November 26.
faq.q: Is there a party on Thanksgiving night itself?

method: The Thanksgiving date comes from the U.S. Office of Personnel Management's federal holiday schedule and New York City's 2026 holiday calendar, and subway hours from the MTA's rider guide, all checked October 23, 2026. Parties come from our published party listings for November 25 and 26, 2026, with venue addresses from our venue records; party times are shown in New York time. Bars come from our database of New York happy hours, which records each bar's schedule and offers from its own website. We counted bars with a Wednesday happy hour within about 500 meters of each party venue, measured straight-line at about 80 meters a minute. The six picks were last checked between September 2 and October 21, 2026.

title: Where to Celebrate a Birthday in NYC: 7 Bookable Bars
h1: Where to celebrate a birthday in NYC: bars that take bookings
keyword: where to celebrate a birthday in nyc
description: Where to celebrate a birthday in NYC: seven bars that take reservations and run happy hours, from Hell's Kitchen to Bushwick, plus booking and bill tips.
answer: If you are working out where to celebrate a birthday in NYC with a group, book a bar that takes reservations and runs a happy hour on your day. Friki Tiki in Hell's Kitchen covers Tuesday to Sunday with buckets and a drink list sized for four, The Ten Bells Brooklyn in Bushwick runs every day with oysters and tapas a few minutes from House of Yes, and Loreley on the Lower East Side pours liter steins and pitchers Monday through Thursday. We list 223 bookable happy hour bars across 50 neighborhoods.
intro:
A birthday out with friends has two problems: getting a table for everyone and keeping the tab reasonable. Bars that take reservations and also run a happy hour solve both. You lock in the space, and the first rounds cost less while people trickle in.

On our list, 223 bars with a happy hour also take bookings through Resy, OpenTable, SevenRooms or Tock, spread across 50 neighborhoods. We picked seven in seven neighborhoods and three boroughs, favoring deals that work for a group: pitchers, steins, buckets, carafes and plates meant for sharing. Each card shows the live deal, the hours and the booking link.

Below the picks: how to book, how to match the deal to the day of the week, how to split the bill without a scene, and where to go dancing when the cake is gone.

picks.why: A tiki bar on West 44th Street, four minutes from 42nd Street-Port Authority. Happy hour runs Tuesday through Sunday in the early evening, so a Saturday or Sunday birthday is covered. Zombies, frozen palomas, Hugo spritzes, wine and beer are on the list, but the group section is the reason to book: a list billed as perfect for four, with a rum drink and buckets of High Noons or Coronitas. Reservations go through Resy.

A German restaurant and biergarten on Rivington Street, two minutes from Bowery on the J and Z. Happy hour runs Monday through Thursday and lasts longest on Mondays and Tuesdays, well into the evening. For a table of friends the list is hard to beat: liter steins, beer pitchers, a Kölsch kranz, select bottles of wine and a beer flight. Bookings go through Tock, which suits a weeknight birthday.

A Bushwick bar on Irving Avenue, three minutes from Jefferson Street on the L. Its happy hour runs every day of the week into the early evening, with oysters, wine specials and Spanish tapas, and its site mentions group reservations alongside walk-ins. It is also the easiest handoff to a dance floor on this list: House of Yes is about three minutes away on foot and Elsewhere about seven.

A bar and restaurant on Second Avenue in Midtown, four minutes from 51st Street (6, E, F). It runs two happy hours: weekday afternoons into the early evening, and a second one late in the evening every night, weekends included. That late window suits a birthday that starts with dinner somewhere else. Every shareable plate is discounted, alongside two signature cocktails, drafts, wine and prosecco. Reservations go through Resy.

An Italian spot on Hudson Street, three minutes from 8th Avenue (A, C, E, L). Happy hour runs every day at the bar and in the outdoor area only, with red or white wine by the glass or carafe, beer, cocktails and bites such as bruschetta, fried zucchini, truffle fries, arancini and meatballs. Book a table through OpenTable for dinner, and start the group at the bar while the deal is on.

A gastropub on Second Avenue, four minutes from 86th Street on the Q. The weekday happy hour runs from mid-afternoon into the early evening with Penrose cocktails, pinot noir and pinot grigio, and mugs of Spaten. Its site also lists a late-night deal on select drinks every night, plus money off brunch drinks or carafes at the bar, handy for a birthday brunch. Book through Resy.

A wine and tapas restaurant on Northern Boulevard in Queens, about twelve minutes from 90th Street-Elmhurst Avenue on the 7. Happy hour runs every day from late afternoon into the early evening: sparkling, white, rosé and red wine by the glass, mimosas, and red or white sangria by the glass or pitcher, with tapas such as olives. A daily window and a sangria pitcher make it an easy weekend birthday. Bookings go through Resy.

sections.h: Booking tips for a birthday group
sections.body:
Book from the link on each card, and do it early if the birthday falls on a Friday or Saturday. Most bars on our list use Resy (152 of the 223 bookable ones) or OpenTable (57), so one account covers almost everything. Give an honest headcount: a table for eight that turns into twelve is the fastest way to lose it.

When you book, ask one question: does the happy hour apply at a reserved table? At some bars it does not. Osteria Nonnino, for example, serves its deal at the bar and in the outdoor area only, so plan to start there and move to the table for food. If you want to bring a cake, ask that too, since every bar sets its own rule.

Set the start time inside the happy hour window on the card, not at the end of it. Guests arrive late, and the first round is the one that saves the most.

sections.h: Match the day to the deal
sections.body: Weekday birthdays are easy: most happy hours run Monday through Friday. Weekends are harder. Of the 223 bookable bars with a happy hour on our list, 96 have one on Saturday or Sunday. Among our picks, Friki Tiki, The Ten Bells Brooklyn, The Horny Ram, Osteria Nonnino and Addictive Wine and Tapas all cover the weekend. For a Monday or Tuesday birthday, Loreley is the standout, with its longest window on those two nights. The Penrose is a weekday choice, though its brunch deal and nightly late-night drinks stretch it further. The Horny Ram's second window, late in the evening every night, is the one to use if the group meets after dinner. Our weekend happy hours page lists every Saturday and Sunday option.

sections.h: Splitting the bill without a scene
sections.body: Decide how you will pay before the first round. The simplest system is one tab on one card, settled by payment app at the end, with the birthday person's share split among everyone else. If the group would rather pay separately, ask the server at the start, not when the check arrives. Tip on the whole bill, including the rounds that were cheaper because of happy hour. Our guide on how much to tip at a bar in NYC covers the usual amounts. Some bars add their own fees; Addictive Wine and Tapas, for one, notes a fee on card payments on its site, so read the check before you divide it.

Three of our picks sit close to party venues on our NYC parties list. The Ten Bells Brooklyn is the clearest: House of Yes, with 15 upcoming parties on our list, is about three minutes away, Sea Wolf Bushwick about the same, and Elsewhere about seven. On the Lower East Side, Cosmo and Outer Heaven are about a minute from Loreley, and Capitale is about five. In the West Village, Common Ground Bar is roughly two minutes from Osteria Nonnino and The Standard Biergarten about four. Check each party page for the date, start time and age limit before you promise the group a dance floor. Many parties sell tickets in advance, so buy them while you are booking the table.

faq.a: Pick a bar that takes reservations and runs a happy hour on your day. Friki Tiki in Hell's Kitchen sells buckets and a drink list sized for four, and Loreley on the Lower East Side pours pitchers and liter steins, so a group round costs less than buying drink by drink.
faq.q: Where can I celebrate a birthday in NYC on a budget?

faq.a: For a group, yes, especially on a Friday or Saturday. We list 223 bars with a happy hour that take bookings, most through Resy or OpenTable, so you can lock in a table and still get the deal.
faq.q: Do I need a reservation for a birthday at a bar in NYC?

faq.a: It depends on the bar, so ask when you book. Osteria Nonnino, for example, serves its happy hour only at the bar and in the outdoor area, and the rule differs from bar to bar.
faq.q: Does happy hour apply at a reserved table?

faq.a: Friki Tiki, The Ten Bells Brooklyn, The Horny Ram, Osteria Nonnino and Addictive Wine and Tapas all run a happy hour on Saturday and Sunday. On our list, 96 of the 223 bookable happy hour bars have a weekend window.

title: Upper East Side Bar Crawl: 4 Weekday Happy Hours on First Ave
h1: Upper East Side Bar Crawl: First Avenue, 76th Street to 70th
description: An Upper East Side bar crawl for Monday to Friday: four happy hours on First Avenue between 76th and 70th Streets, about 530 meters on foot.
answer: For an Upper East Side bar crawl that stays on happy hour, go Monday through Friday and walk four stops down First Avenue: Jones Wood Foundry on East 76th Street, Sefton and Westville in the low 70s, then The Hunterian on East 70th Street. The whole route is about 530 meters, under ten minutes on foot, and all four weekday happy hours overlap in the late afternoon.
intro:
Uptown happy hours spread out, and a crawl that needs a cab between stops is not a crawl. First Avenue in the 70s is the exception: four bars with clean, recently checked happy hours sit within a few blocks of each other, so you can do the whole thing on foot and spend your time sitting rather than walking.

We started from the 30 Upper East Side bars on our list, set aside the ones with stale or unclear deal listings, and kept stops close enough to walk between in a few minutes. The four that made it run from a British gastropub on East 76th Street down to a bar on East 70th Street, with a flatbread-friendly pub and a margarita-heavy restaurant in between. Eleven bars on our list, these four included, have a happy hour within a 10-minute walk of Westville, the third stop, so there is backup if a place is full.

The pick cards below show each bar's live prices and exact hours. Use this guide for the order, the days and the walk.

picks.why: Start at Jones Wood Foundry, a British gastropub at 401 East 76th Street. Its happy hour is at the bar only, Monday to Friday, and it is the shortest window on this route, so it goes first. The deal covers all draft beers, cask ale included, house wines, and the apps and snacks menu. Reservations are on Resy if you want a table later. The 72nd Street Q station is five minutes away.

Walk about three minutes south to Sefton, a pub at 1373 First Avenue. Its weekday happy hour starts before lunch and runs into the early evening, the longest window of the four. The list covers domestic bottles, Stella or Narragansett on draft, pinot grigio, sauvignon blanc, cabernet, a Negroni, an old fashioned, a Moscow mule, margaritas and flatbreads, so this is the stop to eat. The Q at 72nd Street is three minutes away.

Westville is about a minute down the block at 1359 First Avenue. Happy hour runs every day from late afternoon into the early evening and covers classic, spicy or smoky margaritas, sangria, signature and seasonal cocktails, every wine by the glass, every beer and mocktails, which makes it the easy stop for anyone in the group not drinking. The 72nd Street Q station is three minutes away.

Finish around the corner at The Hunterian, on East 70th Street just east of First Avenue. From Tuesday to Sunday its happy hour runs from opening until the early evening, and on Mondays it lasts all day. The deal is simple: money off draft beer, plus wine by the glass and well shots and drinks at happy hour prices. The Q at 72nd Street is five minutes away.

sections.body:
Monday through Friday. Jones Wood Foundry and Sefton only run happy hour on weekdays, while Westville and The Hunterian run every day, so a weekend version loses half the route. Monday is a quietly good choice: The Hunterian keeps its deal going all day that day, so a slow finish still lands on happy hour.

The order follows the clock. Jones Wood Foundry has the shortest window and closes first, so it opens the crawl in the late afternoon. Sefton has been on happy hour since before lunch, and Westville and The Hunterian both carry into the early evening, so the last three stops give you some slack. Plan on about 40 minutes per stop and you will finish as the final windows close. The exact start and end times are on each pick card.

From Jones Wood Foundry on East 76th Street, walk about 200 meters to Sefton, roughly three minutes. Westville is only about 70 meters further down First Avenue, a one-minute hop. The last leg, to The Hunterian on East 70th Street, is about 260 meters, three to four minutes. In total that is about 530 meters, which leaves almost all of the evening for sitting down.

The drinks change as you go. Jones Wood Foundry is the beer stop, with cask ale and every draft on the deal. Sefton is the food stop, with flatbreads next to cocktails and wine. Westville is margaritas, sangria and mocktails. The Hunterian closes with a plain deal on drafts, wine and well drinks. Our distances are straight lines between each bar's coordinates at about 80 meters a minute, so add a little for crossing First Avenue.

The Q's 72nd Street station on Second Avenue is the anchor for this route. Our listings put it three minutes from Sefton and Westville and five from Jones Wood Foundry and The Hunterian, so you can arrive and leave from the same station without doubling back far.

If you would rather start further north, Second Avenue from the 70s into the 80s has more happy hours on our list, but several of those listings were out of date or unclear when we built this route, so we could not vouch for the deals. First Avenue was the one stretch where four reliable deals line up within a few minutes of each other.

On a Saturday or Sunday, keep Westville and The Hunterian and add The Alvin Public House on East 64th Street, which runs happy hour every day in the late afternoon and is about six minutes south of The Hunterian. Further north, Third Avenue Ale House near East 92nd Street runs a weekend daytime window and a late happy hour every night of the week, a useful backup if you are out after dark. For everything else, see the Upper East Side happy hours page, or use the live table below, which lists every happy hour within a 10-minute walk of the route, closest first.

faq.a: Monday through Friday. All four stops on this First Avenue route run happy hour on weekdays, and on Mondays The Hunterian's deal lasts all day. On weekends only Westville and The Hunterian keep a window.
faq.q: Which day works for an Upper East Side bar crawl?

faq.a: About two and a half to three hours. The walking adds up to roughly 530 meters, under ten minutes, so most of the time is spent at the four bars, about 40 minutes each.
faq.q: How long does the crawl take?

faq.a: 72nd Street on the Q. Our listings put it three minutes from Sefton and Westville and five from Jones Wood Foundry and The Hunterian.
faq.q: Which subway station is closest?

faq.a: Not as written. On Saturday or Sunday, pair Westville and The Hunterian with The Alvin Public House on East 64th Street, which runs happy hour every day.
faq.q: Can I do this crawl on a weekend?

faq.a: No. Jones Wood Foundry's deal is at the bar, so walk in and take a bar seat. It also takes Resy bookings if you want a table after the crawl.
faq.q: Do I need reservations?

faq.a: Sefton, the second stop. Its happy hour includes margherita, prosciutto or vegetable flatbreads, and Jones Wood Foundry's deal covers its apps and snacks menu.

title: Upper West Side Bar Crawl: 5 Weekday Happy Hour Stops
h1: An Upper West Side bar crawl on Amsterdam and Columbus
description: An upper west side bar crawl for Monday to Friday: five happy hours on Amsterdam and Columbus Avenues, about 13 minutes of walking from start to finish.
answer: For an upper west side bar crawl that stays on happy hour, go Monday to Friday and walk five stops in this order: Playa Betty's on Amsterdam Avenue, Asset and Da Capo facing each other on Columbus Avenue, then The Wolfe and Hi Life Bar & Grill back on Amsterdam. The route covers about a kilometer, roughly 13 minutes on foot, and starts three minutes from the 72nd Street 1, 2 and 3 station.
intro:
The Upper West Side does not have one nightlife strip, which is why a crawl here needs a plan. The happy hours sit along Amsterdam and Columbus Avenues, a block apart, and they keep different hours. We started from the 39 Upper West Side bars and restaurants on our list, kept the ones whose happy hour runs on the same weekdays and has a posted menu, and ordered them so the earliest window comes first and the latest last.

The result is a zigzag north: a Mexican spot on Amsterdam, a pair of restaurants across Columbus from each other, a pub and a bar with oysters to close. You get beer, margaritas, wine, cocktails and real food along the way, with no leg longer than about six minutes.

Live prices and each bar's exact hours are on the cards below. Use this guide for the order, the days and the walking, and check the cards on the day you go.

picks.why: Start at Playa Betty's, a Mexican restaurant at 320 Amsterdam Avenue. Its happy hour runs every day and opens earliest of the five, in the middle of the afternoon, and it closes in the early evening, so this is the stop to hit first. The menu lists Pacifico pints, rose and Betty's Burger, a good base for the walk ahead. The 72nd Street station on the 1, 2 and 3 is a three-minute walk.

Walk about four minutes east to Asset at 329 Columbus Avenue. Its happy hour runs Monday to Friday and is one of the two shortest windows on the route, ending at the same time as Playa Betty's, so do not linger at the first stop. The menu covers select starters, signature cocktails, selected wines and craft taps, which makes Asset the place to eat something early.

Da Capo is directly across Columbus Avenue at number 322, about 30 meters away. It is an American and Italian bar whose weekday happy hour starts latest of the five, in the early evening, which is why it comes third. The list is short and leans on cocktails: a limoncello spritz and a Taylor Who vodka drink. Da Capo also takes bookings on Resy if you want a table later.

Head back to Amsterdam Avenue and north about six minutes to The Wolfe, a pub at 425 Amsterdam Avenue. Its happy hour runs Monday to Friday from late morning into the early evening, the longest window on the route, with beer, draft, mixed drinks and an Aperol drink on the list. It is the cheap-beer stop of the night. The 79th Street station on the 1 is three minutes away.

Finish about three minutes north at Hi Life Bar & Grill, 477 Amsterdam Avenue. Its happy hour runs every day and ends with The Wolfe's, so arrive with time to spare. The list is the longest of the night: well drinks, margaritas and daiquiris, cosmopolitans, champagne cocktails, house wine, select draft pints and Blue Point oysters by the piece. The 86th Street station on the 1 is four minutes away.

sections.body:
Monday through Friday. Asset, Da Capo and The Wolfe run happy hour on weekdays only, while Playa Betty's and Hi Life run every day, so any weekday covers all five stops. Saturday and Sunday break the middle of the route.

The order follows the clock. Playa Betty's opens its window first, in the middle of the afternoon, and closes in the early evening along with Asset, which is why those two lead. Da Capo starts later, so it sits third. The Wolfe and Hi Life end together in the early evening, so leave Da Capo with time for both. Plan on about 40 minutes per stop and one round at each. If you start late, skip Playa Betty's and open at Asset. If you only have an hour, do Da Capo, The Wolfe and Hi Life. Exact start and end times are on the cards, and they are what to check before you go.

From Playa Betty's on Amsterdam Avenue to Asset on Columbus Avenue is about 310 meters, around four minutes. Da Capo is across the avenue, about 30 meters away. The longest leg follows: about 490 meters back to Amsterdam and north to The Wolfe, roughly six minutes. The last leg to Hi Life is about 200 meters, under three minutes.

In total that is about 1,030 meters, or around 13 minutes of walking spread over the evening. We measure straight-line distance between each bar's coordinates at about 80 meters a minute, so allow a little more for corners and lights. The mix runs from Pacifico and a burger at Playa Betty's to starters and craft taps at Asset, a spritz at Da Capo, cheap beer at The Wolfe and oysters at Hi Life.

Take the 1, 2 or 3 to 72nd Street; our listing puts Playa Betty's three minutes from the station. The B and C also stop at 72nd Street, a minute from The Ribbon on West 72nd Street.

The route ends near the 1 train. The 79th Street station is three minutes from The Wolfe, and 86th Street is four minutes from Hi Life, so you can head home without walking back to the start.

sections.h: If your day does not fit
sections.body:
On a weekend, build a shorter version from the bars with daily windows. Playa Betty's and Hi Life both keep their happy hour on Saturday and Sunday. The Ribbon on West 72nd Street, a minute from the B and C, also runs every day, with a margarita, a UWS Negroni, well drinks, draft and fish tacos on its list. Hoptimist, across Amsterdam Avenue from The Wolfe, adds Saturday to its weekday window, with truffle fries and a baked pretzel.

The table below lists 22 other happy hours within about a 10-minute walk of Asset, closest first, if you want to swap a stop.

faq.a: Any weekday, Monday to Friday. All five stops run happy hour on those days. On Saturday and Sunday only Playa Betty's and Hi Life keep their windows, so the full route does not work.
faq.q: Which day should I do an Upper West Side bar crawl?

faq.a: About three to three and a half hours with one round at each stop. The walking adds up to about 13 minutes over roughly 1,030 meters, starting in the afternoon and finishing in the early evening.
faq.q: How long does the crawl take?

faq.a: Asset or Playa Betty's. Asset's happy hour includes select starters, Playa Betty's has a burger, and Hi Life serves Blue Point oysters by the piece at the last stop.
faq.q: Where should I eat on the route?

faq.a: No, but Da Capo takes bookings on Resy if you want a table later. The other four have no booking link in our listing, so walk in and take a bar seat.

faq.a: Start at 72nd Street on the 1, 2 and 3, three minutes from Playa Betty's. Finish at 86th Street on the 1, four minutes from Hi Life.

title: Greenpoint Bar Crawl: 4 Weekday Happy Hours Off the G
h1: A Greenpoint bar crawl around Greenpoint Avenue
description: A greenpoint bar crawl for Monday to Friday: four happy hours near the Greenpoint Avenue G stop, about 11 minutes of walking, with tacos and margaritas.
answer: For a greenpoint bar crawl on happy hour, go Monday to Friday and walk four stops: Troost and Papacito's, next door to each other on Manhattan Avenue, then west to Panzón on Greenpoint Avenue and back east to Black Rabbit. The loop is under 900 meters, about 11 minutes on foot, and every stop is within a six-minute walk of the Greenpoint Avenue G station.
intro:
Greenpoint is small and walkable, and its happy hours sit in two clusters: one around the Greenpoint Avenue G stop and one down on Nassau Avenue by McCarren Park. Of the 12 Greenpoint bars on our list, four line up neatly near the northern stop, with windows that run on the same weekdays and hand off from one to the next. That is this crawl.

It is a short one. Four stops, under a kilometer of walking, and a mix that goes from a cocktail and wine bar to two-for-one frozen margaritas, a Mexican kitchen with tacos and adobo fries, and a house lager to finish. We kept the route inside Greenpoint, so there is no need to cross into Williamsburg.

Live prices and each bar's exact hours are on the cards below. Use this guide for the order, the days and the walking, and check the cards on the day you go.

picks.why: Start at Troost, a bar at 1011 Manhattan Avenue. Its happy hour runs every day and ends earliest of the four, in the early evening, so it has to come first. The deal is money off beer, cocktails and house wine by the glass or quartino, plus a tap Negroni at a set price. Our listing tags it for cocktails and wine. The Greenpoint Avenue G station is a three-minute walk.

Papacito's is next door at 999 Manhattan Avenue, under a minute's walk. Its afternoon happy hour runs every day, with two-for-one frozen margaritas, cans of Tecate or Modelo Especial, house margaritas, pints of sangria, a tequila shot with a Tecate, and regular or meat nachos. It also runs a weekday taco deal at lunch and another in the last hour of every night, if you come back later.

Walk about seven minutes west along Greenpoint Avenue to Panzón, a Mexican bar and restaurant at number 23. Its happy hour runs weekdays only and starts later than Troost's and Papacito's, in the late afternoon, which is why it sits third. Expect margaritas, non-alcoholic cocktails, Victoria beer, money off draft beer and wine, single tacos and adobo fries. Panzón takes bookings on Resy if your group wants a table.

Finish about four minutes back east at Black Rabbit, 91 Greenpoint Avenue. Its happy hour runs every day and lasts the longest into the evening of the four, so it is the natural last stop. The deal is simple: the bar's own Black Rabbit Lager, and our listing tags it for cheap beer. The Greenpoint Avenue G station is a three-minute walk, so the ride home is easy.

sections.body:
Monday through Friday. Panzón runs happy hour on weekdays only, while Troost, Papacito's and Black Rabbit run every day, so any weekday covers all four stops. On Saturday and Sunday, skip Panzón and do the other three, which are all within about five minutes of each other.

The order follows the clock. Troost's window ends first, so start there in the late afternoon. Papacito's next door runs a little longer. Panzón starts its window later than the first two, so walk over once it opens, and Black Rabbit runs the latest into the evening, which makes it the place to finish. Plan on about 40 minutes per stop and one round at each, which puts the whole crawl at around three hours. The exact start and end times for every window are on the cards, and they are the thing to check before you set out.

Troost to Papacito's is about 40 meters, a few doors along Manhattan Avenue. From Papacito's to Panzón is the longest leg, about 550 meters west toward the river along Greenpoint Avenue, roughly seven minutes. The last leg back to Black Rabbit is about 280 meters, around four minutes.

Add it up and the crawl is about 870 meters of walking, roughly 11 minutes on your feet. Our distances are straight lines between each bar's coordinates at about 80 meters a minute, so allow a minute here and there for corners and crossings.

The mix is the point. You get a Negroni or a glass of wine at Troost, frozen margaritas and nachos at Papacito's, tacos and adobo fries at Panzón, and a house lager at Black Rabbit. If you want to eat properly, Panzón is the stop to do it.

Take the G to Greenpoint Avenue. Our listings put Troost, Papacito's and Black Rabbit three minutes from the station and Panzón about six, so you start and finish at the same stop without doubling back on a long walk.

If you are coming from the south end of the neighborhood, the Nassau Avenue station on the G sits by the second cluster of happy hours, described below.

The Nassau Avenue side of Greenpoint, near McCarren Park, has its own weekday happy hours. Ray's on Lorimer Street runs Monday to Friday with well shots, beer, house cocktails, a burger, a martini with fries and hot wings. Raizes Churrascaria on Nassau Avenue runs a long weekday window with draft beer, well drinks and sangria by the pitcher, and Keg & Lantern, also on Nassau Avenue, has draft beer on its list. From Black Rabbit, Ray's is about 840 meters south, roughly 10 minutes on foot, but its window ends before Black Rabbit's, so the Nassau Avenue bars suit a separate weekday rather than a fifth stop. For a longer night across the border, our Williamsburg bar crawl picks up farther south. The table below lists every happy hour within a 10-minute walk of Papacito's, closest first.

faq.a: Any weekday, Monday to Friday. All four stops run happy hour on those days. On weekends Panzón has no happy hour, so do Troost, Papacito's and Black Rabbit instead.
faq.q: Which day should I do a Greenpoint bar crawl?

faq.a: About three hours with one round at each of the four stops. The walking adds up to roughly 11 minutes over about 870 meters, from the late afternoon into the evening.
faq.q: How long does the crawl take?

faq.a: Panzón and Papacito's. Panzón's happy hour includes single tacos and adobo fries, and Papacito's has regular and meat nachos plus taco deals at lunch and late at night.
faq.q: Where can I eat on the route?

faq.a: No. Panzón takes bookings on Resy if you want a table for a group; the other three have no booking link in our listing, so just walk in.
faq.q: Do I need reservations?

faq.a: Greenpoint Avenue on the G. Troost, Papacito's and Black Rabbit are three minutes from it and Panzón about six, so the same station works for the start and the finish.

title: Margarita Happy Hour NYC: 8 Bars With Margs on the Deal
h1: Margarita happy hour NYC: where the margarita is on the menu
description: Margarita happy hour NYC guide: 8 bars in Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx that list a margarita on their happy hour, with days and subway tips.
answer: For a margarita happy hour NYC locals actually use, start with Mad Dog and Beans in the Financial District or Croton Reservoir Tavern by Bryant Park on a weekday, Toast in Morningside Heights or La Loncheria in Bushwick on any day of the week, and Riviera Maya in Astoria on a Tuesday, when its deal runs all day. Rosa's At Park in Mott Haven covers the Bronx, with Monday and Wednesday happy hours that last all day.
intro:
Plenty of bars say they do drinks specials. Fewer put a margarita on the happy hour list by name. Of the 685 bars we track, 85 list a margarita as an item in their happy hour offers, and dozens more only mention one somewhere in the fine print. This guide is built from that first group: every pick below has the margarita written into its own happy hour menu.

Manhattan holds most of them, 56 of the 85. Brooklyn has 15, Queens 10, and the Bronx and Staten Island two each. By neighborhood, Midtown leads with nine, Astoria follows with six, and the Financial District, Hell's Kitchen, the Upper West Side and the Upper East Side each have five.

The eight picks span four boroughs and are grouped by area. Cards carry live prices and hours; the text covers the kind of margarita, the days and the train.

picks.why: Mad Dog and Beans is a Mexican restaurant on Pearl Street that runs its happy hour Monday through Thursday, from mid-afternoon into the early evening, at the bar only. The drinks list is short and margarita heavy: the house signature margarita on the rocks, a frozen margarita, house wine and Mexican beer. Whitehall Street-South Ferry on the 1, R and W is a three-minute walk, handy before a ferry.

Croton Reservoir Tavern is a pub on West 40th Street, a minute from the 42nd Street-Bryant Park station on the 7, B, D, F and M. Its Tuesday to Friday happy hour is served in The Speakeasy on the lower level, or upstairs when that room is booked. There are two margaritas, a classic and a mango habanero, plus an old fashioned, a Manhattan, sangria, an Aperol spritz, wine, draft beer and well drinks.

Toast, on Broadway two minutes from the 125th Street station on the 1, pours frozen margaritas in a 12-ounce size every day of the week. The afternoon window covers drinks and bites, and a second weekday window late in the evening is drinks only. House red and white, well drinks, flavored martinis and money off drafts round it out. The deals are for dine-in guests, so take a seat.

Rosa's At Park sits on Park Avenue in Mott Haven, two minutes from 138th Street-Grand Concourse on the 4 and 5. Its happy hour lasts all day on Monday and Wednesday, and runs late afternoon into early evening on Tuesday, Thursday and Friday. Margaritas share a line with mojitos, next to classics such as a martini, mule, rum punch and pina colada, plus wine, well drinks, well shots, and Corona, Heineken or Modelo Especial.

Alta Calidad is a Mexican restaurant on Vanderbilt Avenue with a Monday to Thursday happy hour from mid-afternoon to early evening. The drink to order is the Margarita Calidad. The list also has a michelada, a Tecate with a tequila shot and a Los Conejos Malditos wine, and the botanas include salsas and chips, spinach queso fundido, nachos, a quesadilla and yuca fries. Clinton-Washington Avenues on the C is five minutes away.

La Loncheria on Wilson Avenue runs its happy hour every day of the week, late afternoon into early evening, which makes it the easy weekend pick on this list. The menu names both a margarita and a spicy cucumber margarita, alongside house wine, red sangria, tequila and a taco. Morgan Avenue on the L is a six-minute walk, so it works as a first stop on a Bushwick night.

Hellbender on Forest Avenue opens its weekday happy hour menu with three margaritas, each with a half salt rim: a classic, a pineapple margarita, and a margarita topped with club soda for something lighter. A wine by the glass follows on the list. The window is short and lands right after work, so arrive on time. Forest Avenue on the M is a three-minute walk, and the restaurant takes reservations.

Riviera Maya is a Mexican and Latin bar on Steinway Street with one of the longer windows on our list. On Sunday, Monday and Wednesday through Friday, happy hour runs from midday into the early evening, and on Tuesday it lasts all day. Frozen and classic margaritas lead the list, with sangrias, a chilcano, a passion fruit pisco sour and beer. The 30th Avenue N and W station is eight minutes away.

sections.h: Frozen, spicy or classic: what the menus say
sections.body:
Most bars on our list just write margarita, which usually means the house version on the rocks. Ten bars name a frozen margarita on their happy hour. Here that means Mad Dog and Beans, Toast and Riviera Maya, and Papacito's in Greenpoint pours its frozen one two for one.

Eleven bars name a spicy version or one with a hot pepper in it. On this list, La Loncheria has the spicy cucumber margarita and Croton Reservoir Tavern has the mango habanero. Off the list, Barfly in Gramercy does a spicy margarita with a salted rim, and The Bonnie in Astoria saves its spicy margarita for the late window.

Flavors are rarer and more fun. Hellbender does pineapple, Siren in Park Slope and Chateau 49 in Midtown do hibiscus, and Saar Indian Restaurant near Times Square lists tamarind, mango, coconut, peach and strawberry versions next to the regular one.

Downtown, the Financial District has five, so Mad Dog and Beans has company near Wall Street. In Midtown, the leader with nine, Croton Reservoir Tavern sits near Bryant Park, and the Mad Dog & Beans Mexican Cantina in Midtown lists the same signature and frozen margaritas as the downtown location. Uptown, Toast covers Morningside Heights and Harlem, and Rosa's At Park brings the Bronx in, right by the 4 and 5.

In Brooklyn, Alta Calidad works for Prospect Heights and Clinton Hill, and La Loncheria works for Bushwick. In Queens, Astoria has six margarita bars, more than any neighborhood outside Manhattan, and Hellbender gives Ridgewood its own stop on the M.

Weekdays are easy. Most of the 85 bars run their deal Monday through Friday or close to it, and Tuesday through Thursday is the safest bet. Weekends are harder: 37 of the 85 have a happy hour on Saturday or Sunday. On this list, La Loncheria and Toast run every day, and Riviera Maya runs on Sunday.

A few bars build a margarita day into the week. Riviera Maya runs its whole happy hour all day on Tuesday. Rosa's At Park does the same on Monday and Wednesday. Linen Hall near Union Square puts margaritas on its Tuesday special, and La Caverna on the Lower East Side adds margaritas to its Taco Tuesday menu. If you are flexible, pick the day first and the bar second.

Read the small print on the card. Mad Dog and Beans serves its deal at the bar only, Toast's is for dine-in guests, and Croton Reservoir Tavern serves its downstairs unless the room is booked for a private event. Alta Calidad, Croton Reservoir Tavern, Hellbender and Rosa's At Park all have a booking link on the card if you want a table. For a group, look for bigger formats. La Caverna lists a margarita tower on its happy hour, and Deja Vu New York in Astoria lists margarita pitchers. If your crowd wants food with the margaritas, our guide to Taco Tuesday in NYC covers bars where tacos are on the same happy hour.

faq.a: La Loncheria in Bushwick and Toast in Morningside Heights run their margarita happy hours every day, including Saturday and Sunday. Riviera Maya in Astoria runs on Sunday. In total, 37 of the 85 bars on our list with a margarita on the happy hour have a weekend window.
faq.q: Where can I get a margarita at happy hour in NYC on the weekend?

faq.a: Ten bars on our list name a frozen margarita on their happy hour, including Mad Dog and Beans in the Financial District, Toast in Morningside Heights, Riviera Maya in Astoria and Papacito's in Greenpoint, which pours its frozen margarita two for one.
faq.q: Which NYC happy hours have frozen margaritas?
