title: Wings Happy Hour NYC: 8 Bars With Wings on the Deal
h1: Wings happy hour NYC: where wings are on the happy hour menu
description: Wings happy hour NYC guide: 8 bars in Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx that put wings on the happy hour, plus which ones fit game days.
answer: For a wings happy hour NYC sports fans can plan around, The Dawson 39 near Bryant Park runs its deal all day on Saturday and Sunday, Asia Roma in Chinatown sells wings by the piece every day, and Oliver's Astoria adds a late window every night. On weekdays, Grand Street Social in SoHo, The Whiskey in Williamsburg, Krupa Grocery in Park Slope and Kingsbridge Social Club in the Bronx all list wings on the happy hour.
intro:
Wings are one of the most common foods on a New York happy hour menu, and one of the easiest to compare. We searched the offers of the 685 bars on our list: 34 name wings as a happy hour item, and more mention them somewhere in the text around the deal. Manhattan has 19 of the 34, Brooklyn 11, Queens two, and the Bronx and Staten Island one each.

The styles vary more than you might expect. You will find classic buffalo, a jerk and BBQ choice, Calabrian honey, Alabama white BBQ and wings sold one piece at a time. Some bars pair them with a beer and a shot; others treat them as a dinner starter next to oysters or croquettes.

The eight picks below cover four boroughs and both kinds of night out: a weekday after-work snack and a weekend game. Cards show live prices and hours; the text tells you what kind of wings to expect, which days they run and where to get off the train.

picks.why: The Dawson 39 is an Irish restaurant and sports bar on West 39th Street, two minutes from 42nd Street-Bryant Park. Happy hour starts at midday on weekdays and lasts all day on Saturday and Sunday, which makes it the game-day pick here. Wings sit on the small plates list with nachos, guac and chips and cauliflower bites. To drink: house wine, spritzes, bottled Bud and Coors Light, and drafts such as Yuengling, Blue Moon and Miller Lite.

Grand Street Social, at 155 Grand Street in SoHo, runs a weekday happy hour that is mostly a bar food menu. Buffalo hot wings come with company: chicken tenders, truffle and parmesan fries, a giant pretzel, fried calamari, roast pork tacos, mozzarella sticks, a hot dog and half dozens of Bluepoint oysters. Canal Street, served by the 6, J, N, Q, R, W and Z, is two minutes away and has an accessible entrance.

Asia Roma on Mulberry Street prices its happy hour by the piece, every day of the week, from mid-afternoon to early evening. Fried chicken wings are sold one at a time, so you can order exactly as many as you want. The same menu has pork and shrimp dumplings, spring rolls, satay, clams casino, grilled shrimp skewers and Blue Point oysters, which come with a six-piece minimum. Canal Street is a five-minute walk.

Cocteleria Perla Negra on Broadway runs happy hour Tuesday through Sunday, late afternoon into early evening, so it covers a Sunday afternoon too. The menu is short: an order of six chicken wings and New Brunswick oysters by the half dozen or dozen, with Champagne mignonette and cocktail sauce. The bar also notes Taco Tuesday all day and a Wine Wednesday deal on bottles. 137th Street-City College on the 1 is four minutes away.

The Whiskey on Grand Street keeps its happy hour going all day and night on Monday, then until the evening Tuesday through Friday. Wings share the list with a beer and a shot (a Narragansett or a Coors Light pony with a well shot, plus an optional pickle or spicy back), well drinks, wine and a cheeseburger with a beer. Metropolitan Avenue on the G and L is three minutes away.

Krupa Grocery sits on Prospect Park West, a minute from the 15th Street-Prospect Park station on the F and G. Its happy hour is a short snack menu Monday through Thursday in the late afternoon. The crispy chicken wings come with Alabama white BBQ sauce, and the same list has house-made chicken nuggets, salt cod croquettes, risotto balls, blistered shishitos and spicy boiled peanuts. It is a food deal, so pair it with the wine list.

Oliver's Astoria, on Broadway at 38th Street, runs two windows: weekdays from late afternoon into the evening, and every night of the week from late evening until close. Jumbo chicken wings are on its select apps list with dilly chips, buffalo chicken empanadas and mozzarella sticks. Signature cocktails and a cold Miller High Life with an optional house shot cover the drinks. Steinway Street on the M and R is three minutes away.

Kingsbridge Social Club is an Italian-leaning spot on Kingsbridge Avenue in the Bronx, a minute from 238th Street on the 1. Its weekday happy hour runs from mid-afternoon to early evening. The wings are Calabrian honey wings served with an Italian-style ranch, and the menu adds meatballs with garlic bread, a fried eggplant roll-up and pizza fritte. Draft beer, wine and sangria all get money off.

sections.body: If you want wings with a game on, start with the weekend. Only six of the 34 bars with wings on the happy hour run a deal on Saturday or Sunday. The Dawson 39 is the one tagged as a sports bar, and its weekend window runs all day. Asia Roma runs every day, Cocteleria Perla Negra runs through Sunday, and Oliver's Astoria has a late window every night, which suits a game that ends after dark. For a weeknight game, The Whiskey's all-day Monday happy hour and Oliver's late window are the two picks that keep going once the after-work rush is over. For more screens and a deeper list of game-day bars, see our guide on where to watch football in NYC and the sports bar happy hours page.

Wings are mostly a weekday deal. Of the 34 bars, 23 run their happy hour on all five weekdays, and a few skip Monday or Friday, so check the card for your day. Krupa Grocery stops after Thursday, and Cocteleria Perla Negra does not run on Monday.

Three bars on our list name a wing night on Wednesday in their happy hour text: Nostrand Station Bar & Lounge in Crown Heights calls it Wing Wednesday, Dylan Murphy's on the Upper East Side calls it Wild Wing Wednesday, and The Commissioner in Park Slope pairs wings with wine. If you are choosing a night for wings, Wednesday gives you those three on top of the regular weekday list.

sections.h: Styles and how they are sold
sections.body: Most bars list wings by the order, often a plate of six or ten. Asia Roma is the exception, with wings priced by the piece, so it works for one person or a table of eight. Sauces tell you what kind of bar you are in: buffalo at Grand Street Social, Calabrian honey at Kingsbridge Social Club, Alabama white BBQ at Krupa Grocery, and a jerk or BBQ choice at Patrick's on the Hill in Harlem. A few nearby options if your pick is full. Carneval, a few doors down Grand Street from The Whiskey, serves wings with fries in sweet chili, BBQ, guava or buffalo, and notes that a gratuity is included in every bill. On Staten Island, Piccolino Restaurant in Great Kills lists chicken wings with fries on its bar-only happy hour. Our cheap happy hour food guide has more bar snacks beyond wings.

faq.a: The Dawson 39 near Bryant Park runs its happy hour all day on Saturday and Sunday, and Asia Roma in Chinatown sells wings by the piece every day. Cocteleria Perla Negra in Harlem runs through Sunday, and Oliver's Astoria has a late window every night. Only six of the 34 bars with wings on the happy hour have a weekend window.
faq.q: Which NYC bars have wings at happy hour on the weekend?

faq.a: Yes. Three bars on our list name a wing night on Wednesday: Nostrand Station Bar & Lounge in Crown Heights (Wing Wednesday), Dylan Murphy's on the Upper East Side (Wild Wing Wednesday) and The Commissioner in Park Slope (Wine & Wing Wednesday).
faq.q: Is there a Wing Wednesday in NYC?

faq.a: Oliver's Astoria is the clearest option: its late happy hour runs every night of the week until close, and jumbo chicken wings are on the menu. The Whiskey in Williamsburg runs its happy hour all day and night on Monday.
faq.q: Where can I get wings at happy hour after a late game?

faq.a: On our list of 685 bars, 34 name wings as a happy hour item. Manhattan has 19, Brooklyn 11, Queens two, and the Bronx and Staten Island one each.
faq.q: How many NYC bars have wings on the happy hour?

faq.a: Yes. In Brooklyn, try The Whiskey in Williamsburg or Krupa Grocery in Park Slope. In Queens, Oliver's Astoria has jumbo wings, and in the Bronx, Kingsbridge Social Club serves Calabrian honey wings by the 238th Street station on the 1.
faq.q: Are there wings happy hours outside Manhattan?

title: Is Happy Hour Legal in New York? The Rules, Explained
h1: Is happy hour legal in New York? What the law allows and bans
keyword: is happy hour legal in new york
description: Is happy hour legal in New York? Yes. What state law and the SLA allow, what they ban, and what 685 NYC happy hours actually offer.
answer: Is happy hour legal in New York? Yes: bars can sell drinks for less during set hours, and 2-for-1 or half-price specials are allowed as long as no drink costs less than half the bar's regular price for it. State law bans unlimited drinks for a fixed price, and the State Liquor Authority also rules out free drinks and deals it sees as a way around that ban. In NYC, Sojourn Social on the Upper East Side runs a 2-for-1 on weekdays and VERS in Hell's Kitchen offers buy-one-get-one well drinks every day.
intro:
Visitors from places with strict rules on drink specials often ask whether a New York happy hour is even allowed. It is. New York does not ban cheaper drinks at set times. What it bans is a short list of promotions, written into the state's Alcoholic Beverage Control Law and spelled out by the State Liquor Authority (SLA), the agency that licenses every bar and restaurant that pours.

Below: what section 117-a of that law says, what the SLA allows and forbids, what that means when you order, and what the 685 happy hours on our list actually offer. The five picks each show one legal shape of a deal, from 2-for-1 rounds to money off and set happy hour prices. Their hours and prices sit on the cards, which update from each bar's own site.

picks.why: Sojourn Social, a restaurant on Second Avenue, runs one of the clearest 2-for-1 deals on our list: mix and match signature cocktails, draft beer and wine by the glass, Monday to Friday from lunchtime into the early evening. Small plates such as a shrimp taco, a cheeseburger slider and a black bean tostada come at a set price, plus burger-and-cocktail combos. It takes reservations, and the Q at 86th Street is a three-minute walk.

Blue Ribbon Sushi Bar at 30 Rockefeller Plaza pairs a set price on hand rolls with 2-for-1 select sake and beer, Monday to Friday from mid-afternoon into the early evening. It is a sushi bar first, so the deal doubles as a light meal before a show or after a walk around Rockefeller Center. The B, D, F and M at 47th-50th Streets-Rockefeller Center are a two-minute walk.

VERS on Ninth Avenue runs happy hour every day of the week until the early evening. Its posted deal combines a set price on its martini and margarita with buy-one-get-one well drinks and cheaper appetizers, which makes it one of the few places on our list with a 2-for-1 that also runs on Saturday and Sunday. It takes Resy bookings, and the C and E at 50th Street are a three-minute walk.

Papacito's on Manhattan Avenue shows how far a time-limited deal can stretch: it runs up to three happy hours. Weekday lunch brings cheap tacos. The main window, every afternoon, adds a 2-for-1 frozen margarita, house margaritas, sangria, Tecate and Modelo cans, a tequila-and-Tecate combo and nachos. The last hour of every night brings tacos again. The G at Greenpoint Avenue is a three-minute walk.

Cozy Corner in Ridgewood keeps it simple: money off select bottled and draft beers and off an Aperol or Campari spritz, every day from late afternoon into the evening. The freebie here is food, not alcohol: a slice of pizza when you buy a qualifying drink. The kitchen also turns out margherita pizza, fries and mozzarella sticks. The M at Forest Avenue is a six-minute walk.

sections.body:
The rule lives in section 117-a of New York's Alcoholic Beverage Control Law, titled "Unlimited drink offerings prohibited." It says no licensee, acting alone or together with other licensees, may offer, sell, serve or deliver unlimited drinks during a set period of time for a fixed price. The ban also covers a bar letting a party organizer or promoter run that kind of offer.

The same section lets the SLA bar specials it judges to be a way around the rule: free drinks, several drinks for free or for the price of one, or a low starting price that goes up by the hour. Two things sit outside it: private functions not open to the public, such as weddings, banquets and receptions, and a package of food and drinks where the alcohol is incidental to the event.

sections.h: What the State Liquor Authority allows
sections.body:
The SLA's guidance for bars fills in the detail. It allows 2-for-1 or half-price specials as long as no drink is priced lower than one-half of that bar's regular price for the same drink, and it has generally treated anything cheaper as an attempt to get around the law. Its license quick references also answer whether a bar can simply hand a customer a free drink: no, that too violates the unlimited drink offering law. A 2026 SLA advisory on the new for-profit club license repeats the same limits, including no more than two drinks for the price of one.

The SLA lists unlimited drink specials among the most frequent violations it finds at bars, and it can fine a licensee or suspend, cancel or revoke its license. One more rule matters on a busy night: it is a crime to sell, deliver or give away alcohol to a person who is visibly intoxicated, and the licensee answers for it whether the owner or an employee did the pouring.

sections.h: What that means at the bar
sections.body: In practice, a legal New York happy hour is a lower price per drink for a limited window. You pay for each round, even at a 2-for-1 bar. If a bartender will not comp a drink for your birthday, that is the law at work, not bad service. Other limits you will run into are house rules. Many bars keep the deal to the bar seats or the bar area, skip weekends or exclude some drinks, and none of that comes from section 117-a, which deals with unlimited and free drinks. Staff can also stop serving you when you have had enough, because of the visibly intoxicated rule above. Tip on the drinks you order; our guide to tipping at NYC bars covers how much.

sections.h: How NYC happy hours actually look
sections.body: We went through the happy hours of all 685 bars on our list. 434 post item-level deals, and a set happy hour price is by far the most common form: 367 bars list at least one drink or dish at a fixed happy hour price. Money off the regular price shows up at 45 bars, a share off the regular price at 28, and a 2-for-1 at only 9. Food is part of the deal at 241 bars. The fine print is mostly about place and time. 66 bars say their deal applies only at the bar, in the bar area or for dine-in. 191 run happy hour every day of the week, and 78 run more than one window, such as an afternoon slot plus a late one. For when these windows open and close, see what time happy hour is in NYC, and happy hour now shows what is running at the moment you open it.

faq.a: Yes. New York allows bars to lower drink prices for a set period. What state law bans is unlimited drinks for a fixed price, plus free drinks and similar workarounds, under section 117-a of the Alcoholic Beverage Control Law.
faq.q: Is happy hour legal in New York?

faq.a: Yes, within a limit. The State Liquor Authority allows 2-for-1 or half-price specials as long as no drink is priced below one-half of the bar's regular price for the same drink. Offers of more than two drinks for the price of one are not allowed.
faq.q: Are 2-for-1 drink specials legal in New York?

faq.a: Not as a public promotion. Section 117-a bars unlimited drinks for a fixed price during a set period. Private functions that are not open to the public, such as weddings and banquets, and food-and-drink packages where alcohol is incidental to the event are exempt.
faq.q: Are bottomless or open-bar drink deals legal in New York?

faq.a: No. The State Liquor Authority says giving a patron a free drink also violates the unlimited drink offering law. A free snack or slice with a drink, like Cozy Corner's pizza, is food, not alcohol.
faq.q: Can a New York bartender give me a free drink?

faq.a: That is the bar's own policy. Section 117-a deals with unlimited and free drinks, not seating, and 66 bars on our list say their deal applies only at the bar, in the bar area or for dine-in.
faq.q: Why do some happy hours only count at the bar?

faq.a: No. The State Liquor Authority says it is a crime to sell, deliver or give away alcohol to a visibly intoxicated person, and the license holder is responsible whether the owner or an employee served the drink.
faq.q: Can a bar keep serving someone who is drunk during happy hour?

method: Legal points come from section 117-a of New York's Alcoholic Beverage Control Law as published by the New York State Senate, and from State Liquor Authority pages: guidance for licensed retailers, frequent violations by retailers, the tavern and restaurant license quick references, and Advisory 2026-2 on for-profit clubs. Direct fetches of those pages were blocked from our system on October 23, 2026, so we confirmed each point through a web search limited to nysenate.gov and sla.ny.gov that showed the pages' own text. Deal counts cover all 685 bars on our list on October 23, 2026, using each bar's own posted happy hour, last checked between September 2 and October 23, 2026. A bar counts once per finding. This is a plain-language summary, not legal advice.

title: Taco Tuesday NYC: 8 Happy Hours With Tacos on Tuesday
h1: Taco Tuesday NYC: happy hours where tacos and Tuesday line up
description: Taco Tuesday NYC guide: 8 bars in Manhattan, Brooklyn and Queens with tacos on a happy hour that runs on Tuesday, from Lower East Side to Astoria.
answer: For Taco Tuesday NYC bars that put it in writing, go to La Caverna on the Lower East Side, Mad Tropical in Bushwick, whose happy hour runs all night on Tuesday, or Nostrand Station Bar & Lounge in Crown Heights. Papacito's in Greenpoint, El Lugar Cantina in Chelsea, Baylander Steel Beach in Harlem, and Mayahuel and Spanglish NYC in Astoria also have tacos on a happy hour that runs on Tuesday.
intro:
Taco Tuesday is easy to say and harder to find on an actual menu. We started from the happy hour offers of the 685 bars on our list and looked for tacos as a named item. Eighteen bars have them: nine in Manhattan, five in Brooklyn and four in Queens. Then we checked each one's windows, and all 18 run a happy hour on Tuesday. That is less surprising than it sounds, since 653 of the 685 bars on our list have a Tuesday window.

The smaller group is the bars that make Tuesday the taco day. Six bars write Taco Tuesday into their own happy hour text, and three of them are picks below. The rest of the picks have tacos on a happy hour that happens to include Tuesday, which works just as well when you are hungry.

The eight picks cover three boroughs. Cards carry live prices and hours. Use the text for what kind of tacos to expect, how the Tuesday deal differs from the rest of the week, and which train to take.

picks.why: La Caverna on Rivington Street gives Tuesday its own menu. Taco Tuesday runs into the evening, longer than its other windows, with beef, chicken or veggie tacos, margaritas, tequila shots and beer. The rest of the week it switches to a margarita tower, beer, wine and well drinks with no tacos, and there is no happy hour on Monday or Saturday. Essex Street on the F, J, M and Z is two minutes away.

Mad Tropical on Troutman Street runs happy hour every evening it is open, and on Tuesday it keeps going all night for Taco Tuesday. The deal is simple: two tacos, cocktails and draft beer. Its listing says it is closed on Monday. Central Avenue on the M is seven minutes away, and La Loncheria, which lists a taco and margaritas on its daily happy hour, is about three minutes on foot.

Nostrand Station Bar & Lounge sits on Nostrand Avenue a minute from the station of the same name on the 3. Happy hour runs Tuesday through Friday, late afternoon into early evening, with beer, shots, sangria, rum punch and margaritas. On Tuesday it adds a Taco Tuesday special: two tacos of your choice, street corn and a margarita. Wednesday brings wings and fries with rum punch instead.

Papacito's on Manhattan Avenue runs three happy hours, and Tuesday gets all of them. Tacos and fish tacos are on the daytime window, Monday through Friday. Late afternoon brings two-for-one frozen margaritas, house margaritas, sangria, nachos and Tecate or Modelo cans, with no tacos. Then the last hour of every night brings back tacos with a drink. Greenpoint Avenue on the G is three minutes away.

El Lugar Cantina on West 27th Street runs its happy hour Tuesday through Friday at the bar, a short window in the late afternoon. Tacos lead the list, with margaritas, palomas, sangria, house wines and Mexican draft beers. The cantina lists no Monday hours, so Tuesday is the first day of its week. The 28th Street station on the 1 is two minutes away, which makes it an easy stop after work in Chelsea.

Baylander Steel Beach runs a food happy hour Tuesday through Friday, from mid-afternoon to late afternoon, so it suits a long lunch or an early start. The tacos are the draw: fresh lime falafel tacos and grilled shrimp tacos, next to Prohibition's Giant Pretzel with melted jalapeno cheese and Mexican street corn ribs. The 125th Street station on the 1 is six minutes away, and you can book ahead.

Mayahuel on 34th Avenue serves its happy hour food at the bar only, Monday through Friday from late afternoon into early evening, plus a Sunday window. Tacos come as an order of two, alongside guacamole, nachos and a quesadilla. To drink there is a classic margarita, the house Mayahuel and Gloria cocktails, draft beer and house wine. Broadway on the N and W is a three-minute walk.

Spanglish NYC on Ditmars Boulevard has one of the longest windows here: Monday through Friday from midday into the early evening. Chicken tacos are sold one at a time, and the food list adds elote, guacamole, chicken empanadas, buffalo wings and a cheese quesadilla. Drinks include margaritas, a frozen margarita, the Picosito, mojitos, sangria and Corona or Modelo bottles. Astoria-Ditmars Boulevard on the N and W is five minutes away.

sections.body:
At most bars on this list, Tuesday looks like any other weekday. The tacos are on the menu for the whole working week, or every day, and Tuesday is simply included. Mayahuel and Spanglish NYC work that way, and so does El Lugar Cantina, whose week runs Tuesday through Friday.

Three picks treat Tuesday differently. La Caverna only serves tacos on its Tuesday menu, and that window runs the longest of its week. Mad Tropical stretches its usual evening happy hour into an all-night one on Tuesday. Nostrand Station Bar & Lounge bundles tacos, street corn and a margarita into one Tuesday special. Papacito's is the odd one: its tacos are on the daytime window and the last hour of the night, not the late afternoon, so plan your Tuesday around those two.

sections.h: More Taco Tuesday deals on our list
sections.body:
Three more bars name Taco Tuesday in their happy hour text. The Commissioner in Park Slope lists chicken or fish tacos with frozen or rocks margaritas on Tuesday, next to its Monday to Thursday happy hour. Cocteleria Perla Negra in Harlem notes Taco Tuesday all day. Sal y Lima in Rockaway Beach runs its happy hour every day except Tuesday, which it keeps for Taco Tuesday, so check its own page for that night.

Other bars with tacos on a happy hour that includes Tuesday: Panzon in Greenpoint has single tacos, El Coco in Chelsea has tacos from Sunday through Thursday, Deja Vu New York in Astoria has tacos Tuesday through Sunday, and Los Mismos Amigos in Corona has a taco on its weekday afternoon list. Grand Street Social in SoHo has roast pork tacos on its weekday food menu.

Two neighborhoods let you stack a second stop. In Bushwick, Mad Tropical and La Loncheria are about three minutes apart on foot, by our measurement. In Greenpoint, Papacito's and Panzon are about a seven-minute walk apart. For a full walking route in either neighborhood, see our Bushwick bar crawl and Greenpoint bar crawl, and the Tuesday happy hours page lists every deal running that day. A few practical notes. Mayahuel serves its happy hour food at the bar only, and El Lugar Cantina runs its deal at the bar, so take a stool. Baylander Steel Beach and El Lugar Cantina have short windows, so arrive near the start. If you want a drink to go with the tacos, our margarita happy hour guide covers bars that list margaritas by name.

faq.a: La Caverna on the Lower East Side, Mad Tropical in Bushwick and Nostrand Station Bar & Lounge in Crown Heights all name Taco Tuesday on their happy hour and list tacos. The Commissioner in Park Slope and Cocteleria Perla Negra in Harlem also mention Taco Tuesday in their happy hour text.
faq.q: Which NYC bars do Taco Tuesday at happy hour?

faq.a: Yes. Mad Tropical in Bushwick runs its happy hour all night on Tuesday for Taco Tuesday, with two tacos, cocktails and draft beer on the deal. Cocteleria Perla Negra in Harlem notes Taco Tuesday all day.
faq.q: Is there an all-night Taco Tuesday in NYC?

faq.a: Astoria has the most options on our list. Mayahuel serves tacos at the bar on weekdays and Sunday, Spanglish NYC sells chicken tacos one at a time on weekdays, and Deja Vu New York has tacos Tuesday through Sunday. Los Mismos Amigos in Corona has a taco on its weekday afternoon happy hour.
faq.q: Where can I get tacos at happy hour in Queens?

faq.a: Eighteen bars on our list of 685 name tacos as a happy hour item: nine in Manhattan, five in Brooklyn and four in Queens. All 18 run a happy hour on Tuesday.
faq.q: How many NYC happy hours have tacos?

faq.a: Yes, at some bars. Mayahuel, Spanglish NYC and Papacito's include Monday, but La Caverna and Mad Tropical do not, and El Lugar Cantina, Baylander Steel Beach and Nostrand Station Bar & Lounge start on Tuesday.
faq.q: Can I get tacos at happy hour on a Monday?

title: Financial District Bar Crawl: 5 After-Work Stops
h1: Financial District Bar Crawl: Fulton Street to Pearl Street After Work
description: A financial district bar crawl for weekdays after work: five happy hours from Fulton Street down Pearl Street, in walking order, no leg over four minutes.
answer: For a financial district bar crawl after work, go any weekday, Monday to Friday, and walk five happy hours in this order: Sadie's on Fulton Street, Industry Kitchen on South Street, Full Shilling on Pearl Street, then Route 66 Smokehouse and Lucky Tiger, a few doors apart on lower Pearl Street. All five run their deal every weekday from the afternoon, the first two close earliest, and no walk between stops takes more than about four minutes.
intro:
Downtown happy hour is timed for people leaving the office. Of the 19 Financial District bars on our list, 16 run a happy hour on all five weekdays, and 11 of them open the deal by mid-afternoon. The catch is that most of those windows also end in the early evening, so a crawl here has to start promptly and move in the right direction.

This route does that. It starts near the Fulton Street hub, where the two earliest-closing deals sit, then works south and west along Pearl Street and finishes by the Whitehall Street station, where the last two stops keep their prices running the longest. Five bars, under a kilometer of walking, and a mix that runs from a garden spritz to draught beer at a pub, frozen drinks at a smokehouse and a shot-and-beer combo at an Asian bar.

The pick cards below carry the live prices and the exact hours for each stop. Use this guide for the order, the days and the walking, and check the cards before you leave your desk.

picks.why: Start at Sadie's on Fulton Street. The happy hour here is a single drink, a spritz at the garden bar, Monday through Friday from mid-afternoon to early evening. It shares the earliest closing time on the route with the next stop, so come straight from work and keep it to one round. The Fulton Street hub, with the 2, 3, 4, 5, A, C, J and Z trains, is about five minutes away.

Walk about three minutes to Industry Kitchen, an American restaurant on South Street. Its weekday window runs on the same schedule as Sadie's, so treat the two as your first hour. The happy hour list covers draft beer, wines, margaritas and both Aperol and Hugo spritzes, which makes it the most varied drinks stop of the five. Wall Street on the 2 and 3 is a five-minute walk.

Full Shilling is a pub at 160 Pearl Street, about three minutes from Industry Kitchen. Its weekday happy hour starts later than the first two stops and runs into the early evening, so it is the natural first stop if you get out of the office late. Wine, draught beer, bottles and cans, and cocktails are all on the list. Wall Street on the 2 and 3 is two minutes away.

Route 66 Smokehouse is about four minutes south at 79 Pearl Street. Its happy hour runs Monday through Friday from mid-afternoon into the early evening, with beer, wines, well drinks and frozen drinks, and the bar's own site adds specialty martinis on Mondays. It takes bookings, which helps if your group outgrows a few bar stools. Whitehall Street-South Ferry on the 1, R and W is three minutes away.

Finish a minute away at Lucky Tiger, 66 Pearl Street, where the happy hour is served at its Dragon Bar & Night Market. The weekday list has a select cocktail, mocktails, select wine and a Kirin and shochu shot combo, plus a large platter that feeds four to six. It is the only stop with a second window, from late evening until close, if you want a nightcap after dinner.

sections.body:
All five stops run happy hour Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, so any weekday works. Monday has a small bonus, because Route 66 Smokehouse lists specialty martinis that day.

The route does not work on a weekend. None of the five lists a Saturday or Sunday window, and only 5 of the 19 Financial District bars on our list run a deal on Saturdays at all. If you are downtown on a weekend, see the last section for a short version that does work.

sections.h: How to time it after work
sections.body:
The order follows the clock. Sadie's and Industry Kitchen open their deals in the mid-afternoon and close first, so they lead. Full Shilling starts later and runs into the early evening. Route 66 Smokehouse and Lucky Tiger open in the afternoon and keep going until early evening, which makes the Pearl Street pair the safe place to end.

If you leave work at the end of a normal day, you may only catch the tail of the first two windows. In that case, skip ahead: start at Full Shilling and do the last three stops, which together are well under half a kilometer of walking. If you can leave early on a Friday, do all five and plan on about half an hour at each.

Lucky Tiger is the one bar that brings its deal back late at night, from late evening until close. That gives you an option the other stops do not: have dinner nearby after the crawl, then return to Lucky Tiger for one more round at happy hour prices.

From Sadie's on Fulton Street to Industry Kitchen on South Street is about 260 meters, roughly three minutes. Industry Kitchen to Full Shilling on Pearl Street is about 250 meters, another three minutes. The longest leg is next: about 310 meters south along Pearl Street to Route 66 Smokehouse, close to four minutes. Lucky Tiger is about 80 meters further, a one-minute walk.

Add it up and the whole crawl is about 890 meters, or around 11 minutes on your feet. We measure point to point between each bar's coordinates at about 80 meters a minute, and downtown streets bend, so allow a little extra.

The drinks change at every stop. You get a spritz at Sadie's garden bar, a broad list with margaritas and spritzes at Industry Kitchen, draught beer and cocktails at Full Shilling, frozen drinks and well drinks at Route 66 Smokehouse, and a beer and shot combo at Lucky Tiger.

Begin at Fulton Street, which our listing puts about five minutes from Sadie's and which serves the 2, 3, 4, 5, A, C, J and Z trains. With eight lines stopping there, it is an easy place to meet a group coming from different offices.

The route ends near Whitehall Street-South Ferry on the 1, R and W, two minutes from Lucky Tiger and three from Route 66 Smokehouse. Wall Street on the 2 and 3 is also two minutes from Full Shilling, if you drop out halfway.

sections.h: If your day does not fit
sections.body:
On a Saturday or Sunday, stay near the start. Urban Cove Society & Kitchen on Peck Slip, about 210 meters from Sadie's, runs its happy hour every day with beer, select wine and featured cocktails. Fresh Salt on Beekman Street, about 130 meters from Urban Cove, lists happy hour specials every day as well, so the two make a short weekend pair.

On Monday to Thursday, you can add a stop. Mad Dog and Beans sits next door to Route 66 Smokehouse at 83 Pearl Street and serves margaritas, house wine and Mexican beer at happy hour, at the bar only. Toro Loco on Stone Street, under two minutes from Lucky Tiger, is a weekday alternative with its own lager and frozen margaritas, though its window closes early. For more choices on the day, the table below lists happy hours near the route, closest first.

faq.a: Any weekday works, Monday through Friday. All five stops on this route run happy hour on every weekday, and Monday adds specialty martinis at Route 66 Smokehouse. The route does not work on Saturday or Sunday.
faq.q: Which day is best for a Financial District bar crawl?

faq.a: Yes, start at Full Shilling and do the last three stops. Sadie's and Industry Kitchen close their deals first, while Full Shilling, Route 66 Smokehouse and Lucky Tiger run into the early evening, and Lucky Tiger adds a late-night window.
faq.q: I leave work late. Can I still do the crawl?

faq.a: Plan on about two and a half to three hours for all five stops. The walking is only about 11 minutes over roughly 890 meters; the rest is one round and around half an hour at each bar.
faq.q: How long does the crawl take?

faq.a: No, you can walk in for happy hour at every stop. Route 66 Smokehouse and Lucky Tiger take bookings, and their cards above have the link if you are bringing a larger group.
faq.q: Do I need reservations?

faq.a: Start at Fulton Street (2, 3, 4, 5, A, C, J, Z), about five minutes from Sadie's. Finish at Whitehall Street-South Ferry (1, R, W), two minutes from Lucky Tiger.
faq.q: Which subway stations are closest to the start and end?

title: Drinking Age in NYC: ID Rules for Locals and Tourists
h1: Drinking age in NYC: the law, the ID you need, and 18+ nights
description: The drinking age in NYC is 21. Which IDs New York law lets bars accept, why tourists should carry a passport, and 18+ parties in our list.
answer: The drinking age in NYC is 21, set by New York State law, and it applies at every bar, restaurant and club in all five boroughs. Bars can rely only on a valid driver's license or non-driver ID from a U.S. or Canadian government, a valid passport from any country, or a U.S. armed forces ID, so visitors from outside North America should bring their passport. If you are 18 to 20, our parties list has three 18+ nights: at Ernest Records in Bed-Stuy, COLBO NEXT DOOR on the Lower East Side and Knockdown Center in Maspeth.
intro:
There is no local twist here: New York City follows the state's alcohol law, and the state sets the age at 21. What trips visitors up is not the number but the paperwork. New York law spells out which documents a bar may rely on as proof of age, and a driver's license from most countries outside North America is not one of them.

Below: what the law says, which IDs count, how Mobile ID works, practical tips for tourists, and where under-21s can still go out. The six picks are happy hours near Times Square, Rockefeller Center and Lower Manhattan that run every day of the week, so they fit any day of a trip. Their hours and prices sit on the cards, which update from each bar's own site.

picks.why: Faces & Names on West 54th Street is a straightforward bar a block from the 7th Avenue station on the B, D and E. Happy hour runs every day from mid-afternoon into the early evening, with bottled domestic beers, house red or white, well drinks, beer buckets and a daily special that changes through the week, from Margarita Monday to a rosé weekend. It is an easy first stop after a day in Midtown.

Double Knot on Sixth Avenue serves its happy hour in the upstairs bar and lounge every day, late in the afternoon. The list covers specialty cocktails such as the Tautline Hitch, with vodka, apple and ginger, and the Anchor Hitch, with rum, lychee and Thai basil, plus daily white and red wines and sake. It takes Resy bookings, and the B, D, F and M at Rockefeller Center are a two-minute walk.

Blue Fin is a seafood restaurant on Broadway in the middle of Times Square, and its happy hour runs every day in the bar area. The menu leans on food: market oysters, mini lobster rolls, crispy cauliflower, blistered shishito peppers and edamame. Our listing also notes a second round later at night. The N, R and W at 49th Street are a two-minute walk, which makes it handy before a Broadway show.

Gui Steakhouse on Eighth Avenue runs its happy hour at BAR92 every day from mid-afternoon into the early evening. The short list covers a half dozen oysters, a pair of sliders and specialty cocktails, enough for a snack before dinner or a show. It takes OpenTable reservations, and the C and E at 50th Street are a three-minute walk.

Le District, a French cafe and brasserie at 225 Liberty Street, runs a daily happy hour at the bar in the late afternoon, with select bottled beer, select wines by the glass and select cocktails. It is a short walk from the World Trade Center site, so it suits a break after a day of sightseeing downtown. The 1 at WTC Cortlandt is a four-minute walk.

Urban Cove Society & Kitchen on Peck Slip, by the South Street Seaport, runs happy hour every day of the week from mid-afternoon to early evening. The deal covers beer, select wines by the glass and featured cocktails, with a Clear Negroni and a Cynar Negroni on the list. Fulton Street, served by eight subway lines, is a six-minute walk.

sections.h: The legal drinking age in New York
sections.body:
Section 65 of New York's Alcoholic Beverage Control Law says no one may sell, deliver or give away alcohol to any person who is actually or apparently under 21. The rule is statewide, so Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx and Staten Island all work the same way. Note the word apparently: the law covers people who look under 21, which is why bartenders card adults who are clearly old enough to drink.

The law also puts a duty on the customer. Section 65-b makes it unlawful for anyone under 21 to show a bar a false or fraudulent ID, or someone else's, in order to buy alcohol. Borrowing an older friend's license is not a gray area.

Section 65-b also lists the only documents a bar may treat as written proof of age: a valid driver's license or non-driver ID issued by a government in the U.S. or Canada, a valid passport from the U.S. or any other country, or an ID card issued by the U.S. armed forces. The SLA adds that the card must be currently valid. A bar cannot reasonably rely on an expired one, so check your expiry date before you fly.

New York's Mobile ID, the state's digital license, is also allowed. An SLA advisory calls it a permissible form of ID for buying alcohol and for entry to a licensed venue, but says acceptance is voluntary for each bar. A bar cannot require it, and it must still accept a valid physical ID. For an alcohol sale, the bar can ask to see only your photo and your age, and you can decline. The SLA's handbook says bars are not legally required to ask for proof of age, but it strongly recommends they check every time, and most busy places do.

Bring your passport. It is the one document on the list that every visitor has, and a driver's license from Europe, Asia, Latin America or Australia is not on it. A photo of your passport on your phone is not the document itself. If you would rather not carry it all day, plan your evening so you pick it up before heading out. Expect to be carded at the door, again at the bar, or both, whatever your age. Happy hour is mostly a weekday habit in New York, but 191 of the 685 bars on our list run one every day, and that includes 13 of our 31 Times Square bars and 7 of 25 in the Financial District and Battery Park City. Once you are served, tipping is expected on every round; our guide to how much to tip at a bar in NYC has the details.

Being 18 to 20 does not mean staying in. Most nights on our parties list are 21 and up: 473 of the 478 published parties set 21 as the minimum, and two Halloween nights at Common Ground Bar in the Meatpacking District set it at 23. Three are open to 18 and up right now. Smacks / J Surena B2B DJ Set is a house and R&B night at Ernest Records in Bed-Stuy on Saturday, October 24. A local feeling x Agivi is at COLBO NEXT DOOR on the Lower East Side on Monday, October 26. B3K INVITES NY, with Brutalismus 3000, SPFDJ and Dorian Electra, takes over Knockdown Center in Maspeth, Queens, on Friday, November 6. An 18+ door gets you in, not served. Section 65 still applies at the bar inside, so bring the same valid ID and expect to show it again at the bar. Browse the full NYC parties list for new nights; age limits are listed on each one.

faq.a: 21. New York State law bars selling or giving alcohol to anyone actually or apparently under 21, and New York City follows the same rule in all five boroughs.
faq.q: What is the drinking age in NYC?

faq.a: Usually not. New York law lists driver's licenses and non-driver IDs from U.S. and Canadian governments, a valid passport from any country, and U.S. armed forces IDs. A license from another country is not on that list, so bring your passport.
faq.q: Can I use my foreign driver's license as ID at a New York bar?

faq.a: Some do. The State Liquor Authority says Mobile ID is a permissible form of ID for buying alcohol, but acceptance is voluntary for each bar, so carry your physical license too.
faq.q: Do NYC bars accept New York Mobile ID?

faq.a: It should not. The State Liquor Authority says the ID must be currently valid, and a bar cannot reasonably rely on an expired driver's license, non-driver ID or passport.
faq.q: Will a bar accept an expired ID?

faq.a: Some events admit them. Three published parties on our list are 18+ right now, at Ernest Records, COLBO NEXT DOOR and Knockdown Center, but guests under 21 still cannot buy or be served alcohol inside.
faq.q: Can 18-year-olds go to clubs in NYC?

faq.a: Often, yes. The law covers anyone who looks under 21, and the State Liquor Authority strongly recommends that bars check ID every time, even though asking is not legally required.
faq.q: Do NYC bars card people who are obviously over 21?

method: The age rule comes from sections 65 and 65-b of New York's Alcoholic Beverage Control Law as published by the New York State Senate. ID guidance comes from the State Liquor Authority's training materials on section 65-b, its Retail Licensee Handbook (revised July 2025) and Advisory 2024-2 on New York Mobile ID. Direct fetches of those pages were blocked from our system on October 23, 2026, so we confirmed each point through a web search limited to nysenate.gov and sla.ny.gov that showed the pages' own text. Party facts come from our published parties list on October 23, 2026. Bar picks are happy hours that run all seven days near major sights, with deals from each bar's own website, checked between October 17 and October 23, 2026. This is a plain-language summary, not legal advice.

title: Midtown Bar Crawl: 5 Happy Hours Around Bryant Park
h1: Midtown Bar Crawl: A Bryant Park Loop on Happy Hour
description: A midtown bar crawl around Bryant Park: five happy hours between West 39th and West 45th Streets, Tuesday to Friday, in walking order.
answer: For a midtown bar crawl that stays on happy hour, go Tuesday through Friday and loop around Bryant Park: start at Lolita and Valerie, which share an address on West 45th Street, walk south to The Dawson 39 on West 39th Street and Croton Reservoir Tavern on West 40th Street, and finish at Jane Doe on West 44th Street. The longest walk is under seven minutes, and the last two stops keep their deals running latest.
intro:
Midtown has plenty of happy hours, but they are spread over a big area, and a crawl that crosses Fifth Avenue and Lexington twice spends more time walking than drinking. This one stays in a tight loop on the west side of Fifth Avenue, in the blocks just north and south of Bryant Park. Our list has 22 happy hours within 500 meters of Croton Reservoir Tavern, the stop beside the 42nd Street-Bryant Park station, so the area is dense enough to build a full route without long walks.

We kept five bars whose windows overlap on the same days, then ordered them so the deal that ends first comes first. The result goes from Mexican cocktails and oysters on West 45th Street to an Irish pub's bar bites on West 39th, a speakeasy room under a tavern on West 40th, and a daily all-afternoon deal on West 44th to finish.

This route is separate from our guides to Grand Central and Penn Station and to pre-theater drinks in Times Square, and none of its stops repeat those picks. The pick cards below carry the live prices and hours; check them on the day you go.

picks.why: Start at Lolita, a Mexican bar at 45 West 45th Street. Its happy hour runs every day from mid-afternoon to early evening and comes back late at night, and the afternoon window is the first on this route to end, so it leads. The list covers house cocktails such as the Lolita margarita, paloma, daiquiri and mezcal negroni, plus house wines, cervezas and discounted bites. The Rockefeller Center station on the B, D, F and M is three minutes away.

Valerie, a New American restaurant, shares Lolita's address, so stop two is a few steps away. Its happy hour runs Monday through Friday from late afternoon into the early evening, with oysters on the list and, per its own site, cocktails, house wines, draft beers and light bites. The restaurant says group happy hour bookings need a reservation, so book ahead if you are more than a few people.

Walk about six or seven minutes south to The Dawson 39, an Irish pub and restaurant on West 39th Street. It has the longest weekday window of the five, from midday into the early evening, and it keeps a deal on weekends. The list is long: house wines and rose, Aperol and Hugo spritzes, bottled and draft beer, plus nachos, wings, hummus, pretzel bites and a mini charcuterie plate. Make it your food stop.

Croton Reservoir Tavern is two minutes away on West 40th Street, a minute from the 42nd Street-Bryant Park station. Its happy hour runs Tuesday through Friday from late afternoon into the evening, in The Speakeasy on the lower level; if that room is booked for a private event, the same deal moves upstairs. Margaritas, an Old Fashioned, a Manhattan, sangria, an Aperol spritz, select wines, draft beer and well drinks are all on it.

Finish about five minutes north at Jane Doe Bar & Restaurant on West 44th Street. Its happy hour runs every day from late morning into the evening, so it is still on after most of the route has ended. The list starts with the house Jane Doe Amber Ale and adds bottled and draft beers, wine by the glass and mixed drinks. The 5th Avenue station is two minutes away.

sections.body:
Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday are the days when all five stops run happy hour. Croton Reservoir Tavern is the limit: its deal starts on Tuesday, so on a Monday the route drops to four stops. Skip Croton and walk straight from The Dawson 39 to Jane Doe, which is still a short walk.

Weekends are thinner. Lolita and Jane Doe list happy hour every day and The Dawson 39 runs a weekend deal, but Valerie and Croton Reservoir Tavern are weekday only. A Saturday or Sunday version of three stops works, with The Dawson 39 as the anchor.

The order follows the closing times. Lolita's afternoon deal ends first, so it leads. Valerie, at the same address, runs a little longer into the early evening. The Dawson 39 started its window at midday, so it is well underway when you arrive. Croton Reservoir Tavern and Jane Doe have the latest windows of the five, which is why they close out the loop.

If you arrive late, start at The Dawson 39 and do the last three stops. If you only have an hour after work, the Croton and Jane Doe pair is the safest choice, since both keep their prices into the evening.

Lolita gives you one more option. Its second window runs late at night, and Jane Doe is only about 120 meters away, so a late round back at the first stop is a two-minute walk from the last one.

Lolita and Valerie share 45 West 45th Street, so the first leg is a few steps. From there the walk to The Dawson 39 on West 39th Street is the longest of the night, about 520 meters or six to seven minutes, heading south past the park. Croton Reservoir Tavern is about 170 meters away on West 40th Street, two minutes. The last leg is about 430 meters north to Jane Doe on West 44th Street, close to five and a half minutes.

In total, the loop is about 1.1 kilometers, or around 14 minutes of walking. Our distances are straight lines between bar coordinates at about 80 meters a minute, and Midtown crosswalks add time, so leave a little slack.

The mix is deliberate. Lolita brings margaritas and mezcal cocktails, Valerie brings oysters, The Dawson 39 brings the most food, Croton brings classic cocktails in a lower-level room, and Jane Doe brings a house ale for the last round.

Start from the 47th-50th Streets-Rockefeller Center station on the B, D, F and M, which our listing puts three minutes from Lolita and Valerie.

The middle of the loop sits by the 42nd Street-Bryant Park station, served by the 7, B, D, F and M: it is one minute from Croton Reservoir Tavern and two from The Dawson 39. Jane Doe, the final stop, is two minutes from the 5th Avenue station, so you finish within a short walk of the same lines you started on.

faq.a: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday. Those are the only days when all five stops on this route run happy hour, because Croton Reservoir Tavern has no Monday deal.
faq.q: Which day is best for a Midtown bar crawl?

faq.a: Yes, as four stops. Lolita, Valerie, The Dawson 39 and Jane Doe all run happy hour on Monday; skip Croton Reservoir Tavern and walk from The Dawson 39 straight to Jane Doe.
faq.q: Can I do the crawl on a Monday?

faq.a: Plan on about three hours. The walking adds up to about 14 minutes over roughly 1.1 kilometers, and the rest is one round and about half an hour at each of the five bars.
faq.q: How long does the crawl take?

faq.a: Only for a group at Valerie, which says group happy hour bookings need a reservation. Croton Reservoir Tavern also takes bookings online, and its card has the link. Solo drinkers and pairs can walk in everywhere.
faq.q: Do I need reservations?

faq.a: The Dawson 39 has the biggest food list, with nachos, wings, hummus, pretzel bites and a mini charcuterie plate. Lolita has discounted bites and Valerie has oysters at happy hour.
faq.q: Where can I eat on the route?

faq.a: Start at 47th-50th Streets-Rockefeller Center (B, D, F, M), three minutes from Lolita. The 42nd Street-Bryant Park station (7, B, D, F, M) is one minute from Croton Reservoir Tavern, and Jane Doe is two minutes from the 5th Avenue station.
faq.q: Which subway stations are closest?

The five bars on this route were last checked between October 17 and October 23, 2026, and the count of nearby happy hours was run on the same database on October 23, 2026. title: Greenwich Village Bar Crawl: 4 Happy Hours on Foot
h1: Greenwich Village Bar Crawl: West 3rd Street to Houston Street
description: A greenwich village bar crawl for Tuesday to Thursday: four happy hours from West 3rd Street to Houston Street, in walking order, no leg over six minutes.
answer: For a greenwich village bar crawl on happy hour, go on a Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday and walk four stops: Spicy Moon on West 3rd Street, Foursome on Jones Street, Emily on Downing Street and Houston Hall on West Houston Street. The whole walk is under a kilometer, and the deals hand off from late afternoon at Spicy Moon to the evening at Houston Hall.
intro:
Greenwich Village has more happy hours than its size suggests. Our list counts 33 bars in the neighborhood, and 22 bars with a happy hour sit within 400 meters of Foursome on Jones Street, the second stop on this route. The windows here are short, though, and many end in the early evening, so a Village crawl only works if you start on time and walk toward the later deals.

This route does that in four stops. It begins on West 3rd Street in the blocks near Washington Square, crosses to Jones Street, drops down to Downing Street and ends on West Houston Street, where the last happy hour runs the longest. Along the way you get sake and a lychee martini, a one-price spritz or margarita, a pizza restaurant's wings, and beer by the liter.

These are different blocks and different bars from our West Village bar crawl and from the bars we picked for the Village Halloween Parade. The live prices and exact hours are on each pick card below; check them before you set out.

picks.why: Start at Spicy Moon on West 3rd Street. Its happy hour runs Sunday through Thursday in the late afternoon and is drinks only: Golden Dragon lager, house red or white wine, a house spritz, a lychee martini, Itami Onigoroshi cup sake and a ginger lychee refresher. Go as soon as the window opens, because the next stop's deal ends at the same time. West 4th Street-Washington Square is a four-minute walk.

Walk about six minutes west to Foursome Bar and Restaurant on Jones Street, two minutes from the West 4th Street station. Its happy hour runs Monday through Friday on the same late-afternoon schedule as Spicy Moon, and it keeps things simple: wine, spritzes and margaritas at one happy hour price, plus small bites at another. It takes reservations, but a quick round at happy hour should not need one.

Emily, a pizza restaurant at 35 Downing Street, is about four to five minutes south. Its happy hour runs Monday through Thursday, starts later than the first two stops and ends in the early evening. The deal takes money off house cocktails, beer and wine, and Hot Nguyen's Wings, so this is the place to eat something before the last stop. The Houston Street station on the 1 is two minutes away.

Finish under two minutes away at Houston Hall, a pub at 222 West Houston Street, one minute from the Houston Street station on the 1. Its happy hour runs Tuesday through Friday from late afternoon into the evening, the longest window on the route. It covers beer in three sizes up to a liter, wine, cocktails and frozen drinks, plus an empanada sampler, a slider trio and a personal cheese pizza.

sections.body:
Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday are the only days when all four stops run happy hour. Monday drops Houston Hall, whose weekday deal starts on Tuesday. Friday drops both Spicy Moon, which runs Sunday through Thursday, and Emily, which stops after Thursday. On Saturday none of the four has a window.

That makes this a midweek crawl. Pick the day first, then check the four cards above for that day's hours, since each bar sets its own window. If your night falls on a Friday or a Sunday, the last section has versions that work.

Spicy Moon and Foursome share the same late-afternoon window, and both end in the early evening at the same moment. That is the tight part of the route: arrive at Spicy Moon as the deal opens, keep it to one round, and walk on to Foursome with time to spare.

Emily's window opens later than the first two and ends a little after them, so it is the natural third stop. Houston Hall runs the longest of the four, well into the evening, which is why it closes the night. If you are late, skip Spicy Moon and start at Foursome. If you can only make it after work, go straight to Emily and Houston Hall, which are less than two minutes apart.

The walking is short enough that you can spend about half an hour at each of the first three and still reach Houston Hall with plenty of happy hour left.

The first leg is the longest: about 470 meters from Spicy Moon on West 3rd Street to Foursome on Jones Street, about six minutes. From Foursome it is about 360 meters to Emily on Downing Street, four to five minutes. The last leg is about 110 meters to Houston Hall on West Houston Street, under two minutes.

In total, the crawl is about 940 meters, or roughly 12 minutes of walking. We measure straight lines between each bar's coordinates at about 80 meters per minute, so add a minute for corners and crossings.

Each stop has a different strength. Spicy Moon is the cocktail and sake stop, Foursome is the one-price stop, Emily is the food stop, and Houston Hall is the beer stop, with liters on the list and three kinds of bar food to share.

sections.h: If your day does not fit
sections.body:
On a Friday, swap two stops. Start at Foursome, walk about 140 meters to Little Havana on Cornelia Street, where the happy hour covers nachos and fries at the bar only, Monday through Friday. Then go about 260 meters to Judy Z's Sports Tavern & Kitchen on Seventh Avenue South, which runs happy hour Wednesday through Friday with beers, mixed drinks and frozen drinks. Houston Hall is about 110 meters from there to finish.

On a Sunday, pair Spicy Moon with Pepe Rosso on Sullivan Street, about 310 meters away, which lists beer and house wine at happy hour every day. Houston Hall's own site lists happy hour all day on Sunday, and it is about 300 meters from Pepe Rosso. For more options on the day, the table below lists happy hours near the route, closest first.

faq.a: Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday. Those are the only days when all four stops on this route run happy hour: Houston Hall has no Monday deal, and Spicy Moon and Emily have none on Friday.
faq.q: Which day is best for a Greenwich Village bar crawl?

faq.a: Yes, with two swaps. Start at Foursome, then go to Little Havana on Cornelia Street and Judy Z's Sports Tavern & Kitchen on Seventh Avenue South, and finish at Houston Hall. All four run happy hour on Friday.
faq.q: Can I do this crawl on a Friday?

faq.a: Plan on about two and a half hours. The walking is about 12 minutes over roughly 940 meters, and the rest is one round and about half an hour at each stop, with a longer finish at Houston Hall.
faq.q: How long does the crawl take?

faq.a: No, you can walk in at all four stops for happy hour. Spicy Moon and Foursome take bookings, and their cards above have the link if you want a table for a group.
faq.q: Do I need reservations?

faq.a: It uses different bars and different blocks. The West Village crawl runs along Hudson, Bank, Perry and Christopher Streets, while this route goes from West 3rd Street across Jones and Downing Streets to West Houston Street, with none of the same stops.

title: Can You Drink in Public in NYC? Open Container Rules
h1: Can you drink in public in NYC? The open container law, explained
keyword: can you drink in public in nyc
description: Can you drink in public in NYC? No. The open container law, parks and subway rules, and 6 patio and rooftop happy hours where you can drink outside.
answer: Can you drink in public in NYC? No: city law bans drinking alcohol, or carrying an open container of it, on streets, sidewalks and other public places, and parks and subway rules ban it too. To drink outdoors legally, sit at a licensed bar's patio, garden or rooftop, such as the garden bar at Sadie's in the Financial District, the patio at Jack & Charlie's No. 118 in the West Village or Glass Ceiling Rooftop in Koreatown, all with happy hours on weekdays.
intro:
New York has a reputation as a late-night city, so visitors are often surprised that a beer on the stoop or a bottle of wine in the park is against the rules. The open container law is a city law, and it applies in all five boroughs, on every street and sidewalk. Parks, beaches and the subway have their own rules that say the same thing.

The legal way to drink in the open air is at a bar or restaurant whose license covers its outdoor space: a sidewalk cafe, a back garden or a rooftop. Below: what the law says, the places people most often get it wrong, how outdoor seating at bars works, and six outdoor and rooftop happy hours from our list. Their hours and prices sit on the cards, which update from each bar's own site.

picks.why: Sadie's on Fulton Street runs a garden bar, and its happy hour is a spritz deal served Monday to Friday from mid-afternoon into the early evening. It is a short list, but it is one of the few Financial District happy hours on our list with outdoor space, which suits a weekday after the office or a walk around the Seaport. Fulton Street, served by eight subway lines, is a five-minute walk.

Jack & Charlie's No. 118 on Greenwich Avenue serves its happy hour only at the bar and on the patio, every day of the week from late afternoon into the evening. The menu is food-forward: oysters, a Caesar salad with baby gem and herbed breadcrumbs, and a popover French dip with shaved roast beef and horseradish. The A, C, E and L at 8th Avenue are a two-minute walk.

Glass Ceiling Rooftop on Broadway near 28th Street runs two happy hour windows, Tuesday to Saturday: one in the late afternoon and a second late at night. The list covers espresso, dirty and cosmo martinis, classic cocktails such as a margarita, old fashioned, paloma and mule, plus flatbreads, a chef's chipcuterie board and a Caesar. The R and W at 28th Street are a one-minute walk.

Castell Rooftop Lounge sits inside the AC Hotel on West 40th Street, steps from Times Square and the theaters. Its happy hour runs Monday to Friday in the late afternoon, with cocktails, wines and beer each at a set happy hour price, which makes it an easy round before a Broadway curtain. The 42nd Street-Port Authority Bus Terminal station, with twelve lines, is a three-minute walk.

Meraki Greek Bistro on Grand Street in Williamsburg has outdoor seating and a weekday happy hour from mid-afternoon into the early evening. The deal is a menu of Greek plates at one set price: Greek-style ceviche, horiatiki and halloumi salads, spreads, sliders, calamari, meatballs, souvlaki and spanakopita. It takes SevenRooms reservations, and the L at Bedford Avenue is a six-minute walk.

Vacations Bar & Rooftop on Cypress Avenue is the Bushwick option, and its deal could not be simpler: money off everything, Tuesday to Friday in the early evening. That makes it a good spot to start a night in the neighborhood, with the roof as the draw while the weather holds. The L at Jefferson Street is a four-minute walk.

sections.h: What the open container law says
sections.body:
The rule is section 10-125 of the New York City Administrative Code. It bars drinking an alcoholic beverage in a public place, and it bars carrying an open container of alcohol with the intent to drink it there. Carrying an open container counts as evidence that you meant to drink it, so walking with an open can is enough. The code carves out permitted block parties, feasts and similar events, but the city's street permit office says alcohol is not allowed at the parades, block parties and street festivals it permits, so do not count on that exception.

The city has repeated that the open container law remains in effect, and a 2026 City Council resolution describes state law and the Administrative Code as generally prohibiting drinking in public places, including streets and sidewalks. Since the Criminal Justice Reform Act took effect in 2017, police can write a civil summons for open container, heard at the city's Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings (OATH), instead of sending you to criminal court. OATH lists open container among the charges that can qualify for community service instead of a penalty.

sections.h: Parks, the subway and drinks to go
sections.body:
Parks have their own rule. NYC Parks rules say that, except where the Parks Commissioner specifically allows it, no one may drink alcohol in any park, playground, beach, pool or other park property. A few venues on park land sell drinks from authorized vendors, and that is the exception, not the rule, so leave the picnic wine at home.

The subway is off limits too: New York City Transit's rules of conduct bar drinking alcohol or carrying an opened or unsealed container of it anywhere in the system. And a cocktail to go is not a pass to drink on the sidewalk. The State Liquor Authority's guidance on drinks to go says those drinks are subject to the city's and the state's open container laws, so keep the lid on until you are home.

sections.h: Where you can drink outside legally
sections.body: Outdoor seating at a bar is legal because it is part of the licensed premises. Dining Out NYC, the city's permanent outdoor dining program, lets restaurants set up sidewalk and roadway cafes, and the city says they can serve alcohol there only if they hold a State Liquor Authority license. The SLA requires a licensee to get approval before adding outdoor space, whether it is a patio it controls or a cafe on city sidewalk or street, and if the city permit ends, alcohol service in that space has to stop right away. For you, that means two things. Your drink stays in the seating area: stepping past the cafe barrier onto the open sidewalk with a glass puts you back under the open container law. And a rooftop, garden or back patio at a licensed bar is the legal answer to wanting a drink in the fresh air. Our outdoor happy hours and rooftop happy hours pages keep those lists current.

sections.h: Outdoor and rooftop happy hours in our data
sections.body: Open-air happy hours are rare on our list. Of 685 bars, 15 carry the outdoor tag and 10 the rooftop tag, 25 in all. Manhattan has 18 of them, Brooklyn 5 and Queens 2. Only 11 run a happy hour on Saturday or Sunday, and 6 run one every day, so this is mostly a weekday plan. Several, including Jack & Charlie's No. 118, Osteria Nonnino and Cotta Osteria, keep their deal to the bar and the outdoor seats. It is late October, so the season matters. Outdoor seats depend on the weather and on each bar's own schedule. Check before you go, and have an indoor backup nearby. For the hours these deals usually run, see what time happy hour is in NYC.

faq.a: No. New York City's open container law bars drinking alcohol, or carrying an open container with intent to drink, in public places such as streets and sidewalks. Parks and the subway have their own bans.
faq.q: Can you drink in public in NYC?

faq.a: No, not on your own. NYC Parks rules bar drinking alcohol in any park, playground, beach or pool unless the Parks Commissioner has specifically allowed it, such as at a permitted vendor or event.
faq.q: Can you drink in Central Park or other NYC parks?

faq.a: Not with it open. The State Liquor Authority says drinks bought to go are subject to the city's and state's open container laws, so keep the container sealed until you are off the street.
faq.q: Can I walk down the street with a to-go cocktail in NYC?

faq.a: No. New York City Transit's rules of conduct bar drinking alcohol or carrying an opened or unsealed container of it anywhere on the system.
faq.q: Can you drink on the subway in NYC?

faq.a: Yes, if the bar's liquor license covers that space. The State Liquor Authority must approve outdoor space before a bar serves alcohol in it, and you need to keep your drink within the seating area.
faq.q: Is it legal to drink at a bar's sidewalk table?

faq.a: Usually a summons. Under the Criminal Justice Reform Act, police can write a civil summons heard at OATH instead of a criminal one, and OATH lists open container among the charges that can qualify for community service.
faq.q: What happens if you get caught drinking in public in NYC?

method: The open container rule comes from New York City Administrative Code section 10-125 as amended by Local Law 74 of 2016 (NYC Council, Int 1067-2016), a city notice confirming the law remains in effect, and a 2026 City Council resolution describing current law. Enforcement details come from the City Council's Criminal Justice Reform Act pages and OATH's hearings FAQ. Parks rules come from NYC Parks rule 1-05, subway rules from New York City Transit's rules of conduct, drinks-to-go guidance from the State Liquor Authority FAQ posted on nyc.gov, outdoor dining from NYC Business's Dining Out NYC page and SLA Advisory 2024-1, and block party rules from the city's street permit office. Direct fetches of these official pages were blocked from our system on October 23, 2026, so we confirmed each point through a web search limited to the official domains that showed the pages' own text. Bar counts cover the 685 bars on our list on October 23, 2026, and picks use deals from each bar's own website, checked between October 19 and October 23, 2026. This is a plain-language summary, not legal advice.

title: Things to Do in NYC in November 2026: Nights Out by Week
h1: Things to Do in NYC in November: A 2026 Night-Out Guide

description: Things to do in NYC in November 2026: 177 parties week by week, the Marathon, Veterans Day and the 100th Macy's Parade, plus happy hours.
answer: Things to do in NYC in November 2026 start with three dates: the TCS New York City Marathon on Sunday, November 1, the Veterans Day Parade on Fifth Avenue on Wednesday, November 11, and the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade on Thursday, November 26. After dark, our list has 177 published parties for the month, peaking on Friday, November 13 and at Time Warp NYC in the Brooklyn Navy Yard on November 20 and 21.
intro:
November in New York opens with Marathon Sunday and the end of daylight saving time on the same day, puts a parade on Fifth Avenue in the middle, and closes with Thanksgiving week and a long weekend. In between come four full weekends of parties.

We pulled every published party on our list with a November 2026 date: 177 at 45 venues. Brooklyn hosts 97, Manhattan 66 and Queens 14. Saturdays carry 71 and Fridays 64, leaving 42 for Sunday through Thursday. By sound, 45 are tagged house, techno or trance and 36 Latin or reggaeton; 19 are rooftop nights and 26 start before 8 p.m. Below, week by week, are the standout nights, each linked to its party page for tickets, age rules and status, then six happy hours near the busiest venues.

picks.why: The pub pick, at 236 Butler Street in Gowanus, about a minute on foot from Public Records, which has 16 nights on our November list. Happy hour runs every day: Tuesday through Sunday in the late afternoon with Bavarian pretzels and craft drafts, and Monday from open to close with beers, well drinks and cocktails. Union Street on the R is six minutes away.

The oyster pick, on Irving Avenue in Bushwick. Happy hour runs every day until the early evening with discounted oysters, wine specials and Spanish tapas, a light meal before a long night. House of Yes and Sea Wolf are each about three minutes on foot and Elsewhere about seven. Jefferson Street on the L is three minutes away.

The cheap-beer pick, at 112 Avenue A, about a minute from DROM and its throwback nights. Happy hour runs every day from opening until the early evening with draft beer, house wine and well drinks, and the bar lists a second, late-night window from Sunday to Wednesday. First Avenue on the L is seven minutes away.

The karaoke pick, on Orchard Street about five minutes on foot from The Delancey. Happy hour runs every day from opening into the evening, with lemon drop, kamikaze, sake and soju shots, draft beer, wine, sake or soju bombs and cocktails, and the private rooms have an early-evening rate. Delancey Street on the F, J, M and Z is three minutes away.

The sports bar pick, an Irish bar and restaurant on West 39th Street, two minutes from 42nd Street-Bryant Park. Happy hour runs from midday on weekdays and all day on Saturday and Sunday, with house wine, spritzes, bottled and draft beer, nachos, wings and pretzel bites. Nebula and the Magic Hour rooftop are four and five minutes away.

The rooftop pick, at 1204 Broadway, a minute from 28th Street on the R and W. It runs two happy hours Tuesday through Saturday, one in the late afternoon and one late at night, with martinis, classic cocktails such as margaritas and palomas, flatbreads and a Caesar. Somewhere Nowhere, home of Haus of Joon, is about five minutes away.

sections.h: November 1 to 8: Marathon Sunday, then the first full weekend
sections.body: The 2026 TCS New York City Marathon is on Sunday, November 1. New York Road Runners says the race finishes in Central Park and that this year marks 50 years of the five-borough course. See where to watch the NYC Marathon for bars along the course. Clocks also fall back an hour early that morning, per NIST, so Halloween Saturday night runs an hour longer. Eight parties close out Halloween weekend on Sunday, including Run Punch Vol. 3, a marathon after-party at Moondog HiFi in Bushwick and Circoloco's Sunday session at Brooklyn Storehouse from midday. The week of November 2 to 8 has 50 parties, 39 of them on Friday and Saturday. Friday the 6th brings B3K Invites NY with Brutalismus 3000 and Dorian Electra at Knockdown Center in Maspeth, the only November party on our list open to 18 and up, and Eli Escobar all night at House of Yes. Volkoder's set at The Chocolate Factory is already sold out. On Saturday the 7th, Benji B plays Public Records and Zombies in Miami play live at The Chocolate Factory.

sections.h: November 9 to 15: Veterans Day and the month's busiest Friday
sections.body: Veterans Day falls on Wednesday, November 11. The United War Veterans Council, which organizes the parade, lists the 2026 New York City Veterans Day Parade on Fifth Avenue that day; start time and route were not posted when we checked, so look at its site before you go. That evening, Date Nite: Vinyl Happy Hour at Sleepwalk in Williamsburg is one of four Wednesday editions this month. The week has 48 parties, and Friday the 13th is the busiest night of November on our list, with 21. Pick by sound: Cut Copy's DJ set at Elsewhere, Durations with Dasha Rush at Public Records, or The Hustle, a 70s disco night at DROM. Kyle Cooke at Marquee is sold out, and DJ Snake plays Marquee the night before. Saturday the 14th has 20 more: DAX J open to close at Knockdown Center, DJ Sprinkles at Public Records and Eli Escobar and Bag Raiders at SILO Brooklyn.

The third week is quiet midweek and heavy on the weekend: 40 parties, 34 of them on Friday and Saturday. The headline is Time Warp NYC at Duggal Greenhouse in the Brooklyn Navy Yard, listed with a Friday pass, a Saturday pass and a two-day pass for November 20 and 21. Thursday the 19th warms up with Techno Thursday at SILO Brooklyn. If Time Warp is not your scene, Friday also has Eptic at SILO Brooklyn, Take Me Out, a 2000s disco punk night at DROM, and Kasango at Somewhere Nowhere. Saturday brings Snakehips at Elsewhere and Joshwa open to close at 99 Scott. On Sunday, Shelter with Timmy Regisford starts in the afternoon at Public Records.

Thanksgiving is Thursday, November 26, per the federal holiday calendar, and the week has 31 parties on our list. Wednesday the 25th, Thanksgiving Eve, is the big night, with seven parties, among them Flashback with Louie Vega at Superior Ingredients and Soul in the Horn with Natasha Diggs at The Chocolate Factory. Our Thanksgiving Eve plan maps the night, and the Thanksgiving Eve party page keeps the lineup current. Thursday is the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, which Macy's says airs live on NBC and Peacock. Macy's had not posted a 2026 route map when we checked, so check its site closer to the day. Only one party is listed that night: Groundcontrol's Thanksgiving at Superior Ingredients in Williamsburg. The long weekend picks up on Friday with Sidepiece at Marquee and Luciid at SILO Brooklyn. Saturday the 28th has 13 parties, led by Felix Da Housecat at House of Yes and MPH at Knockdown Center.

sections.h: Weekly regulars and happy hours by theme
sections.body: Some nights repeat all month. Every Friday and Saturday there is a reggaeton rooftop party at Lost in Paradise in Long Island City, Monstera at Sea Wolf in Bushwick, and Reggaeton Fridays and Safaera Saturdays at The Delancey on the Lower East Side. Lyra Rooftop Party runs six nights at Magic Hour in the Garment District, Haus of Joon plays Somewhere Nowhere every Saturday, and Loco Carnaval closes every Sunday there. For the next few days, check this weekend's parties. The six happy hours above each sit within about seven minutes on foot of a busy party venue, one per theme: a pub, oysters, cheap beer, karaoke, a sports bar and a rooftop.
