title: Koreatown Bar Crawl: 4 Happy Hours, Ending in Karaoke
h1: Koreatown Bar Crawl: Herald Square to a 32nd Street Karaoke Room
description: A Koreatown bar crawl for Monday to Wednesday: four happy hours from West 36th Street to a karaoke lounge on West 32nd Street, under 1 km on foot.
answer: For a Koreatown bar crawl that stays on happy hour, go on a Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday and walk four stops: The Ragtrader Bo Peep on West 36th Street, Legasea Bar & Grill on Seventh Avenue, Stella 34 Trattoria on West 34th Street and Maru Karaoke Lounge on West 32nd Street. The walk is about 920 meters in all, and the karaoke stop's evening happy hour starts as the other three wind down.
intro:
Koreatown packs a lot into a few blocks around Herald Square, and our list for the area stretches from West 27th Street up to West 36th Street and over to Seventh Avenue by Penn Station. Thirteen bars sit in it, and this route uses four of them: a food-first bar, an oyster bar, an Italian trattoria and a karaoke lounge on West 32nd Street, the block most people picture when they hear the name.

We dropped bars whose deal listings were stale, empty or jumbled, and built the order around one fixed point: Maru's happy hour starts in the evening, just as the others end, so the crawl finishes with a microphone. Fifty bars on our list, these four included, have a happy hour within a 10-minute walk of Stella 34, the third stop, which is one of the densest pockets we track.

Use this guide for the order, the days and the walk. Live prices and exact hours are on each pick card below.

picks.why: Start at The Ragtrader Bo Peep, a bar on West 36th Street two minutes from the 34th Street-Herald Square station. Its weekday happy hour runs from midday and ends before the others on this route, so it goes first. The deal is all food: onion soup arancini, spinach artichoke dip, crispy tandoori cauliflower, fries and a fried chicken slider. Eat here, since the next three stops are mostly about drinks.

Walk about four minutes west to Legasea Bar & Grill at 485 Seventh Avenue. Its happy hour runs Monday to Friday from mid-afternoon into the early evening, at the bar only, with discounted oysters, fries, beer, wine and martinis. Walk-ins are welcome and the full menu is also served. It is the oyster stop of the night, and 34th Street-Penn Station on the 1, 2 and 3 is two minutes away.

Stella 34 Trattoria is about three minutes south at 151 West 34th Street, a minute from Herald Square. Its weekday happy hour starts in the late afternoon and is served only at the bar. Signature cocktails include a Lampone Mule, a Dante Daiquiri and a Bergamot 75, and the first one comes with a small margherita pizza. Classic cocktails, daily wines and draft or bottled beer are on the list too.

Finish about five minutes southeast at Maru Karaoke Lounge on West 32nd Street. Its happy hour runs Sunday through Wednesday in the evening, the latest window of the four, with domestic beer, shots of Jameson, Jack Daniel's, Fireball, Tito's, Bacardi or Cuervo, a beer and shot combo, well drinks and cocktails. Private karaoke rooms are discounted during happy hour too. Herald Square is three minutes away.

sections.body:
Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday. The first three stops run happy hour Monday to Friday, and Maru runs its deal Sunday through Wednesday, so those three weeknights are the only ones where all four line up. Thursday and Friday still work for the first three; see the last section for a different finish.

The order follows the clock. The Ragtrader's food deal starts at midday and ends first, so it opens the crawl in the late afternoon. Legasea has been on happy hour since mid-afternoon, and Stella 34's bar deal starts a little later, so those two fill the middle. Both close in the early evening, which is about when Maru's evening window opens. Plan on 40 to 45 minutes at each of the first three stops, then settle in at Maru. Exact times are on the pick cards.

From The Ragtrader on West 36th Street to Legasea on Seventh Avenue is about 320 meters, around four minutes. Legasea to Stella 34 on West 34th Street is about 230 meters, three minutes. The last leg, to Maru on West 32nd Street, is about 370 meters, close to five minutes. That is about 920 meters in total, roughly 12 minutes on foot.

The stops each do one thing. The Ragtrader is the food stop, with arancini, dip and sliders. Legasea is oysters and martinis at the bar. Stella 34 is cocktails with a free small pizza on the first signature drink. Maru is beer, shots and a karaoke room. Our distances are straight lines between bar coordinates at about 80 meters a minute, so allow a little extra for corners and crossings.

The 34th Street-Herald Square station, served by the B, D, F, M, N, Q, R and W, is the hub here: our listings put it two minutes from The Ragtrader, a minute from Stella 34 and three minutes from Maru. Legasea is closer to 34th Street-Penn Station on the 1, 2 and 3. Either way you can arrive and leave by subway without a long walk.

At Maru, the happy hour deal covers private rooms as well as drinks, so a group can take its own room for the window. Arrive as the window opens to get the most of it, and agree on a playlist before the first round of shots, not after.

On a Thursday or Friday, keep the first three stops and swap Maru for Glass Ceiling Rooftop at 1204 Broadway, also on our Koreatown list. It runs a late-afternoon happy hour and a second one late at night, Tuesday through Saturday, with martinis, classic cocktails, flatbreads and a Caesar. It is about six minutes from Stella 34, so you can go for the late window after dinner. Weekends are thin. Only four of the 13 Koreatown bars on our list run a Saturday happy hour, and Glass Ceiling is the only one of them with a detailed deal posted. For more, see the Koreatown happy hours page or the live table below, which lists every happy hour near Herald Square, closest first.

title: Chelsea Bar Crawl: 5 Happy Hours, Monday to Thursday
h1: Chelsea Bar Crawl: Five Stops From West 19th to West 16th
description: A Chelsea bar crawl for Monday to Thursday: five happy hours from West 19th Street down Eighth Avenue to West 16th Street, about 1.5 km on foot.
answer: For a Chelsea bar crawl that stays on happy hour, go Monday to Thursday and walk five stops: Boqueria Spanish Tapas on West 19th Street, The Cooper Still on West 22nd Street, El Coco on Eighth Avenue, Chelsea Ristorante Italiano lower on Eighth Avenue, and La Devozione on West 16th Street. No leg is longer than about five minutes, and the happy hour windows run from mid-afternoon into the early evening in that order.
intro:
Chelsea is wide, from Sixth Avenue to the river, and its happy hours come in pockets rather than one strip. The southern pocket, between 14th and 23rd Streets around Seventh and Eighth Avenues, is the one where five reliable deals sit close enough to walk between, and where the windows line up neatly from afternoon to early evening.

We started from the 18 Chelsea bars on our list and dropped those with stale, empty or muddled deal listings. Five made the cut: a tapas bar, a pub, a margarita bar, an Italian restaurant and a cocktail bar. Twenty-six bars on our list, these five included, have a happy hour within a 10-minute walk of El Coco, the middle stop, so there are fallbacks all along the route.

One note on the line: Boqueria Spanish Tapas is filed under Chelsea on our list, but at 53 West 19th Street it sits just east of Sixth Avenue, where Chelsea meets Flatiron. The other four are inside Chelsea proper. Live prices and exact hours are on each pick card below.

picks.why: Start at Boqueria Spanish Tapas on West 19th Street, just across Sixth Avenue on the Flatiron side. Its weekday happy hour starts mid-afternoon, the earliest of the five, with pan con tomate, croquetas, patatas bravas, a serrano ham grilled cheese, beef sliders and churros, plus mini martinis, a mini espresso martini and Spanish beer. It also runs a weekend window. The 23rd Street F and M stop is four minutes away.

Walk about five minutes northwest to The Cooper Still, a pub on West 22nd Street a minute from the 23rd Street 1 stop. Its happy hour runs from opening until the early evening, Monday to Friday, with seasonal spritzes, mules and margaritas, drafts such as Stella, Goose Island, Kona and Sam Adams Seasonal, sauvignon blanc, malbec or rose, well drinks, a big bowl of fries and spinach artichoke dip.

El Coco on Eighth Avenue is three to four minutes west. Its happy hour runs Sunday through Thursday from midday into the early evening, which is why this route stops at Thursday. Expect a long margarita list, classic, frozen, watermelon and Blue Hawaiian, plus a passionfruit martini, a lemon drop, a blueberry coconut mojito, a cucumber smash, small bites and tacos. The 23rd Street C and E stop is three minutes away.

Head about five minutes south down Eighth Avenue to Chelsea Ristorante Italiano at number 108. Its weekday happy hour is short and starts in the early evening, so time this stop for when it opens. Drinks include a limoncello spritz, wine, well drinks, birra, a Chelsea Pimm's, a margarita and a Candy Crush, with zucchine fritte, calamari, bruschetta, polpettine, focaccia and a cheese plate. The 14th Street station is a minute away.

Finish about five minutes west at La Devozione, a bar at 428 West 16th Street. Its weekday happy hour runs into the early evening, the last window on the route, and is served only at the cocktail bar and communal tables. The food list includes spaghetti aglio e olio pasta chips, marinated olives and mac and cheese lollipops, and our list tags it for cocktails and wine. The 14th Street A, C, E and L station is five minutes away.

sections.body:
Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday. Four of the five stops run happy hour Monday to Friday, but El Coco's deal runs Sunday through Thursday, so Thursday is the last night all five line up. On a Friday, skip El Coco and walk straight from The Cooper Still down to Chelsea Ristorante Italiano, about seven minutes. On weekends the route does not hold: only Boqueria and El Coco, on Sunday, keep a window.

The order follows the clock. Boqueria opens its window first, mid-afternoon, and The Cooper Still's deal ends in the early evening, so those two come first. El Coco has been running since midday and gives you slack in the middle. Chelsea Ristorante Italiano's window is the shortest and starts latest among the first four, and La Devozione's runs latest of all, so the crawl ends on West 16th Street. Plan on about 40 minutes at each stop; exact times are on the cards.

From Boqueria on West 19th Street to The Cooper Still on West 22nd Street is about 410 meters, around five minutes. El Coco on Eighth Avenue is about 280 meters on, three to four minutes. Chelsea Ristorante Italiano is about 360 meters south on Eighth Avenue, four to five minutes, and La Devozione on West 16th Street is about 420 meters west, roughly five minutes. That is about 1.5 kilometers in all, under 20 minutes of walking spread across five legs.

The mix moves from tapas and mini martinis to pub drafts and dips, then margaritas, then Italian plates and spritzes, and finally cocktails with bar snacks. If you want one proper meal, make it Boqueria at the start or Chelsea Ristorante Italiano near the end. Distances are straight lines between each bar's coordinates at about 80 meters a minute, so allow a little extra for avenue crossings.

Start from the 23rd Street station on the F and M, which our listing puts four minutes from Boqueria. The Cooper Still sits a minute from the 23rd Street stop on the 1, and El Coco three minutes from 23rd Street on the C and E, so you can join the crawl midway if you are running late.

The route ends near 14th Street, where the A, C, E and L station is a minute from Chelsea Ristorante Italiano and five minutes from La Devozione. That makes the last two stops easy to leave from in any direction.

sections.h: If your day does not fit
sections.body: For a Friday or Saturday, look west. OfCorsica on Eleventh Avenue runs happy hour Tuesday through Saturday in the afternoon, with drinks from Vesper martinis to daiquiris, about five minutes from La Devozione. Porchlight, further up Eleventh Avenue in West Chelsea, runs a house cocktail happy hour every day. Boqueria keeps a shorter weekend window too. For more, see the Chelsea happy hours page, or use the live table below, which lists every happy hour within a 10-minute walk of El Coco, closest first.

faq.a: Monday through Thursday. Those are the only days all five stops run happy hour, because El Coco's deal runs Sunday to Thursday and the other four are weekday deals. On Friday, skip El Coco and do the other four.
faq.q: Which day works for a Chelsea bar crawl?

faq.a: About four hours with one round at each stop. The walking adds up to roughly 1.5 kilometers, under 20 minutes, starting mid-afternoon and finishing in the early evening.
faq.q: How long does the crawl take?

faq.a: It is on the edge. Our list files it under Chelsea, but 53 West 19th Street sits just east of Sixth Avenue, where many people would say Flatiron. The other four stops are in Chelsea proper.
faq.q: Is Boqueria really in Chelsea?

faq.a: Boqueria at the start or Chelsea Ristorante Italiano near the end. Boqueria's happy hour includes croquetas, sliders and a serrano ham grilled cheese; Chelsea Ristorante Italiano adds calamari, polpettine and a cheese plate.
faq.q: Where should I eat on the route?

faq.a: Start at 23rd Street on the F and M, four minutes from Boqueria. Finish at 14th Street on the A, C, E and L, five minutes from La Devozione.
faq.q: Which subway stations are closest to the start and end?

faq.a: Not this route. On Saturday, try OfCorsica on Eleventh Avenue, which runs happy hour Tuesday through Saturday, with Porchlight's daily happy hour nearby and Boqueria's weekend window.
faq.q: Can I do a Chelsea bar crawl on a weekend?

table_title: Happy hours within a 10-minute walk of the route
method: We built this route from the 18 Chelsea bars in our database, which records each bar's happy hour schedule and offers from its own website. The five stops were last checked between October 16 and October 23, 2026. We dropped bars with stale, empty or garbled listings, kept those whose windows share Monday to Thursday, and ordered the stops by when each window opens and closes. Walking times are straight-line distances between bar coordinates at about 80 meters a minute. Subway stations and walking times come from each bar's listing.

title: Friendsgiving NYC 2026: 8 Bookable Happy Hours
h1: Friendsgiving NYC: Where to Take Your Group Thanksgiving Week 2026
description: Friendsgiving NYC guide for Thanksgiving week 2026: 8 bookable happy hours in 8 neighborhoods, tips for groups and the bill, and parties Nov 20 to 29.
answer: For Friendsgiving NYC plans in Thanksgiving week 2026 (Thanksgiving is Thursday, November 26), book a place that takes reservations and runs a happy hour with food to share: Boqueria Spanish Tapas in Chelsea, Meraki Greek Bistro in Williamsburg, Pera SoHo, Oliver's Astoria and Mudville in Tribeca all run Monday through Friday. For the weekend after, Boqueria, Siren in Park Slope and Juniper near Penn Station keep their happy hours on Saturday and Sunday.
intro:
Friendsgiving is easier when someone else does the dishes. In New York that usually means a bar or restaurant that takes a booking, so your group has a table waiting, plus a happy hour, so the first round and a few shared plates cost less. This guide covers Thanksgiving week 2026, from the weekend of November 21 and 22 through Sunday, November 29.

We started from the 223 places on our list that take reservations online and kept the ones with a posted happy hour that covers food or drinks a group can share, each checked against the venue's own website in the past two weeks. The eight picks sit in eight different neighborhoods across Manhattan, Brooklyn and Queens. Each card shows live prices and exact hours, and the table below lists every bookable happy hour in the city.

picks.why: Boqueria on West 19th Street is a Spanish tapas restaurant, and its happy hour is made for a table that shares: pan con tomate, croquetas, patatas bravas, a serrano ham grilled cheese, beef sliders and churros, plus mini martinis, a mini espresso martini and Spanish beer. It runs on weekday afternoons and again on Saturday and Sunday, so it covers the Friendsgiving weekend too. The F and M at 23rd Street are four minutes away.

Meraki Greek Bistro on Grand Street turns its weekday happy hour into a meze spread: Greek-style ceviche, horiatiki and halloumi salads, a spreads platter, calamari, meatballs, spanakopita, sliders and souvlaki. Order several and pass them around. The window opens mid-afternoon Monday through Friday, which suits an early Friendsgiving on the Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday before the holiday. Bedford Avenue on the L is a six-minute walk.

Pera SoHo on Thompson Street is a Mediterranean restaurant with a single-price happy hour that covers mezze, signature cocktails, wines by the glass, draft beer and mocktails, so the friend who is skipping alcohol gets a deal too. It runs Monday through Friday in the late afternoon. The C and E at Spring Street are two minutes away, which makes it an easy meeting point for a group coming from all over Manhattan.

Oliver's Astoria, on Broadway at 38th Street, is a neighborhood bar whose weekday afternoon happy hour leans into bar food: jumbo chicken wings, dilly chips, buffalo chicken empanadas, mozzarella sticks and truffle fries, plus signature cocktails with the option to add a house shot. It is a relaxed pick for a casual Queens Friendsgiving before everyone scatters for the holiday. Steinway Street on the M and R is three minutes away.

The Factory 380 on Third Avenue in Kips Bay runs happy hour Monday through Friday and again on Sunday, with frozen cocktails, signature cocktails, select wines, drafts and bottles. The snack list works for a group: buffalo chicken dip, mozzarella sticks and a martini with truffle parm fries. The Sunday window makes it a good fit for a slow Friendsgiving on November 29. The 6 at 28th Street is a four-minute walk.

Mudville sits on Chambers Street, a minute from the Chambers Street station on the 2, 3, A, C, E, R and W. Its weekday afternoon happy hour takes money off the Share and Mingle plates along with draft beers, select wines, well drinks and specialty cocktails. That makes it the downtown choice for an after-work Friendsgiving early in Thanksgiving week, before people leave town for the holiday.

Siren on Fifth Avenue in Park Slope is a seafood restaurant with a raw bar happy hour: East Coast oysters and littleneck clams, plus a hibiscus margarita, a Bee's Knees and a South Slope gimlet. It runs Tuesday through Sunday, with an earlier window from Friday to Sunday, and the shellfish deal is for the bar and lounge only, so send a couple of people ahead. The R at 25th Street is five minutes away.

Juniper on West 35th Street lists a happy hour every day of the week, starting earlier on Friday, which helps if your group is meeting after Black Friday shopping or arriving through Penn Station, two minutes away on foot. The list covers a classic margarita, The Ivy Martini, peach mango sangria, house wines, 212 Lager and Harpoon IPA, plus High Noon and Sun Cruiser cans.

sections.body: Thanksgiving 2026 falls on Thursday, November 26, so most Friendsgivings land on one of two stretches: Monday to Wednesday before the holiday, or Friday to Sunday after it. Early in the week is the easier booking. All eight picks run a weekday happy hour, and every one of them except Siren is on from Monday. Wednesday is also Thanksgiving Eve, a big night out in its own right, so if you want the party version of that night, read our Thanksgiving Eve NYC 2026 plan and the Thanksgiving Eve parties list. Thursday itself is a gamble: holiday hours can differ from the regular schedules on our cards, so call first. For the weekend after: of the 223 bookable places on our list, 60 post a happy hour on a Friday, Saturday or Sunday. Among the picks, Boqueria, Siren and Juniper run on both Saturday and Sunday, and The Factory 380 adds Sunday. For more options, the weekend happy hours page is sorted by what is running.

sections.h: How to book for a group
sections.body:
Book early and for the real headcount. Most of our picks take reservations through Resy or OpenTable, and Meraki uses SevenRooms. For anything past about eight people, call or use the venue's events form, because online booking tools often stop at smaller party sizes.

Ask one question when you book: does the happy hour apply at a reserved table? Some deals are for the bar area only. Siren's raw bar deal, for example, is limited to the bar and lounge. If the answer is bar only, have the first arrivals grab seats at the bar for a round of happy hour drinks and plates, then move to the table when everyone is there. Book inside the window, not at its end, and order the shareable plates first while the deal is on.

sections.h: Splitting the bill without the drama
sections.body: Decide how you will pay before anyone orders. The simplest plan for a big table is one card for the whole check and a payment app to settle up afterward, with the host splitting it evenly. If you want separate checks, ask when you book, not when the bill arrives, because some places will not split a large table at the end of the night. Read the menu or ask about service charges for large parties, since some restaurants add one automatically and you do not want to tip twice. On the tip itself, our guide to how much to tip at a bar in NYC covers what locals leave, so one person can do the math for the whole table.

If the group wants to keep going after dinner, our calendar lists 81 published parties between Friday, November 20 and Sunday, November 29, all 21 and up, and five of them carry a Thanksgiving theme. Thanksgiving night itself has one: Groundcontrol Presents: Thanksgiving with KOFLA and Cristian Arango at Superior Ingredients in Williamsburg. The weekend after has 28 parties. On Friday, November 27, NOSTALGIA: A Throwback Classic Night runs at Deluxx Fluxx in the East Village. On Saturday, November 28, Curiouser and Curiouser with Felix Da Housecat takes over House of Yes in Bushwick, and Suave Saturdays, a Latin-inspired sunset party, starts early at Somewhere Nowhere in Chelsea, a short ride from Boqueria. On Sunday, November 29, The Atrium with Eli Escobar and Jen Cardini starts in the afternoon at Public Records in Gowanus, not far from Siren. The full list is on our NYC parties page.

faq.a: There is no fixed date: most groups hold Friendsgiving in the days around Thanksgiving, which is Thursday, November 26, 2026. The Monday to Wednesday before it and the weekend of November 28 and 29 are the easiest times to book a table, since many people spend Thursday with family.
faq.q: When is Friendsgiving in 2026?

faq.a: Yes, many do: 223 bars and restaurants on our list take bookings online through services such as Resy, OpenTable and SevenRooms. For groups of more than about eight, call the venue or use its events form, since online tools often cap party size.
faq.q: Do NYC bars take reservations for big groups?

faq.a: Sometimes, so ask when you book. Some happy hours are for the bar area only, such as Siren's raw bar deal in Park Slope, which is limited to the bar and lounge. Others, like Pera SoHo's, are listed without a bar-only rule on the venue's own page.
faq.q: Does happy hour apply to a reserved table?

faq.a: Put the whole check on one card and settle up afterward with a payment app. If you need separate checks, request them when you book rather than at the end of the night, and look for an automatic service charge before you add a tip.
faq.q: What is the easiest way to split a Friendsgiving bill?

faq.a: Boqueria Spanish Tapas in Chelsea, Siren in Park Slope and Juniper in Koreatown run happy hour on both Saturday and Sunday, and The Factory 380 in Kips Bay runs on Sunday. Our weekend happy hours page lists the rest.
faq.q: Which of these picks have a happy hour on the weekend after Thanksgiving?

table_title: Every bookable happy hour in NYC
method: We worked from the 702 bars and restaurants on our list, kept the 223 that take online reservations, and chose eight with a posted happy hour that covers food or drinks a group can share, in eight different neighborhoods. Each deal and schedule comes from the venue's own website, checked between October 16 and October 24, 2026. Party listings come from our published NYC parties for November 20 to 29, 2026. The Thanksgiving date comes from the U.S. Office of Personnel Management's federal holidays list; the page could not be fetched directly, so we confirmed it through a search restricted to opm.gov that showed the page's own text.

title: Christmas Bars NYC 2026: Pop-Ups Confirmed So Far
h1: Christmas Bars NYC 2026: What Is Confirmed and Where to Drink Nearby
description: Christmas bars NYC 2026: which holiday pop-ups are confirmed on official pages, which are not announced yet, and happy hours a short walk from each.
answer: As of October 25, the Christmas bars NYC 2026 lineup confirmed on official pages is short: Miracle lists Miracle on 9th Street at The Cabinet in the East Village plus Miracle at Someday and Miracle at Vacations in Brooklyn, and Bryant Park's Winter Village, with The Lodge bar, opens October 28. Miracle has not posted exact 2026 dates, and Sippin' Santa has not announced a 2026 New York location. For a confirmed happy hour nearby, try Lovers of Today, Sea Wolf, Grand Army or Lolita.
intro:
Every November a few New York bars swap their usual look for tinsel, themed cocktails and Christmas music and run as holiday pop-ups through the season. The trouble with planning a 2026 visit in late October is that most of what turns up online is last year's coverage, with last year's dates. This guide sticks to what each pop-up or host bar has posted on its own official pages for the 2026 season, as of October 25, and says plainly where the 2026 details are not out yet.

For each confirmed spot we added bars from our own list with a happy hour a short walk away, with an eye on Saturday and Sunday windows, since weekends are when most people have time for a pop-up. Prices and times are live on each card, and the table below lists weekend happy hours across the city.

picks.why: Lovers of Today is a cocktail bar on East 7th Street, about a five-minute walk from The Cabinet, home of Miracle on 9th Street. Its happy hour on signature drinks runs every day, Saturday and Sunday included, in the early evening, and there is a second late-night window early in the week. That makes it a dependable place to wait if Miracle is full. The L at 1st Avenue is seven minutes away.

Romeo's on St. Marks Place is about six minutes on foot from The Cabinet. It posts a weekday happy hour from late afternoon and a longer weekend one on Saturday and Sunday that starts in the early afternoon, which suits a daytime plan: happy hour first, then the walk east toward Avenue C and Miracle on 9th Street. Check the card for the current deal. The L at 1st Avenue is a seven-minute walk.

Vacations Bar & Rooftop on Cypress Avenue in Bushwick is one of the two Brooklyn hosts on Miracle's official 2026 locations page, listed as Miracle at Vacations. Its own happy hour takes money off everything Tuesday through Friday in the early evening. During the Miracle run, ask whether that deal also covers the holiday cocktail list. Jefferson Street on the L is a four-minute walk.

Sea Wolf, a restaurant on Wyckoff Avenue, is about a four-minute walk from Vacations and a minute from the Jefferson Street L station. Its happy hour runs every day of the week, weekends included, with beers, house wine and frozen drinks, and its own page also lists oysters and wings. Use it as the first stop before Miracle at Vacations, especially on a Saturday or Sunday when Vacations has no happy hour.

Grand Army on State Street is about two minutes from Someday Bar on Atlantic Avenue, the other Brooklyn host on Miracle's 2026 list. Its happy hour runs every day: early evening Monday to Thursday, a little earlier on Friday, and in the afternoon on Saturday and Sunday, so a weekend visit can start with a deal and end at Miracle. Hoyt-Schermerhorn on the A, C and G is two minutes away.

Lolita on West 45th Street is a few blocks north of Bryant Park and its Winter Village. It runs happy hour every day of the week, in the afternoon and again late at night, with cocktails such as a Lolita Margarita, Paloma, Daiquiri and Mezcal Negroni, plus house wines, cervezas and bites. From Friday to Sunday it adds a tacos and guacamole deal. The B, D, F and M at Rockefeller Center are three minutes away.

Follia is a restaurant on Third Avenue, about five blocks south of Rolf's, the German restaurant that keeps its Christmas decorations up all year. Follia's happy hour runs Sunday through Friday in the late afternoon, with draft beer, select wines, spritzes and a Sbagliato, and its own page says the bar keeps the deal going a little longer from Sunday to Thursday. The L at Third Avenue is four minutes away.

sections.body:
Miracle, the Christmas cocktail pop-up that began in the East Village in 2014, lists three New York locations on its official 2026 locations page. Miracle on 9th Street is the Manhattan one, hosted by The Cabinet, a mezcal bar at 649 East 9th Street according to The Cabinet's own site. In Brooklyn, Miracle at Someday is at Someday Bar, 364 Atlantic Avenue, and Miracle at Vacations is at Vacations Bar & Rooftop, 48 Cypress Avenue in Bushwick.

The calendar is not confirmed yet. Miracle on 9th Street's own Instagram says it is closed for the season and will be back in November 2026, but none of the official pages we checked post an opening or closing date for any of the three New York locations. Miracle's site says reservations are handled by each location directly, so watch the host bars' own channels.

Our list has 32 happy hours within about a 10-minute walk of The Cabinet, and 10 of them post a Saturday or Sunday window. Lovers of Today is the closest of those, with Romeo's a few minutes farther. Sea Wolf is about four minutes from Vacations, and Grand Army is two minutes from Someday.

sections.h: Confirmed for 2026: Winter Village at Bryant Park
sections.body:
Bryant Park's official site lists the Bank of America Winter Village opening on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, and running through February 28, 2027, with the free-admission rink, the holiday shops and The Lodge, a bar and food hall on the rink deck. The park also lists its Cozy Igloos, private igloos you book for a group, returning on November 5. It is not a Christmas bar in the Miracle sense, but The Lodge is the one confirmed holiday-season bar in this guide that you can walk into next week.

For a happy hour first, Lolita is about four minutes north of the park and runs its deal every day. Our list has 49 happy hours within about a 10-minute walk of Bryant Park, but only 10 of them post a Saturday or Sunday window, so a weekend visit here takes a little more planning.

Several holiday bars that New Yorkers look for every year had not posted 2026 New York details on their own pages as of October 25. Sippin' Santa, the tropical Christmas pop-up that was born at Boilermaker in New York in 2015 as a companion to Miracle, lists no 2026 New York location on its official site, which is still taking 2026 partnership inquiries. Jingle Jangle, The Dead Rabbit's holiday pop-up, still shows last season's run on its event page. Frosty's Christmas Bar's New York page says its season is over and offers a sign-up list. We are not repeating last year's dates for any of them, because they do not carry over; follow each one's official account for the 2026 news.

If you want Christmas decor before the pop-ups open, Rolf's German Restaurant at 281 Third Avenue, at 22nd Street, keeps its decorations up all year, according to its own site, which describes more than 200,000 lights and many vintage ornaments. The site also says holiday-season reservations are taken by phone. Follia, about five blocks south on Third Avenue, has a happy hour for a drink before or after.

Our weekend happy hours page shows what is running on Saturday and Sunday anywhere in the city. For dancing, our NYC parties calendar has 62 published parties between December 1 and December 24, 57 of them on Fridays and Saturdays. The holiday-themed one so far is BOOTS! 60s Holiday Dance Party at The Sultan Room in Bushwick on Friday, December 11, a short ride from Vacations and Sea Wolf.

faq.a: No exact date is posted on Miracle's official pages yet. Miracle on 9th Street's own Instagram says it returns in November 2026, and Miracle's 2026 locations page lists it at The Cabinet in the East Village, with Brooklyn locations at Someday and Vacations.
faq.q: When does Miracle open in NYC in 2026?

faq.a: Not announced. As of October 25, 2026, Sippin' Santa's official site lists no New York location for the 2026 season.
faq.q: Is Sippin' Santa in New York in 2026?

faq.a: At The Cabinet, a mezcal bar at 649 East 9th Street in the East Village. Lovers of Today on East 7th Street and Romeo's on St. Marks Place both run weekend happy hours about five to six minutes away on foot.
faq.q: Where is Miracle on 9th Street?

faq.a: Book through the host bar: Miracle's official site says reservations are handled by each location directly. Watch The Cabinet, Someday or Vacations for booking details once 2026 dates are posted.
faq.q: Do you need a reservation for Miracle?

faq.a: Wednesday, October 28, 2026, according to Bryant Park's official site, and it runs through February 28, 2027. The Lodge bar and food hall opens with it, and the Cozy Igloos return on November 5.
faq.q: When does Winter Village at Bryant Park open in 2026?

faq.a: All of the confirmed ones do. Near Miracle on 9th Street, Lovers of Today and Romeo's run on Saturday and Sunday; near Miracle at Vacations, Sea Wolf runs every day; near Miracle at Someday, Grand Army has a weekend afternoon window; and near Bryant Park, Lolita runs daily.
faq.q: Which Christmas pop-ups have a happy hour nearby on weekends?

table_title: Weekend happy hours across NYC
method: Pop-up facts come only from each pop-up's or host bar's official pages, checked October 25, 2026: Miracle's 2026 locations page and Miracle on 9th Street's Instagram, The Cabinet's and Someday Bar's own sites for addresses, Bryant Park's site for Winter Village, and the official sites of Sippin' Santa, The Dead Rabbit, Frosty's and Rolf's. Direct fetches of these sites were blocked, so we confirmed each through web searches restricted to the official domain that showed the page's own text. We did not use any past season's dates. Bar picks and counts come from our list of 702 bars, with deals from each bar's own site checked between October 19 and October 25, 2026. Walking distances are straight-line estimates from street addresses at about 80 meters a minute. Party counts come from our published NYC parties.

title: Thanksgiving Weekend NYC 2026: Parties and Happy Hours
h1: Thanksgiving Weekend NYC 2026: Where to Go Out, Wednesday to Sunday
description: Thanksgiving weekend NYC 2026, night by night: Wednesday dance parties, Thursday after dinner, Friday and Saturday club nights, and weekend happy hours.
answer: Thanksgiving weekend NYC nights run from Wednesday, November 25 to Sunday, November 29, 2026, with 40 published parties on our calendar. Wednesday has Louie Vega's Flashback at Superior Ingredients in Williamsburg and Soul In The Horn at The Chocolate Factory in Bushwick, and Thursday has Ground Control's Thanksgiving night with KOFLA and Cristian Arango. Friday brings Night & Day at Signal, Saturday has Felix Da Housecat at House of Yes, and Sunday closes with Chus & Ceballos on The Roof at Superior Ingredients.
intro:
Thanksgiving falls on Thursday, November 26 this year, and the party calendar wraps around it. Wednesday is busy, Thursday is quiet until dinner is cleared, and Saturday is the fullest night. Sunday leans toward daytime parties that end early.

This guide walks the five nights in order. Each party links to its own page with live ticket status and price. All 40 parties on the calendar for these nights are 21+, and none was sold out when we pulled the data. For happy hours we use each bar's regular weekly schedule, so check holiday hours, above all on Thursday.

picks.why: Sea Wolf sits at 19 Wyckoff Avenue, a minute from the Jefferson St L stop and on the same avenue as House of Yes. Its happy hour runs every day of the week, so Wednesday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday are all covered on the regular schedule, with beers, house wine and frozen drinks on the deal. The venue also hosts the MONSTERA reggaeton party on Friday and Saturday nights.

OTB at 141 Broadway in Williamsburg runs a weeknight happy hour plus a weekend one from midday into the afternoon, which makes it a good Saturday or Sunday warm-up before Superior Ingredients or a Sunday roof session. The deal covers margaritas, martinis, Aperol spritz, house wine, half a dozen oysters and a cheeseburger. Marcy Avenue on the J, M and Z is a 6-minute walk.

sections.h: Wednesday, November 25: the big night out
sections.body:
Nine published parties land on Wednesday, and four are billed around Thanksgiving. Our Thanksgiving Eve guide covers this night in full, so here is the short version. Louie Vega plays Flashback in the Main Room at Superior Ingredients from 9 PM, and Soul In The Horn runs at The Chocolate Factory from 10 PM to 5 AM.

DayBreak at Elsewhere in Bushwick runs from 10 PM to 3 AM with no lineup announced, and Elsewhere asks for a physical, scannable ID. In Manhattan, TMML's Thanksgiving Eve house night at PUBLIC ArtSpace on Chrystie Street starts at 10 PM with a dress code: no athletic wear, shorts or flip-flops.

If you want music without the late night, Date Nite: Vinyl Happy Hour at Sleepwalk on Bushwick Avenue runs from 6 PM to 10 PM, with crate-digging DJs and happy hour specials at the bar.

Thanksgiving night is the quietest night on the calendar. Ground Control's party with KOFLA and Cristian Arango at Superior Ingredients is the only published party for Thursday, with doors at 10 PM.

Bars are harder to call. On a normal week, 828 of the 844 bars we track list a Thursday happy hour, but holiday hours are not in our data. Check the bar's own site or call before you head out.

sections.h: Friday and Saturday, November 27 and 28: the weekend proper
sections.body:
Friday has 10 published parties and Saturday has 17, the busiest night of the five. On Friday, Night & Day at Signal runs into Saturday afternoon. At The Delancey on the Lower East Side, reggaetonLABS hosts Reggaeton Fridays from 11 PM; the listing says a ticket guarantees entry only before midnight, and the dress code is upscale casual.

Saturday spreads across three boroughs. UK garage producer MPH headlines the Main Hall at Knockdown Center in Maspeth from 10 PM to 5 AM. THE KAGE Chapter 01 at Capitale on the Bowery pairs sanctioned fights in an octagon cage with an after-hours party from 12:30 AM. For an early start, Suave Saturdays at Somewhere Nowhere NYC in Chelsea is a Latin-inspired sunset party from 5 PM to 10 PM, and only arrivals before 6 PM are guaranteed entry.

sections.h: Happy hours open over the long weekend
sections.body:
Weekend happy hours are rarer than weekday ones. Of the 844 bars on yaynyc, 311 list a Saturday happy hour and 344 list a Sunday one, and 273 cover Wednesday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday on their regular schedule. The table below has live times and prices.

A few bars pair well with the parties above. Sea Wolf on Wyckoff Avenue runs its happy hour every day and sits on the same avenue as House of Yes, so it works before Saturday's Felix Da Housecat night. OTB on Broadway in Williamsburg has a weekend happy hour from midday, a natural first stop before Sunday on The Roof. On the Lower East Side, Mila's Bistro runs oysters, cocktails and beers on its weekend window, two minutes from Delancey St-Essex St. These are regular schedules, so a quick look at the bar's site saves a wasted trip.

sections.h: Sunday, November 29 and tips for the whole weekend
sections.body:
Sunday has three published parties, and two of them are daytime. Chus & Ceballos play The Roof at Superior Ingredients from 2 PM to 10 PM. In Gowanus, Eli Escobar and Jen Cardini take The Atrium at Public Records from 4 PM to 10 PM; doors close an hour before the end, and large bags and coats must be checked.

title: Free Things to Do in NYC at Night: Fall Parties and Cheap Drinks
h1: Free Things to Do in NYC at Night This Fall: No-Cover Parties, Low-Cost Happy Hours
keyword: free things to do in nyc at night
description: Free things to do in NYC at night this fall: 21 free-entry parties in Brooklyn and Manhattan, plus happy hours with the lowest drink deals to start.
answer: For free things to do in NYC at night this fall, the yaynyc calendar lists 21 free-entry parties between October 28 and December 16, led by Date Nite: Vinyl Happy Hour at Sleepwalk in Williamsburg every Wednesday and Reggaeton Fridays and Safaera on Saturdays at The Delancey on the Lower East Side. Start with a low-cost happy hour at Phoenix Bar in the East Village or Art Bar in the West Village, both daily, or Papacito's in Greenpoint, which adds a late taco deal in the last hour of every night.
intro:
A night out in New York does not have to start with a cover charge. Our parties calendar lists 21 upcoming free-entry nights at five venues, from a Wednesday vinyl session in Williamsburg to reggaeton on the Lower East Side until 4 AM. Two free Halloween parties are already sold out, so they are not here.

We paired the parties with happy hours that list some of the lowest drink deals in our data, each checked against the bar's own site in the last two weeks. Prices show on the cards, so the text sticks to what is on the menu and which days it runs. Every party below is 21+, so bring ID.

picks.why: Papacito's is a Greenpoint bar at 999 Manhattan Avenue, three minutes from the Greenpoint Avenue G. It runs three happy hours: a weekday lunch window with tacos and cans, an early evening window every day with Tecate or Modelo cans, house margaritas, pints of sangria, a tequila-and-Tecate combo, nachos and two-for-one frozen margaritas, then a taco deal with a drink in the last hour of every night.

Phoenix Bar sits on East 13th Street, a minute from the 1st Avenue L. Its happy hour runs every afternoon into the early evening, seven days a week, with Bud and Bud Light, well drinks and red or white wine. On Mondays the deal lasts all day for Blue Monday, a night of new wave, synth and moody pop.

Art Bar is on Eighth Avenue in the West Village, three minutes from the 14 St stop for the A, C, E and L. The list is simple: draft beer, well drinks, house wine and sparkling wine, every day from late afternoon into early evening. Weekends count too, so it suits an early Saturday or Sunday start.

Juke Bar is at 400 Troutman Street in Bushwick, a minute from the Jefferson Street L. Its happy hour runs Monday to Friday from late afternoon to early evening, with beer, house liquor, wine and cocktails on the list. Use it as the first stop on a Bushwick Thursday before Nightbreed at Purgatory or Techno Thursday at SILO.

The Little Whiskey is a pub at 36 Wilson Avenue in Bushwick, about six minutes on foot from the Morgan Avenue L. Happy hour covers PBR tall boys, Miller High Life, wine and well drinks. It runs all day on Mondays, and Tuesday to Friday it lasts into the evening, a bit later than most picks here.

169 Bar is on East Broadway on the Lower East Side, a minute from the East Broadway F. Its happy hour is a weekend deal, Saturday and Sunday from the afternoon into early evening, with money off liquor drinks and beer, plus a well shot paired with any beer. It is a sensible warm-up for Safaera at The Delancey.

Isla & Co. is at 139 Orchard Street, three minutes from the Delancey Street station on the F, J, M and Z. Happy hour runs every day from late afternoon, with select beers, wines and cocktails. Mondays are oyster night, when the happy hour lasts all day. On weekends it works as an early round before The Delancey.

sections.h: Free parties on the calendar this fall
sections.body:
Wednesdays are the steadiest free night. Date Nite: Vinyl Happy Hour, presented by Hotel Kismet, runs at Sleepwalk, 251 Bushwick Avenue, from 6 PM to 10 PM every week from October 28 through December 16. Collectors play vintage and global grooves on vinyl, with happy hour specials at the bar. See /parties/date-nite-vinyl-happy-hour-2026-10-28 and /parties/date-nite-vinyl-happy-hour-2026-11-04.

Fridays and Saturdays belong to reggaetonLABS at The Delancey, 168 Delancey Street. Reggaeton Fridays (/parties/reggaeton-fridays-2026-11-06) and Safaera (/parties/safaera-2026-11-07), a reggaeton and Latin night, run from 11 PM to 4 AM every weekend from November 6 to December 5. The dress code is upscale casual.

Thursdays bring one-offs. Nightbreed fills the downstairs room at Purgatory in Bushwick on October 29 from 8 PM to midnight with synth, post punk, goth and 80s, and costumes are encouraged (/parties/downstairs-nightbreed-2026-10-29). On November 5, Nervous Records sets up a speakeasy pop-up at Shinsen, 44 Bowery, from 9 PM to 1 AM with Cosmo and Mike Nervous (/parties/nervous-records-speakeasy-w-cosmo-and-mike-nervous-2026-11-05). On November 19, Techno Thursday takes SILO Brooklyn's main room from melodic techno into hard techno, led by Roman Messer and Bruce Wayne (/parties/techno-thursday-melodic2hard-main-room-event-free-w-rsvp-2026-11-19).

sections.h: Read the fine print on free entry
sections.body:
At The Delancey, a DICE ticket guarantees entry before midnight. The organizer says the party does not charge cover, but after midnight there is a two-drink minimum to get in, so arrive early if you want to spend nothing at the door. Bring a government-issued ID with your date of birth.

The Thursday one-offs run on RSVPs. Nervous Records at Shinsen is entry by RSVP on DICE, and the listing advises arriving early without confirming that an RSVP guarantees entry. Techno Thursday at SILO has a limited number of free RSVP tickets, the listing says tickets are also sold at the door, and the promoter advises arriving early. Date Nite and Nightbreed list no RSVP rule.

For the Wednesday vinyl night, Post No Bills sits at 253 Bushwick Avenue, a few doors from Sleepwalk, with drafts and well drinks on a daily happy hour. Its menu reads messily in our data, so it is not a pick, but the address makes it an easy first round. Juke Bar and The Little Whiskey cover the Bushwick Thursdays.

For The Delancey, mind the gap: both Lower East Side picks end their happy hours in the early evening, and the parties start at 11 PM. Isla & Co. works any day, and 169 Bar only on weekends, which suits Safaera. Plan dinner in between. If you just want a cheap drink with no party, Phoenix Bar and Art Bar run their happy hours seven days a week, and the table below shows the lowest drink deal in each neighborhood.

sections.h: A free night out, day by day
sections.body: Monday has no free parties listed, so make it a happy hour night: Phoenix Bar, The Little Whiskey and Isla & Co. run their deals all day. Wednesday is Date Nite at Sleepwalk; the November 25 edition falls on Thanksgiving Eve. Thursday depends on the date: Nightbreed on October 29, Nervous Records on November 5, Techno Thursday on November 19. Friday and Saturday are The Delancey, arriving before midnight, with 169 Bar on Saturday afternoon. On Sunday, Art Bar, Phoenix Bar and Papacito's still run their happy hours.

faq.a: Yes. The yaynyc calendar lists 21 free-entry parties between October 28 and December 16, 2026, at Sleepwalk, Purgatory, SILO Brooklyn, Shinsen and The Delancey. The Sleepwalk Wednesdays and The Delancey weekends repeat every week.
faq.q: Are there free parties in NYC this fall?

faq.a: Sometimes. Nervous Records at Shinsen and Techno Thursday at SILO are entry by RSVP on DICE, and both listings say to arrive early. At The Delancey, a DICE ticket guarantees entry before midnight.
faq.q: Do I need an RSVP for free parties in NYC?

faq.a: Not quite. The organizer says Reggaeton Fridays and Safaera do not charge cover, but after midnight there is a two-drink minimum to get in.
faq.q: Is The Delancey free all night?

faq.a: Yes, every free party in this guide is 21+. The Delancey asks for a government-issued ID showing your date of birth, and SILO accepts a government-issued photo ID or a passport.

faq.a: Papacito's in Greenpoint is the latest of our picks, with a taco deal with a drink in the last hour of every night. Most cheap happy hours end in the early evening; 20 of the 844 bars in our data are tagged for late-night happy hours.
